papers.title: Degeneracy graph determinants and higher-dimensional Young diagrams
papers.summary: Kemp and Ramgoolam proposed a basis of monomials for a commutative semisimple algebra with generators \(C_1,\ldots, C_L\), constructed from a degeneracy graph which records how the eigenspaces of \( C_1\) are successively split by \( C_2,\ldots, C_L\). They showed that the basis property is equivalent to the non-vanishing of the determinant of the matrix of values of these monomials on the projector basis, and conjectured a factorised formula for this determinant, as a product of powers of eigenvalue differences. We prove this formula for any number of generators. The proof uses graph analogues of Newton polynomials. Their evaluation matrix is not triangular in general, but expanding the rows of the children of each node of the penultimate layer in a Newton basis of their eigenvalues makes it block triangular, with diagonal blocks given by smaller degeneracy graphs in which the final layer is removed. The formula then follows by induction on the number of layers. We show that the exponents in the determinant are overlap volumes of higher-dimensional Young diagrams attached to the nodes of the graph: intervals, ordinary Young diagrams, plane partitions and their higher analogues. Finally, the block triangular structure gives an explicit recursive inversion of the evaluation matrix, expressing the projectors in the monomial basis.

papers.title: Giant Wilson loops from Fredholm determinants
papers.summary: We study large-k symmetric and antisymmetric Wilson loops in N=4 super-Yang-Mills theory. We represent their generating functions as Fredholm determinants built from the Hermite kernel weighted by a symbol function that encodes the representation. Using the integrable structure of the kernel, we systematically apply the Tracy-Widom approach to derive a closed system of integro-differential equations. The equations are then solved order by order in 1/N by a WKB ansatz, while keeping the symbol function general. We find a closed-form expression for the leading and subleading order contributions to the generating functions. Finally, specializing to the two representations, we perform the large-k saddle-point analysis and find the subleading contribution to the Wilson loop. Our results confirm the previously observed discrepancies with the dual D-brane description of giant Wilson loops.

papers.title: Thermal AdS two-point functions and loop induced effective one-point vertices
papers.summary: We present a study of thermal two-point functions from Witten diagrams in thermal AdS$_{d+1}$, defined with the conformal boundary $S_\beta^1 \times \mathbb{R}^{d-1}$, with an aim to establish a connection between thermal CFT data and perturbative bulk dynamics. We analyze one-loop tadpole and bench diagrams arising from the cubic $\phi\phi\chi$ interaction in the bulk, segregating the different relative thermal winding sectors for the bench, and also extend the analysis to include quartic scalar contact diagrams with and without derivative interactions. We also analyze the spinning exchange thermal two-point function. Utilizing the split representation of bulk propagators and the method of images we reorganize the thermal Witten diagrams into the standard AdS integrals and obtain spectral and image-sum representations that make KMS periodicity of the correlators manifest. Additionally, we show possible position dependent effective one-point vertices of scalar and spinning fields in the bulk arising from the reduction of the coincident- point thermal bulk to bulk propagator loop, allowing tadpole-type diagrams to be reconstructed from effective local bulk interactions. The bench diagram however retains an intrinsically bi-local structure. We further investigate the thermal one-point coefficients and perturbative OPE data encoded in these thermal correlators, including contributions associated with anomalous dimensions. Finally, we examine their relation to thermal dispersion relations and the role of contributions that are not determined by discontinuity data alone. Our results provide a set of explicit bulk constructions for exploring the analytic structure of thermal CFT correlators and their connection to the thermal conformal bootstrap.

papers.title: Post-Newtonian theory in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetimes
papers.summary: We develop the post-Newtonian framework for the near-zone dynamics of a binary in de Sitter and anti-de Sitter spacetime. We consider a binary interacting via a free scalar field in a fixed (A)dS background in $D+1$ spacetime dimensions, with $D\ge3$ and odd. Using multipole expansion and re-summation techniques, we solve for the field degrees of freedom to obtain an effective particle description in the form of a Fokker action. We derive the equations of motion for the binary up to second post-Newtonian (2PN) order and obtain the corresponding 2PN Hamiltonian and conserved charges in phase space. We show that the conformal algebra, corresponding to the isometry algebra of the (A)dS background, is realised in phase space as a curvature-dependent deformation of the Poincare algebra at each PN order. Our results provide a systematic extension of post-Newtonian effective dynamics to finite-curvature backgrounds. This could serve as a useful framework for studying bound-state dynamics in (A)dS as well as in the corresponding holographic CFT.

papers.title: Heavy-Heavy-Light-Light correlators from holography on the worldsheet
papers.summary: We study correlation functions of light local operators and defect changing operators on the conformal line set by the 1/2 BPS Wilson line of $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills. We consider the defect changing operators associated with geometrical and internal cusp angles, which at strong coupling have a large scaling dimension and back-react on the dual $AdS_2$ world-sheet. We set up a holographic computation of correlation functions, in which the light operators are described by fluctuations around the cusped classical string solution, so that correlators of two defect changing operators and an arbitrary number of light protected operators are obtained from the on-shell action of these fluctuations. We implement this prescription in detail for the case of certain 4-point functions, with two light and two defect changing operators. Finally, since for small cusp angles the defect changing operators become light, we manage to derive relations satisfied by integrated correlators of light operators, valid at any coupling. We verify these relations at strong coupling for both internal and geometrical cusps.

papers.title: Hamiltonian surface charges in General Parallel Relativity
papers.summary: General Parallel Relativity is a dynamically equivalent formulation of Einstein gravity in which the parallel frame supplies explicit boundary reference data. In this formulation, finite-region energy-momentum and horizon entropy arise as distinct Hamiltonian surface charges. Diffeomorphisms along canonical frame directions define a quasi-local energy-momentum including a matter surface term, while normal-plane boosts at a smooth horizon give entropy. These covariant formulas are applied to the Reissner-Nordstr\"om black hole and to a dilatonic charged black hole. In both examples, the matter contribution and its Legendre transform complete the Misner-Sharp mass into the Hamiltonian energy appropriate to the chosen electromagnetic boundary datum. The resulting horizon charges satisfy the thermodynamic relation obtained independently from the Euclidean boundary action.

papers.title: Index for a mutation loop
papers.summary: Motivated by the 3d-3d correspondence, we introduce an index $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi$ for a mutation loop $\phi$ of a quiver and an integer $g \geq 0$. We prove its integrality $\mathcal{I}_g^\phi \in \mathbb{Z}$ under certain conditions, which extends the integrality conjecture of Gang--Kim--Yoon for $3$-manifolds to the broader framework of mutation loops in cluster algebras. Our index also has an interpretation as the genus-$g$ partition function of a $(1+1)$-dimensional TQFT. We provide explicit computations for mutation loops of period one. In particular, in the case of the generalized Kronecker quivers, we give an explicit formula expressing the generating function of the indices for all genera $g$ as a ratio of polynomials. Altogether, we provide a new insight to the interplay between the geometry of $3$-manifolds and cluster algebra.

papers.title: Invertible subalgebras for chiral semion topological order
papers.summary: Chiral topological order is incompatible with strictly two-dimensional local commuting-projector Hamiltonians on finite-dimensional tensor-product Hilbert spaces. Invertible subalgebras (ISAs) provide an alternative framework. We construct an ISA supporting chiral semions, together with its anti-semion commutant, on a square lattice with one qubit per edge. We give explicit non-Pauli generators for both algebras and prove that together they generate all local operators on the Hilbert space. Starting from the $\mathbb{Z}_4$ toric code, we condense the boson $e^2m^2$ and identify the semion and anti-semion algebras. We then decompose each $\mathbb{Z}_4$ qudit into two qubits and use a finite-depth circuit to disentangle one qubit per edge fixed by the condensation constraints. Pumping the semion ISA along the $z$ direction defines an explicit three-dimensional non-Clifford quantum cellular automaton (QCA). We show that pumping eight times is equivalent to a translation followed by a finite-depth quantum circuit with ancillary qubits. We also give an explicit finite-depth circuit relating this construction to the semion QCA previously obtained from topological quantum field theory. A similar condensation construction yields a $U(1)_4$ ISA on a square lattice. Together with the semion and earlier odd-prime ISAs, finite stacking realizes every pointed Witt class of bosonic Abelian anyon theories. Finally, we extend both constructions to all spatial dimensions $d=4k{-}2$, with one qubit or $\mathbb{Z}_4$ qudit on each $(2k{-}1)$-cell for the semion or $U(1)_4$ ISA, respectively.

papers.title: Stabilizer R\'enyi Entropy Without a Phase Reference
papers.summary: Stabilizer R\'enyi entropy quantifies magic relative to a complete Pauli frame. In settings such as helicity states of massless particles, unsynchronized qubit registers, energy eigenbases, and systems under superselection rules, the computational basis may be fixed while the transverse Pauli axes remain unspecified. The stabilizer R\'enyi entropy then depends on the choice of those axes. We define a phase-averaged stabilizer R\'enyi entropy by averaging the Pauli moments before taking the logarithm. It is exactly invariant under independent local rephasings. For pure states, it vanishes precisely when the state is a stabilizer state in every phase convention. For a broad class of sparse supports, it reduces to a closed-form function of the basis-state probabilities alone. Within this class, the ceiling for $n$ channels is $\ln[n^{3}/(6n-5)]$ for $n\geq3$ and $\ln\frac{7}{5}$ for two channels. We apply the invariant to tree-level gluon scattering at four and five points, where the helicity-basis phases are unspecified. It saturates the two- and three-channel ceilings: $\ln\frac{7}{5}$ at four points and $\ln\frac{27}{13}$ in $3\to2$ scattering. In same-helicity $2\to3$ scattering, it lies between a floor of $\ln\frac{8}{7}$ and a ceiling of $\ln\frac{184}{125}$, reached in the resolved soft limit and particular collinear limits, respectively. In every configuration studied, the invariant is independent of the fixed external colors.

papers.title: Thin shells in Lovelock and Quasi-topological gravities
papers.summary: We derive the junction conditions for spherically symmetric thin shells in Lovelock and Quasi-topological gravities along two independent routes: from the distributional form of the field equations, and from the boundary term that makes the variational problem well-posed in the non-null case. The former method is ambiguous as it stands, since the equations contain products of Heaviside step functions with a Dirac delta. We show that the singular parts of the field equations are exact differentials in the jumping variables, so that the Vol'pert chain rule for functions of bounded variation fixes these singular combinations uniquely and no products of two deltas survive for a single shell, finding that both routes then agree. The same rule yields the null junction conditions, for which no boundary term is available in Quasi-topological gravities, together with the mass conservation law of the shell. These results clarify recent questions concerning the existence of thin shells in these theories. In particular, we show that previous claims that the junction conditions force the shell mass to vary with radius are incorrect and arise from treating a trapezoidal approximation to the relevant distributional products as exact. Our results also provide a basis for the recent analyses of mass inflation in these theories.

papers.title: The Forgetful Black Hole: Memory Burden and Hysteresis in Hawking Evaporation
papers.summary: The memory-burden scenario of black hole evaporation proposes that Hawking emission may become increasingly suppressed as maintaining stored quantum information becomes dynamically costly. In this work, we revisit this scenario and investigate the conditions under which information retention can produce a genuine dynamical burden. We derive general scaling conditions for incremental memory accumulation at a fixed fractional mass loss and establish a conditional no-go result: entropy-suppressed, zero-mean deposits with subextensive integrated correlations cannot produce an order-one luminosity modification through unamplified accumulation and bounded feedback. We identify three essential requirements for dynamical memory: a record of the past must be written, retained, and coupled back to subsequent evaporation. We illustrate these requirements with concrete toy models that exhibit either a prolonged but finite black hole lifetime or an asymptotically approached finite-mass state (an effective remnant). We further distinguish kinetic-memory, thermodynamic-memory, and spectral-memory sub-categories of possible memory-burden mechanisms. In particular, we demonstrate that an independently evolving memory variable can generate evaporation-accretion hysteresis, such that a black hole returning to the same mass may possess a different retained memory and consequently a different luminosity. This history dependence may have implications for primordial black hole phenomenology. Finally, we briefly discuss the possibility of "merger rejuvenation", in which black hole mergers reorganize or reset the effective memory state.

papers.title: Anomalies, higher symmetries, and homotopy theory I: crossed precosheaves and a nonabelian Cech construction
papers.summary: Symmetries of a quantum field theory or a quantum lattice model are expected to be described not by a group but by a homotopy type, whose homotopy groups are the higher symmetry groups and whose Postnikov invariants encode 't Hooft anomalies. We propose a homotopy-theoretic definition of 't Hooft anomalies based on the structure of localized symmetries in the operator-algebraic approach. The input is a crossed precosheaf: a collection of groups attached to regions of space, equipped with pairings recording that the commutator of two transformations localized in two regions is localized in their intersection. To a crossed precosheaf and a finite family of regions we attach a pointed connected homotopy type, the Cech-Loday classifying space. As the family of regions ranges over finite covers of space, the classifying spaces form a pro-object in the homotopy category. There is a canonical map from the ordinary classifying space of the symmetry group to this pro-type. Composing this map with a group action gives an anomaly whose nontriviality obstructs gauging. In favorable cases, the Cech-Loday space is essentially independent of the cover. In such cases, the homotopy fiber of the canonical map is a candidate for the classifying space of the higher group of symmetries. We give examples of crossed precosheaves arising from gauge transformations in continuum field theory and from quantum cellular automata and finite-depth circuits. For quantum spin systems in one and two dimensions, our construction recovers the Else-Nayak index and its generalizations to two dimensions.

papers.title: Gravity from generalized entropy
papers.summary: Gravity from entropy (GfE) identifies its Lagrangian with the geometric quantum relative entropy (GQRE) between the spacetime metric and a metric induced by matter and curvature, treating the metric itself as a quantum operator. We extend this construction to the Tsallis, R\'enyi, and Sharma-Mittal families, which we call gravity from generalized entropy (GfGE), and determine their common Einstein limit, weak-field spectra, auxiliary-field formulation, and horizon entropy. The entropy choice controls the leading higher-curvature terms and additional modes. We confirm that the linearized GfE spectrum contains a healthy scalar and a Planck-scale tachyonic spin-2 ghost. We identify the conditions that remove this ghost: curvature must enter through its scalar trace, or the entropy generator must be flat to quadratic order at the identity. The latter gives exact general relativity for Tsallis at $q=0$ and ghost-free $f(R,L_m)$ theories for R\'enyi and Sharma-Mittal. On shell, the auxiliary G-field is proportional to the tensor in Wald's entropy formula. For analytic entropy functions, horizons with a single curvature scale have an area term followed by constant and inverse-area corrections. We also extend the volume-constraint cosmological constant to the full family; its leading entropy dependence is set by the scalar mass. A finite set of entropy-function derivatives controls the leading weak-curvature departures from general relativity.

papers.title: Effective Fermion-Photon Vertex in a Rotating Relativistic Medium: Tree-Level Structure
papers.summary: We study the tree-level fermion-photon effective vertex for on-shell particles in a relativistic environment undergoing rigid rotation at zero temperature. The rotational background breaks translational invariance in the transverse plane and introduces a preferred direction, leading to a distinct decomposition of the vertex into longitudinal and transverse structures with respect to the rotation axis. Using fermion and photon modes constructed in the rotating frame, we derive the corresponding selection rules and show that the energy and the longitudinal component of the momentum are conserved, whereas no independent transverse momentum-conservation condition arises. Instead, the transverse dependence is governed by radial integrals involving three Bessel functions, whose support constrains the magnitudes of the transverse momentum projections. The vertex can be organized in a circular basis for the transverse components and a Cartesian basis along the rotation axis, and expressed in terms of six Dirac structures. Their coefficients define 24 form-factor components associated with the photon-mode components, physical photon states, and spin-dependent structures induced by the rotating background. We also verify current conservation and gauge invariance of the resulting tree-level matrix element under the boundary conditions considered. These results provide the tree-level structure of the fermion-photon interaction in rotating relativistic matter and establish the basis for the study of radiative corrections in vortical backgrounds.

papers.title: Magnetically Charged Black Holes from Grand Unified Theory
papers.summary: Grand Unified models of particle physics inevitably give rise to magnetic monopoles. Often the model will also contain a weakly broken discrete symmetry that leads to the formation of biased domain walls that survive for a limited period in cosmology. For a range of the discrete symmetry breaking parameter, domain walls can collapse to form magnetically charged extremal black holes lighter than $\simeq 1\, {\rm kg}$ but these are not expected to survive until the present epoch due to Hawking evaporation and Schwinger pair production of monopoles. If the parameter is smaller still, the black holes may be astrophysical, with mass greater than $10^{15}\, {\rm g}$ and with sub-extremal magnetic charge: $Q \simeq 10^8$ (for our canonical choice of parameters). The cosmological energy density in residual magnetic monopoles depends on the discrete symmetry breaking parameter and for sufficiently small values of the parameter, the magnetic monopole density can satisfy all observational constraints.

papers.title: A quantum probabilistic approach to the emergence of an inflationary Starobinsky Universe
papers.summary: We propose that the necessary conditions for the existence of inflation could be explained by a quantum probabilistic approach. We interpret physical states $\psi$ obtained via the path integral formulation as probability density amplitudes for the Universe to be measured at a particular geometric configuration. First, we examine the problem of ordering ambiguities in the Wheeler-DeWitt (WDW) equation. We develop a formalism to handle ambiguities in the canonical quantization of a $1d$ minisuperspace by defining ambiguity functions within the WDW equation. We define a Hilbert space inner product for calculating physical observables, and using an argument from the hermiticity of the Hamiltonian, we obtain an expression for its measure $\mu$ in addition to constraints on the ambiguity functions. By defining a new quantum state $\Psi =\sqrt{\mu} \psi$ and using the path integral formalism, we are able to resolve ambiguities and prove the theory is universal. We then generalize for any $M$-dimensional minisuperspace system, for which we can prove universality in the semi-classical approximation for a large class of models. We also show that this universality extends to all orders of quantum theory if the target space manifold of the theory is flat. We calculate probability amplitudes for various cosmological scenarios involving Starobinsky inflation. We summarize the Hartle-Hawking no-boundary proposal for GR and we comment on the distinct possibilities of defining a contour of integration: the sign choice of Hartle-Hawking vs that of Linde-Vilenkin. We make an analogous calculation for $R^{2}$ gravity and find that for the Linde- Vilenkin choice it is statistically more likely for the Universe to emerge in its inflationary stage. Finally, we calculate transition amplitudes when the kinetic energy of the inflaton field $\phi$ takes non-zero values.

papers.title: Tidal deformability of white dwarfs in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld gravity
papers.summary: We compute the static quadrupole Love number $k_2$ and the dimensionless tidal deformability $\Lambda$ of cold white dwarfs in Eddington-inspired Born-Infeld (EiBI) gravity. Matter couples to the physical metric while perturbation equations are solved in an auxiliary metric, so the physical tidal field near the surface depends on derivatives of the equation of state. This dependence is regular for a surface polytropic index $1<\Gamma_{\rm env}<3/2$, but not for the $\Gamma = 5/3$ Chandrasekhar equation of state. The mechanism, an algebraic map between the metric that carries perturbations and the metric that matter feels, is common to Palatini-type theories, so the same type of surface condition should apply to tidal calculations in this wider class. We use thermodynamically consistent envelopes that exactly reach zero enthalpy. At five masses from \(0.6\) to \(1.3\,\Msun\) and five sampled Born-Infeld couplings \(\kappa\), with $|\kappa|\le5\times10^6\,\mathrm{m^2}$, the EiBI-GR differences are approximately linear in $\kappa$. The largest absolute fractional shifts are \(3.89\times 10^{-5}\) in the stellar radius $R$, \(4.09\times 10^{-5}\) in $k_2$, and \(2.36\times 10^{-4}\) in $\Lambda$. Across nine envelope models, half the spread of each quantity relative to the baseline envelope is at most \(0.0186\) in $R$ and \(0.0857\) in \(k_2\), but only \(3.02\times 10^{-5}\) in \(\Lambda\) as the changes in \(k_2\) and \(R^5\) largely cancel. A high-precision calculation shows that the envelope dependence of the EiBI-GR difference in \(\Lambda\) is small. Half the spread of this difference ranges from \(1.067\times 10^{-12}\) to \(6.208\times 10^{-11}\) over the 20 nonzero mass-coupling points.

papers.title: Multi-Instantons and Exact-WKB Stokes Jumps in Multi-Well Quantum Mechanics
papers.summary: We study the relation between the exact-WKB Delabaere--Dillinger--Pham Stokes jumps and the multi-instanton expansion of a one-dimensional potential with $N$ equal-depth minima. For a single barrier this relation is the Bogomolny--Zinn-Justin cancellation between the instanton--anti-instanton ambiguity and the Borel ambiguity of perturbation theory, and we extend it to every consecutive barrier interval and to the integration contours themselves. In the dilute large-$T$ regime at fixed nonperturbative grade, we derive the quasi-zero mode integral over the instanton separations from the Euclidean path integral and reduce it to Gamma and Hankel periods. With the local Weber level function of each well and one normalization per well fixed by the local Weber connection matrix, these periods reproduce the two lateral connected exact-WKB coefficients. The two lateral contours of each instanton--anti-instanton separation differ by exactly one Hankel cycle, and this linear Picard--Lefschetz relation reproduces the Stokes jump of the connected coefficient. A numerical solution of the Schr\"odinger equation for a symmetric triple well confirms the resulting two-barrier level splitting. At higher fixed grade, the map from ordered event sequences to normalized scalar coefficient products is not one-to-one. At leading dilute order the scalar weight of a closed event sequence depends only on the numbers of barrier crossings, $\mathcal I\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs, and $\mathcal I\mathcal I$/$\bar{\mathcal I}\bar{\mathcal I}$ pairs. We construct two inequivalent grade-six triple-well event sequences with the same product of local Weber amplitudes, which embed in every potential with $N\ge3$ wells. Our results hold within the regular dilute, one-loop, local Weber approximation.

papers.title: All Quiet on the Vector Front: Scalar Growth and Perturbative Control in Horndeski--Weyl-squared Gravity
papers.summary: Higher-order curvature corrections to general relativity arise naturally in many fundamental theories and provide phenomenologically interesting low-energy effective field theories. However, higher-derivative terms can introduce ghost modes, which call the validity of such models into question. Here, we thoroughly investigate the classical linear stability of the most general second-order scalar-tensor theory, namely the Horndeski theory of gravity, augmented by a Weyl-squared term in the action. We consider shift-symmetric de Sitter and power-law FLRW backgrounds and study the evolution of linear perturbations. Vector perturbations are free of gradient and tachyonic instabilities for a positive Weyl-induced mass squared. Tensor perturbations necessarily contain a ghost; their superhorizon branches are bounded, while a frozen-background calculation identifies a separate finite-momentum stability condition. The scalar sector instead contains a growing long-wavelength branch for all expanding backgrounds we consider, which is inherited by at least one of the gauge-invariant Bardeen potentials. We show that this growth enters the Bardeen potentials through an inverse-gradient factor $a^2/k^2$: the dynamical scalar fields remain bounded on the inflationary backgrounds, the direct contribution of the growing shear to the clock-matched tidal field cancels, and the electric part of the Weyl tensor decays. We discuss the implications of our results for perturbative control and for the phenomenological viability of theories including quadratic curvature corrections.

papers.title: Correlation between gravitational wave frequencies as a signature of new black hole physics
papers.summary: We point out that for black holes (BH) of the same mass, despite of arising from two entirely different physical arguments, the peak frequency of the coarse-grained gravitational wave (GW) spectrum of gravitons $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}$ is very close to the peak frequency of the GW spectrum produced from binary BH mergers $f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}$. In particular, we find that $f_\text{peak}^\text{graviton}/f_\text{peak}^\text{merger}\approx 2.3$ independent from BH mass or population. If BHs are still evaporating, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{-1}$ with $M_i$ is the initial BH mass. If BHs evaporated in the radiation (matter) dominated era, the peak frequencies scale as $\propto M_i^{1/2}$ ($\propto M_i$) respectively after taking into account redshift effect. Any deviation from the aforementioned magical ratio would indicate new BH physics. The sweetest frequency ballpark to look for this correlation is around $10^{14}\ \rm Hz-10^{20}\ \rm Hz$ where both GW spectra are allowed to have maximum amplitude. As a demonstration of what the new physics could be, we consider a phenomenological self-similar regular BH model of Hayward featuring a single hair parameter. The observed ratio of peak frequencies can be used to directly infer the hair parameter, along with crucial properties of the novel BH solution such as Hawking temperature, horizon size, and innermost stable circular orbit. We also comment on the pros and cons of correlating frequencies among other GW sources such as formation, population fluctuation, and sudden transition of adiabatic perturbation.

papers.title: Quantization of positive Lagrangians
papers.summary: A Lagrangian submanifold in an almost Calabi-Yau manifold is called positive if the real part of the holomorphic volume form restricted to it is positive. It is called $\epsilon$-positive if the ratio of the restrictions of the imaginary and real parts of the holomorphic volume form is bounded by $\frac{1}{\epsilon}.$ An exact isotopy class of positive Lagrangian submanifolds admits a natural Riemannian metric. We prove that the Riemannian metric restricted to the subset of $\epsilon$-positive Lagrangians induces a path metric when the relative K\"ahler class of the ambient Calabi-Yau manifold lies on a line of rational slope. The proof relies on the construction of a sequence of quantization maps from a circle bundle over the space of positive Lagrangians to the dual of the space of holomorphic sections of powers of a prequantum line bundle. The rationality condition for the relative K\"ahler class allows us to reduce to the case of Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangians. Building on ideas of Tian and Nirenberg-Wells, H\"ormander estimates are used to show that functions on a Bohr-Sommerfeld Lagrangian can be approximated by holomorphic sections of a sufficiently high power of the prequantum line bundle. Consequently, the quantization maps eventually separate fibers of the circle bundle.

papers.title: Thermalization of the Primordial Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background
papers.summary: It is conventionally believed that the Stochastic Gravitational-Wave Background (SGWB) from inflation provides information about the earliest universe. However, in this Letter, we present a different picture. Our analysis starts from the observation that the inflation-predicted spectrum implies gravitons reside in high-occupation states, which significantly enhances their self-interactions and triggers rapid thermalization. We show that approximately $80\%$ of the primordial gravitons participate in this thermalization, forming a Bose--Einstein distribution and thereby erasing the primordial information. Evaluated using typical inflation parameters, this thermalized spectrum yields a present-day peak frequency of $f_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 1.4 \times 10^8 \, \mathrm{Hz}$ in the hundred-megahertz band with a peak amplitude of $\Omega_{0, \text{peak}}^{(\text{th})} \sim 3.5 \times 10^{-13}$. Due to the sharp drop-off away from the peak, the resulting spectrum lies beyond the reach of low-frequency observatories like PTAs, LISA, and LIGO, but remains uniquely accessible to high-frequency detectors such as microwave cavity resonators and dielectric haloscopes.

papers.title: Origin of the red spectral tilt in Inflation without an Inflaton
papers.summary: In Inflation without an Inflaton (IWI), a de Sitter (dS) background drives inflation, and the graviton bilinear generates scalar perturbations at second order, with no inflaton or additional fundamental scalar field. We investigate how this scenario can account for the observed scalar spectral tilt. The tensor-mode dependence of the scalar power spectrum gives the consistency relation $n_s-1=2n_T$, since it contains four tensor mode functions. The scalar spectral tilt $n_s\simeq0.9649$ at CMB scales therefore gives $n_T\simeq-0.0175$, independent of the tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$, hence different from the standard single-field slow-roll prediction $n_T=-r/8$. A full time-dependent calculation of $\phi_2$ in exact dS leads to an almost scale-invariant scalar power spectrum, with a small blue infrared residual on the order of $n_s-1\simeq+4\times10^{-4}$. In order to account for the observed red tilt, we introduce a slow drift in the Hubble rate, parametrized by $\varepsilon=-\dot H/H^2$. The tensor tilt is then given by $n_T=-2\varepsilon$, implying $n_s-1\simeq-4\varepsilon$, at leading order. The observed tilt requires $\varepsilon_\ast\simeq0.0088$, far exceeding the drift that can be sustained by the classical graviton backreaction, for which we find $|\varepsilon_{\rm self}|\lesssim10^{-11}$. Therefore, we investigate the quantum break-time of dS as the origin of the background evolution. In this picture, the scalar tilt becomes $n_s-1=-4C_qN_{sp}(H/m_{pl})^2$, where $C_q$ is an order-one depletion coefficient, and the tilt is directly connected to the particle content of dS, $N_{sp}$. The evolution of the drift itself further predicts a positive running of $\alpha_s=+\tfrac12(1-n_s)^2\simeq+6\times10^{-4}$. These results conclude the distinctive observational predictions of the IWI scenario, establishing it as a falsifiable alternative to standard inflaton-driven models.

papers.summary: We review the role of relative entropy in quantum field theories, where the local von Neumann algebras are generically of type III. As a new result, we prove that the relative entropy between a locally squeezed state and the Minkowski vacuum is finite for free fermions.

papers.title: Evolution of multihadron fragmentation functions with nonperturbative behavior
papers.summary: QCD calculations that use multihadron fragmentation functions usually involve multiple invariant mass scales simultaneously, with only one being the hard scale associated with an overall hard process. The other scales are associated with relative internal motion intrinsic to the fragmenting parton and the multihadron system. Nonperturbative contributions to this later type of dependence attract interest for their association with intrinsic partonic structures, but care is needed in disentangling the truly nonperturbative effects from perturbative behavior and relating the former to universal nonperturbative matrix elements. To this end, we show how to evolve collinear multihadron fragmentation functions in a way that accounts for the simultaneous presence of these extra scales. The general multihadron fragmentation functions evolve in the same way as ordinary single hadron fragmentation functions, with the dependence on the extra scales separated out. We use this to unify treatments of perturbative and nonperturbative effects in multihadron systems in a way that optimizes for interpretations focused on partonic structure.

papers.title: Analytical Time-Domain Waveforms for Black-Hole Scattering in the Self-Force Expansion
papers.summary: We obtain a systematic understanding of the time-domain gravitational waveform of hyperbolic black-hole scattering at first order in the self-force expansion and all orders in the post-Newtonian/post-Minkowskian (PN/PM) expansion. The continuous frequency spectrum of unbound orbits makes the inverse Fourier transform to the time domain diverge order by order; we introduce a dimensional-regularization-inspired prescription that cures this uniformly. We show that the full waveform then follows, at any PM and PN order, from a single family of integrals, generated by the Lauricella function $F_D^{(3)}$, which we calculate using strategies familiar from the study of Feynman integrals. As a proof of principle, we use this understanding to compute the quadrupolar 1SF waveform through relative 10PM-20PN, that is to order ${\cal O}(G^{10} v^{42})$, the full 1SF waveform to 10PM-10PN, as well as the asymptotic fluxes and the dissipative scattering angle at the corresponding accuracy.

papers.title: Topological recursion for spin enumeration of hypermaps
papers.summary: We establish topological recursion for the spin enumeration of hypermaps, or, in the dual language, spin dessins d'enfants. This problem has remarkable features distinguishing it from other applications of topological recursion to enumerative combinatorics. First, the spectral curve is elliptic rather than rational, as in most cases studied before. Second, it contains degenerate ramification points, and one has to apply a version of degenerate topological recursion. Finally, the meromorphic correlator differentials have "moving" poles on the antidiagonals between pairs of distinct arguments, and one has to adjust the loop equations to this kind of degeneracy as well. The computations involve concepts of different kinds, such as BKP integrability, Gaussian integrals, the x-y swap, and symplectic duality.

To simplify the problem, we compactify one additional dimension and relate the amplitude to a supersymmetric index computation. We find agreement with the expected answer even at finite values of $N$.

papers.title: A Note on Kinematic Flow and Differential Equations for Two-Site One-Loop Graph in FRW Spacetime
papers.summary: In this work, we systematically study the differential systems governing loop-level wavefunction coefficients of conformally-coupled scalar field theory within a general power-law FRW cosmology. By utilizing the twisted cohomology, hyperplane arrangements, and IBP techniques, we derive the canonical differential equations for two-site one-loop bubble and tadpole systems, revealing distinct structural differences. We present new insights into the one-loop tadpole system, uncovering that its integral family can include multiple parent functions due to distinct pairs of relative hyperplanes associated with each function, unlike the single parent function appearing in the one-loop bubble case. Moreover, we demonstrate that the tadpole correlator selectively probes only a subset of the cohomology space, despite the hyperplane arrangement suggesting a higher-dimensional structure. Another novel contribution of this work is the extension of kinematic flow framework to the loop-level scenarios for the first time. Using a graphical approach based on family trees generated by marked tubing graphs, which encode singularity structures, we efficiently construct the differential equations and uncover the hierarchical relationships among the associated master integrals. Additionally, we provide a preliminary discussion on generalization to two-site higher-loop configurations. We propose a general decomposition formula for the canonical form of a two-site diagram with arbitrary loops, breaking it into unshifted and shifted components associated with the fundamental tree-level and bubble-like structures, and establish a block-wise decomposition rule for the matrix $A$ in the corresponding differential system. These advancements provide a unified framework for two-site loop-level correlators and lay the groundwork for future study of more complex multi-site loop systems.

papers.title: Strong-field regime within effective field theory
papers.summary: Building upon the Covariant Derivative Expansion, we develop a method to compute effective actions that is able to capture non-perturbative effects induced by strong background fields. We demonstrate the method in scalar QED, by deriving the full second-derivative corrections to the scalar Heisenberg--Euler effective action. The corresponding result is interpreted as an effective field theory with three characteristic scales, two of which are large (mass and field strength) in comparison with the remaining one (derivatives of the field). As an application, we show that, at this order, the transseries structure of the Schwinger pair production rate is preserved, even if the involved coefficients are modified. Our analysis also helps clarify recent disagreements concerning the coefficients of this effective action.

papers.title: On anomaly free 4d $\mathcal{N}$=4 and 6d (2,0) conformal supergravities and UV finiteness of Poincar\'e supergravities
papers.summary: We review the structure of superconformal anomalies in 4d $\mathcal N$=4 conformal supergravity (CSG) coupled to a number N$_\rm v$ of $ \mathcal N$=4 vector multiplets and 6d (2,0) CSG coupled to N$_{_{\rm T}}$ of (2,0) tensor multiplets. Anomalies cancel if N$_\rm v$=4 and N$_{_{\rm T}}$=26 respectively. If the CSG part of the action is dropped and N$_{\rm v}$=6+ n$_{\rm v}$, the first theory is classically equivalent to the 4d $\mathcal N$=4 Poincar\'e supergravity (PSG) coupled to n$_{\rm v}$ vector multiplets, while the second one with N$_{_{\rm T}}$=5+ n$_{_{\rm T}}$ is classically equivalent to the 6d (2,0) PSG coupled to n$_{\rm T}$ tensor multiplets. We argue that these facts imply that divergences in the 4d PSG with n$_{\rm v}$ vectors should be proportional to n$_{\rm v}$+2 and similarly in the 6d PSG with n$_{_{\rm T}}$ tensors to n$_{_{\rm T}}$-21. These predictions appear to be consistent with known results of explicit scattering amplitude computations in these 4d and 6d PSG theories.

papers.title: Quantum simulation of traversable-wormhole-inspired quantum teleportation in a chaotic binary sparse SYK model
papers.summary: We report the experimental signature of holographically motivated quantum teleportation on a quantum processor, driven by the highly entangled, chaotic dynamics of a many-body system. Specifically, we implement the traversable-wormhole (TW) protocol utilizing a \textit{chaotic} binary sparse $N = 8$ Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev (SYK) model. This optimized approach dramatically reduces circuit depth for noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware while rigorously preserving the spectral chaos required for gravitational duality. Diagnosing the teleportation signal via mutual information, we find that while inherent noise in NISQ hardware precludes perfect quantitative agreement with exact numerical simulations, our experimental results provide evidence for the essential qualitative signature: a sign-dependent asymmetry. This work establishes a practical framework for holographic quantum simulations, offering a novel empirical testbed for exploring holographic quantum gravity.

papers.title: Some universalities in the partition functions of low-dimensional gravity models
papers.summary: In this work, first, we discuss the connections between various low-dimensional quantum gravity models, including 3d Chern-Simons, 2d Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT), 2d background field (BF) theory, 2d Liouville, 2d Wess-Zumino-Witten (WZW), and 1d Schwarzian, which are related through holography and dimension reduction, and discuss some universalities in their partition functions. Then, we specifically examine the JT partition function and the partition function of $\mathcal{N}=(2,2)$ on $S^2$ and $\text{AdS}_2$ and discuss their similarities and therefore examine our proposed universalities. We change the parameters in each model and based on the change in the structure of the partition functions, strengthen our conjectures. We also use eigenfunctions, spectra and the behaviors of Wheeler-DeWitt wavefunctions to generate more universalities between these low-dimensional quantum gravity models, specifically in their partition functions. Finally, we use entanglement entropy, complexity and RG flows, particularly in the context of wormholes, to find more universalities in quantum gravity models.

papers.title: $S$-duality, boundary states, and higher-form symmetries on ALE spaces
papers.summary: We study Abelian $S$-duality of Maxwell theory on $A$-type asymptotically locally Euclidean (ALE) spaces. Unlike on closed four-manifolds, the Maxwell path integral on an ALE space is not naturally a scalar partition function. Rather, it decomposes into theta-function blocks labeled by flat $U(1)$ holonomy sectors on the asymptotic lens-space boundary. We interpret these blocks as components of the Hilbert-space boundary state prepared by the ALE path integral. With this interpretation, the apparent failure of ordinary modularity is replaced by vector-valued modular covariance under the action of the modular group. We test this picture explicitly for Eguchi-Hanson space by gluing it to its orientation reversal. The resulting closed four-manifold is diffeomorphic to $S^2\times S^2$, and the natural pairing of the two ALE boundary states reproduces the standard Maxwell partition function on $S^2\times S^2$. We then refine the construction by turning on electric and magnetic $1$-form symmetry backgrounds. In their presence, the ALE theta blocks are not ordinary functions, but sections of a line bundle over the Cartan torus associated with the $A_{N-1}$ root lattice, reflecting the mixed electric-magnetic $1$-form anomaly. We also discuss gauging discrete $\mathbb Z_k$ subgroups of the $1$-form symmetries and show that the vector-valued boundary-state structure remains the natural covariant framework after gauging. In this sense, ALE spaces behave as chiral building blocks for four-dimensional Maxwell theory: individual ALE blocks carry sector-resolved boundary data, while gluing pairs these sectors to produce an ordinary closed-manifold partition function, much like the pairing of left- and right-moving conformal blocks in two-dimensional CFT.

papers.title: Universal Closed Form for Dynamical Love Numbers of Black Holes
papers.summary: Black hole static Love numbers vanish, but their dynamical counterparts do not. We present the entire scheme-independent dynamical response $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}$ of a Schwarzschild black hole in closed form, to all orders in $G$, and for every spin $s$ and multipole $\ell$. The result is $\bar{F}_{\ell,s}/4\pi R_S^{2\ell+1}=\Phi_{\ell,s}(\bar{y})-\tfrac12\eta\,\Phi_{\ell,s}'(\bar{y})$ with $\bar{y}=-\tfrac12\eta^2\tau$ and $\eta=i\omega R_S$. Here $\Phi_{\ell,s}$ is simply the leading-log solution to the renormalization group equation, but lifting the running logarithm to $\tau=\log(R_S/R)-2\sum_{k\ge2}\zeta_k\,\eta^{k-1}$ resums it to all orders. This tower of Riemann zeta values is the Newtonian phase in disguise: it originates from the long-range $1/r$ potential in the far zone, and is universal across multipole and spin. Our result exhibits a factorization pinned to three ingredients: the strength of horizon absorption, the running rate in the near zone, and the dressed logarithm in the far zone. Using shell effective field theory, we independently verify our formula for scalar, electromagnetic, and gravitational perturbations, reaching $\mathcal O(G^{15})$.

papers.title: Quantum Field Theory Of Cosmological Perturbations Induced By Ultralight Dark Matter
papers.summary: The growth of primordial perturbations during the matter-dominated era is primarily driven by dark matter. Ultralight scalar fields (ULDM) are a promising candidate for this role, conventionally modeled as operating in a classical, high-occupation regime. In this work, we develop a first-principles field-theoretic framework to investigate the impact of ULDM on linear cosmological perturbations during matter domination, explicitly retaining its quantum nature. Deriving a closed equation for the graviton field dynamics, we compute and regularize its source terms for a generic Gaussian initial state of the ULDM field within the adiabatic (WKB) approximation, employing the middle-point working assumption for non-local terms. After gauge-fixing we find that, contrary to previous claims, the classical condensate of ULDM has no influence on gravitational wave propagation. However, the time-dependent graviton effective mass induced by quantum pressure of the squeezed state can drive parametric resonance in specific primordial gravitational wave modes. We demonstrate this growth is negligible for non-relativistic ULDM at matter-radiation equality under the assumption of a power-law squeezing spectrum for masses in the range $m \sim 10^{-21}{-}10^{-24}$ eV.

papers.title: Genus-One Rigidity of Bounded Virasoro Pairings for 3D Gravity
papers.summary: We study whether varying the topological boundary of the doubled Virasoro TQFT can produce distinct torus pairings for an ensemble interpretation of 3D gravity. In the ordinary nondegenerate sector, every bounded pairing that commutes with the modular transformations is scalar, and vacuum normalization selects the diagonal pairing. The proof identifies the modular transformations with the even Weil representation and applies the Cowling--Steger lattice-restriction theorem. Under the ordinary block-diagonal vacuum--continuum ansatz, positivity and the two vacuum marginals also make a Borel-measure pairing bounded, without assuming absolute continuity; modular invariance then forces the same diagonal pairing. These two classes therefore contain no distinct torus pairings to average. A nontrivial Virasoro boundary ensemble must involve genus-one data outside these classes, additional sectors or vacuum--continuum couplings, or information invisible in the torus pairing. Elementary proofs in explicit regular sectors explain the rigidity mechanisms, and numerical calculations provide independent checks.

papers.title: Tripartite Form Universality in Holographic Entropy Inequalities
papers.summary: To elucidate the meaning of holographic entropy inequalities (beyond subadditivity) which characterize the entanglement structure of geometric states in holography, arXiv:2309.06296 proposed the "tripartite form" for these inequalities, consisting of tripartite information and conditional tripartite information terms with unit coefficients. While this provides a compact and useful packaging of the inequalities, it is not a priori guaranteed that all inequalities can be recast in this form. Here we conjecture that they can, and present substantial evidence, by proving that the two known infinite families of holographic entropy inequalities found in arXiv:2309.15145 can indeed be written in the tripartite form. This is significant because such recasting is particularly nontrivial for these families. Apart from providing the explicit tripartite form expressions for every member of these two infinite families, we detail how we arrived at them, in the process deriving several useful identities which may serve as stepping stones to formulate further repackaging of the corresponding information quantities. We also illustrate the power of the tripartite form by proving a number of structural properties satisfied by any holographic entropy inequality.

(2007) for the K\"ahler--Einstein metric of $\mathrm{dP}_3$ using the Laplacian spectrum of low torus-invariant modes. papers.title: Coherent Release Fronts in Krylov Chains and Thermal AdS$_2$ Response

The tail sets the logarithmic transit scale, while the finite sector shapes the resulting distribution. The early edge records the number of serial steps before emission, while the late edge reflects slow resonances and interference and can also exhibit logarithmic enhancements. Thus, one- and two-site sectors can share the same leading resonance in their continued-fraction descriptions yet produce distinct cumulative occupation patterns. We illustrate this framework in thermal AdS$_2$, where a dressed oscillator yields, in the weak-coupling limit, a two-site shallow sector coupled to the conformal tail.

papers.title: Conformal Anomalies and Generalised Energy Conservation in De Sitter Spacetime
papers.summary: We show that for bulk discrete series fields whose dual operators have integer conformal dimensions, the Generalised Energy Conservation (GEC) condition for de Sitter (dS) scattering amplitudes defined in even-dimensional extended Poincar\'e spacetime corresponds precisely to the absence of boundary conformal anomalies, including beta-function contributions, at the level of tree-level contact interactions. In contrast, holographic consistency in AdS/CFT enforces only the locality of the conformal anomaly. We find novel, unique four-point interactions involving three identical conformally coupled scalars and one discrete series scalar by performing both GEC and holographic bootstraps. This demonstrates that the solutions to GEC form a measure-zero subset of the holographically consistent solutions. Our holographic analysis agrees precisely with the expected renormalisation conditions for conformal field theory correlators. In addition, the constraint for a particular four-point configuration may be relevant for testing holographic consistency of scale-separated non-supersymmetric AdS$_4$ vacua.

papers.title: Haagerup conformal field theory at central charge eight

papers.title: Isotensor $\pi\pi \pi$ scattering with a $\rho$ resonant subsystem from QCD
papers.summary: This work presents a lattice quantum chromodynamics (QCD) determination of $\pi\pi\pi$ scattering amplitudes for the isospin-2 channel with angular momentum and parity $J^{P} = 1^+$. These combined data constrain the low-lying partial waves of the infinite-volume three-pion K matrix, from which we solve a set of coupled integral equations to extract the corresponding scattering amplitudes.

papers.title: Dirac Observables for Gowdy Cosmologies Regular at the Big Bang
papers.summary: Gowdy cosmologies are exact, spatially inhomogeneous solutions of the vacuum Einstein equations which describe nonlinear gravitational waves coalescing at the big bang singularity. With toroidal spatial sections they provenly have the asymptotic velocity domination property, in that close to the big bang dynamical spatial gradients fade out and the dynamics is governed by a Carroll-type gravity theory. Here we construct an infinite set of exact Dirac observables for Gowdy cosmologies, valid off-shell, strongly, and without gauge fixing. These observables stay regular at the big bang and can be matched to much simpler Dirac observables of the Carroll-type gravity theory. Conversely, in an adapted foliation there is a systematic anti-Newtonian expansion (in inverse powers of the reduced Newton constant) of the full Dirac observables whose leading terms are the Carroll ones. In particular, this provides an off-shell generalization of the asymptotic velocity domination property.

papers.title: Probing scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves in the nHz band: NANOGrav and SKA
papers.summary: Scalar-induced gravitational waves (SIGWs) have recently attracted considerable interest, both as a possible explanation for the nanohertz signal reported by the Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) collaboration and for their connection with primordial black hole (PBH) physics. In addition to SIGWs, scalar-tensor-induced gravitational waves (STGWs) have emerged as a promising cosmological source of the stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB). In this paper, we compute the STGWs generated during a generic matter-dominated (MD) era, as well as during an early matter-dominated (eMD) epoch followed by a sudden transition to the standard radiation-dominated (RD) stage, working in the Poisson gauge. We find that, in a purely MD age, the corresponding energy density rapidly dilutes, whereas in the presence of an eMD phase it remains non-vanishing due to the short duration of the eMD period. We then investigate whether the STGW signal could provide a dominant contribution to the \texttt{NANOGrav 15-year} dataset and we forecast the prospects for its detection with future observations by the Square Kilometre Array (SKA). In particular, we consider STGWs generated during both eMD and RD eras, including their linear-order contributions. We further inject the scalar-induced contribution, both as an additional component and as the only signal, and compare the spectra against the same datasets. Our results show that, although the SIGWs still appear to provide the dominant contribution and the posteriors are tightly constrained by the requirement of avoiding PBH overproduction, the GWs induced by scalar-tensor mixing constitute a viable target for future, more sensitive nano-Hz detectors of the SGWB.

papers.title: The Spurion Massive EFT (SMEFT)
papers.summary: We use the amplitude formulation of the SMEFT to introduce a spurion analysis of the SMEFT low-energy amplitudes in terms of the Higgs VEV. Each SMEFT contact-term is given as a sum of a few spurion structures, whose number depends on the electroweak charges of the external legs. The coefficients of these structures involve singlet combinations of Higgses from higher-order SMEFT contributions. We use this to derive the spurion expansions of the W- and Z-boson masses and mixing, and their three-point couplings to fermions. The textures of these couplings are saturated by the dimension-eight SMEFT. Our analysis can be generalized to higher-point amplitudes and nonzero Yukawa couplings.

papers.title: Expanding quantum magnetic field
papers.summary: We develop the quantum theory of the causal formation of a long-range magnetic field generated by an external current that is instantaneously switched on and subsequently kept constant in time. The resulting non-equilibrium quantum state, describing the expanding magnetic field, is obtained exactly and compared with the corresponding quantum magnetostatic state. In contrast to the magnetostatic case, the expanding solution exhibits a propagating shockwave-like front separating regions where the magnetic field has already been formed from those that remain causally disconnected from the source. We show that although the expanding field locally approaches the magnetostatic field behind the shockwave-like front, the associated quantum systems remain distinct at all times. In particular, we obtain manifestly different results for the energy, photon number, and their fluctuations in expanding and magnetostatic field configurations. Our results are first derived for a general external current and then illustrated with a specific example.

papers.title: Time-reversed stochastic inflation in the quantum well
papers.summary: Time-reversed stochastic inflation solves the stochastic evolution of the inflationary universe backward in time, by counting the number of e-folds from the end of quantum diffusion towards some initial state. The point of view of observers attached to the end-of-inflation hypersurface is thus enforced. In this work, we exactly solve time-reversed stochastic inflation in a flat and bounded potential, the so-called quantum well. At given lifetime, the field behaviour is found to be either indistinguishable from the one obtained in a semi-infinite flat potential, or, subject to enhanced stochasticity where any memory of the initial state is erased. The derived distribution of curvature perturbations reduces to the semi-infinite result for small fluctuations while it develops exponential tails for the large ones. Such tails arise for both positive and negative values, and decay twice as fast as the one obtained in the standard forward stochastic inflation. These differences may have important consequences for tail-sensitive phenomena, such as primordial black hole formation.

papers.title: On the Renormalization Group Flow of Active Flocks
papers.summary: We study the statistical field-theoretic renormalization of active flocks via the Martin-Siggia-Rose-De Dominicis-Janssen (MSRDJ) formulation of stochastic dynamics, focusing on the Toner-Tu theory of Malthusian flocks, or polar-ordered, momentum non-conserving active fluids in which density fluctuations relax sufficiently rapidly to be eliminated as hydrodynamic degrees of freedom. Working in the limit of isotropic diffusion in two spatial dimensions, we perform an all orders analysis of the perturbative renormalization of propagators and interaction vertices. We show that a nonlinearly realized diagonal rotation/shift symmetry gives rise to Ward identities that protect the trigonometric structure of the convective derivative, ensuring that the sine and cosine interaction potentials retain their functional form under renormalization up to a rescaling of their overall couplings. We demonstrate that the freedom to renormalize the dynamical critical exponent in this boost non-invariant theory prevents the determination of the precise values of the critical exponents and anomalous dimensions in the theory, highlighting parallels and crucial differences with sine-Gordon and XY models. We express all anomalous dimensions as functions of the dynamical critical exponent, which remains undetermined due to the absence of a relation ordinarily forced upon boost invariant systems. We revisit and contextualize several claims and counterclaims in the recent literature in light of these results.

papers.title: Soft-Radiation-Induced Decoherence of Heavy-Quark Spin Entanglement at the Electron-Ion Collider
papers.summary: Using the soft-gluon theorem, we identify a soft-recoil mechanism by which unresolved gluon radiation induces decoherence in the spin correlations of heavy quark-antiquark pairs produced by longitudinally polarized virtual photons in deep-inelastic scattering. Upon tracing over the unresolved gluon, the reduced spin density matrix is block diagonal in the mirror parity of the production plane and is governed by two coefficients: a parity-odd normal-spin flip, which reduces the normal-axis correlation, and a parity-even stochastic rotation of the spin-correlation plane about its normal, which suppresses the in-plane spin coherences while leaving the normal-axis correlation unchanged. From the complete tree-level next-to-soft amplitude with the exact color-octet structure we derive both coefficients, together with the trace and antisymmetric in-plane terms, in closed form. The parity-odd coefficient is the larger one, by a factor of at least $3.5$, and grows as the inverse square of the heavy-quark transverse momentum. We estimate the resulting reduction of concurrence and Bell-CHSH violation, and propose an infrared-safe, radiation-binned EIC observable, formed at fixed Born kinematics after longitudinal-transverse separation, which isolates the two channels. We estimate its size, including multiple wide-angle emissions in an independent-emission model, the conditions under which detector and kinematic effects cancel, and the statistics required. The latter, however, exceed the yield of exclusive heavy-baryon pairs at nominal EIC luminosity by several orders of magnitude, makes the observable elusive for the measurement accessible in that channel.

papers.title: Complex chromoelectric polarizability of a heavy-quarkonium resonance: pole response and channel-resolved effective-theory representation
papers.summary: For a stable compact quarkonium state in the pNRQCD multipole regime, chromoelectric polarizability arises at leading order from two E1 transitions through virtual color-octet states. For an unstable state, we define the corresponding response through the quadratic displacement of its complex resonance pole in a weak chromoelectric background, so that its real and imaginary parts describe field-induced shifts of the pole mass and width. Starting from a renormalized background-field correlator, we show that the resonance polarizability is given by the complete two-field kernel normalized by the energy derivative of the full inverse propagator at the pole. In an effective theory with explicitly separated intermediate sectors, the kernel contains the standard E1-octet-E1 contribution, the complete source response of decay channels already coupled at zero field, and local contributions. This distinction becomes essential above open-flavor threshold and reduces to the standard pNRQCD polarizability in the stable, energy-independent limit. A simple $D\bar D$ realization for the $\psi(3770)$ gives the complex pole-residue factor $1/[1-\sigma'(z_\psi)]=0.800-0.336$, illustrating that threshold dressing can substantially modify both the magnitude and phase of the response. The resulting pole-based relation identifies the quantity required for a source-dependent coupled-channel determination of the chromoelectric polarizability of a heavy-quarkonium resonance.

papers.title: Classical soft theorems meet the post-Newtonian expansion
papers.summary: Classical soft theorems govern the non-analytic structure of electromagnetic and gravitational radiation in the low-frequency regime, with the gravitational memory effect providing the canonical realization of the classical soft graviton theorem. While the soft behavior of radiation from hyperbolic scattering is well understood, its realization in gravitationally bound systems remains less explored. In this work, we study the soft structure of gravitational waveforms generated by compact binaries, focusing on the scattering of emitted radiation off the static background curvature within the multipolar post-Newtonian framework. We isolate the infrared (IR) logarithms associated with hereditary effects, including the tail-of-memory, and their higher generalizations with n-tail insertions. The resulting amplitudes exhibit a Laurent expansion in frequency space consistent with the Sahoo-Sen logarithmic soft theorems, thereby establishing a direct correspondence between gravitational memory effects, their higher-order tail corrections, and the soft expansion. We also comment on ultraviolet (UV) logarithms arising from short-distance sensitivity of the multipole expansion and their associated renormalization-group running.

papers.title: Stability and Formation of Solitonic Boson Stars
papers.summary: We extend a previous study of the radial stability of solitonic boson stars by nonlinearly evolving them under aspherical perturbations, and by studying their formation from the collapse of scalar clouds. We focus in particular on models previously identified as radially stable, despite having positive binding energy, which ordinarily suggests that dispersion of all scalar matter is energetically preferred. A mode analysis of our 3+1 evolutions produces no evidence for the presence of a non-radial instability in any radially stable model, including those with positive binding energy. However, we do find evidence that such models do not generically form via gravitational cooling. We also find that it is possible to form another kind of compact object, which undergoes long-lasting radial oscillations and hence cannot be described as a stationary boson star. These objects may be characterized, we suggest, by energetically favoured multi-oscillating solutions to the Einstein-Klein-Gordon equations, present in certain regions of the parameter space.

papers.title: Safety of dynamical SUSY breaking and gaugino condensation in models of spontaneous CP violation
papers.summary: Solving the strong CP problem with spontaneous CP violation (SCPV) in SUSY requires that the constant term of the superpotential and the SUSY-breaking F-term be real to high accuracy. When both are generated dynamically, by gaugino condensation and by dynamical SUSY breaking (DSB), their phases need not vanish even if every theta-angle vanishes and every coupling is real; e.g., the multivalued non-perturbative superpotential may sit on a branch with a complex phase. In fact, gaugino condensation, in pure SUSY Yang-Mills theory and in its Affleck-Dine-Seiberg generalization, is safe only for N_c - N_f in {1,2} (N_c = 2 for pure SYM); otherwise the phase of the constant term reaches the gluino mass through anomaly mediation. The SUSY-breaking F-term is the main source of the MSSM soft masses, including the gluino mass, so its phase reaches theta-bar as well. In the framework of global SUSY, the 3-2 model introduces no phase. The ISS model is safe in that sector as long as the quark-mass splittings exceed the messenger-loop corrections; when they fall below, a complex vacuum orientation can generate an O(1) phase. The IYIT model can generate a purely imaginary F-term: for half of the real Yukawa parameter space, the meson VEV is purely imaginary and CP is spontaneously broken. In all three, the vacuum of the field coupled to the messengers is aligned with the constant term, so a complex constant term generates a strong CP phase through a second route, separate from anomaly mediation.

papers.title: Measuring $V_{cb}$ at electron-proton colliders
papers.summary: We study the prospects for an independent determination of $V_{cb}$ from bottom-tagged charged-current deep-inelastic scattering at future electron-proton colliders: the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh. The transition $e^- c \to \nu_e b$ probes $|V_{cb}|^2$ through a process with different theoretical and experimental uncertainties from semileptonic $B$ decays. We fit ratios of $b$-tagged charged-current event counts over flavour-inclusive ones in kinematic bins, including correlated parton-distribution and flavour-tag calibration uncertainties, and floating the other CKM parameters. With projected parton distributions and tagging performance motivated by existing studies, we find a potential relative sensitivity in $|V_{cb}|$ of about $0.8\%$ at the LHeC with $1\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity and $0.7\%$ at FCC-eh with $2\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$. The corresponding EIC sensitivity is instead at the level of $20 - 30 \%$, depending on the configuration. The LHeC could thus provide a high-energy determination competitive with low-energy ones, but with substantially different dominant systematic uncertainties, on the timescale of its proposed operation between the HL-LHC and FCC-ee. We identify precise flavour-tag calibration and control of the kinematic response as the main requirements for realising this potential sensitivity.

papers.title: Direct Detection of Solar Neutrinos to Probe Tensions and Break Degeneracies in Long-Baseline Neutrino Experiments
papers.summary: Long-baseline (LBL) accelerator experiments are sensitive not only to the standard neutrino oscillation parameters but also to new physics. Currently, there exists a tension between NOvA and T2K data that can be explained by vector non-standard neutrino interactions (NSI) with complex couplings, which in turn introduce degeneracies in LBL measurements. We demonstrate that dark matter direct detection experiments can use their measurements of solar neutrinos to test the NSI resolution of this tension and to break these degeneracies. Using recent solar neutrino data from LZ, XENONnT, and PandaX-4T, we show that dark matter direct detection experiments already constrain part of the NSI solution of the NOvA-T2K tension. These experiments can also probe parts of the NSI parameter space that even DUNE will be blind to. Our analysis combines nuclear recoils from $^8$B neutrinos and electron recoils from $pp$ neutrinos. A future xenon experiment, such as XLZD or PandaX-xT, will be able to cover a significant fraction of the NSI solution of the NOvA-T2K tension.

papers.title: Exothermic dark-photon dark matter and the LZ high-recoil event: finite-reheating constraints
papers.summary: An excited dark-matter state can produce a high-energy nuclear recoil by releasing its mass splitting in a collision. Motivated by the $248$~keV LUX--ZEPLIN candidate, we study freeze-in of a $45$~GeV pseudo-Dirac particle with a $1$~MeV splitting and a $1$~GeV dark photon during non-instantaneous reheating. We choose a recoil normalization compatible with the published INTEGRAL/SPI three-photon decay limit. It predicts $0.43$ events in the LZ window and retains the reference recoil shape. Including both dark-photon and $Z$ exchange, we calculate production and entropy dilution for backgrounds with $T\propto a^{-\alpha}$ and $\rho_\phi\propto a^{-3(1+\omega)}$. For $\Tmax=m_\chi$, the observed abundance requires $\Trh=1.32$~GeV for matter-like constant-width reheating, $3.09$~GeV for quartic oscillations with scalar decay, and $0.588$~GeV for quartic oscillations with constant width, compared with $4.10$~GeV for instantaneous reheating. These finite-reheating solutions are insensitive to increasing $\Tmax$ above $m_\chi$. For $\Tmax\geq m_\chi$, adiabatic kination has no solution with $\Trh>5.96$~MeV, the BBN-motivated cutoff adopted for our scans. At $\alpha_D=10^{-10}$, the estimated thermal-mediator source is below $0.2\%$ of the Standard Model source, and self-conversion does not appreciably deplete the excited population. The calculation relates an exothermic recoil benchmark to the production and dilution history before radiation domination.

papers.title: A spurionic interpretation of RG-stable parameter relations in the two-Higgs-doublet model
papers.summary: Recent work on the two-Higgs-doublet model (2HDM) has uncovered basis-invariant relations among the parameters in the scalar potential that are stable under renormalization group (RG) evolution but do not coincide with any of the standard Higgs-family or Generalized-$\mathrm{CP}$ symmetry classes of the scalar sector. These relations have subsequently been reformulated in terms of so-called GOOFy transformations. In this paper, we show that the same fixed surface admits a conventional interpretation in terms of spurions. The gauge-covariant kinetic terms of the 2HDM possess a Higgs-family $\mathrm{U}(2)_H$ symmetry, and the couplings in the potential may be organized into irreducible spurions under its nontrivial $\mathrm{SU}(2)_H$ subgroup. We first explain the one-loop closure in the spurion language and then establish stability to all orders in the scalar and gauge couplings in any mass-independent scheme. General Yukawa couplings introduce additional Higgs-family covariants and can spoil the scalar-sector selection rule. We therefore consider the six conventional Higgs-family and Generalized-$\mathrm{CP}$ symmetries of the 2HDM, imposed as exact symmetries of the full Lagrangian, and show that closure is controlled by whether the relevant Higgs-family triplet contains an invariant direction. The spurion formulation thus provides a basis-covariant and conventional group-theoretic explanation of the RG stability of the 2HDM parameter relations.

papers.title: Two-loop $gg\to AA$ amplitudes near threshold and the double parton scattering singularity
papers.summary: The two-loop amplitudes for pseudoscalar pair production in gluon fusion, $gg\to AA$, with each pseudoscalar emitted from its own effective gluon vertex, are known in closed form, but large cancellations near threshold obscure their analytic structure. We expand the IR-finite amplitudes in the pseudoscalar velocity $\beta_A$ through $\beta_A^6$ at fixed scattering angle. All inverse powers of $\beta_A$ and the odd powers through $\beta_A^5$ cancel, and at leading power the angular dependence enters only through $\ln(2p_T/m_A)$. We identify this logarithm with the double parton scattering (DPS) singularity: with the overall constant fixed at threshold, the factorisation formula of Gaunt and Stirling reproduces the velocity dependence of its one-loop coefficient in the forward limit to $3\times10^{-15}$, and a one-loop $gg\to HH$ analysis confirms the corresponding CP-even weight. At two loops the equal-helicity amplitude grows as $\ln^3p_T$, with the leading logarithmic ratio of planar $\mathcal N=4$ super Yang-Mills theory, while the opposite helicity amplitude, which has no one-loop DPS logarithm, grows as $\ln^2p_T$. In the finite virtual correction, relative to the squared tree amplitude, the highest logarithm at order $\alpha_s^2$ is $-\tfrac{7}{64}\alpha_s^2N_c^2\ln^2(2p_T/m_A)$. For $\beta_A\leq0.2$ the series reproduce the unexpanded amplitudes with relative errors of at most $6.77\times10^{-5}$ at the tested points; they provide this two-loop contribution to the hard function for soft-gluon resummation of the pair invariant-mass distribution near $m_{AA}=2m_A$ and are released with code for their numerical evaluation.

papers.title: Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory and its application to $X_b$
papers.summary: Following the discovery of the exotic state $X(3872)$ in the charmonium spectrum, the possible existence of an analogous state, $X_b$, in the bottomonium sector has attracted considerable attention of the hadronic physics community. In this work, we lay the ground for the development of Born-Oppenheimer chiral effective field theory (BO$\chi$EFT), that allows us to include both quark and hadron degrees of freedom as well as the full complexity of the meson-exchange potential in a systematic way. For illustration, the formalism to leading order (LO) is applied to the system of $\chi_{b1}$ states and in particular the $X_b$. The two parameters that are present at this order are constrained using experimental information on the bottomonium spectrum together with lattice input on static quark-antiquark potentials, including string breaking effects. The framework identifies the observed $1^{++}$ state at 10.513 GeV with a predominantly molecular $X_b$, the bottom counterpart of the $X(3872)$, and predicts an additional predominantly compact bottomonium state at 10.544 GeV, about 60 MeV below the $B\bar{B}^*$ threshold.

papers.title: Quasiparticle Modeling of Strongly Magnetized Strange Quark Systems
papers.summary: We examine spin-polarized Strange Quark Matter and the complex structure of Strange Quark Stars in the existence of a strong magnetic field. Our framework uses a quasiparticle model, en hanced by a QCD-informed effective quark mass dependent on both chemical potential value and magnetic field strength. The resulting Equation of State yields an energy per baryon below the iron limit, supporting the hypothesis that the actual ground state of matter is strange matter. The Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff expressions are solved and find that the maximum stellar mass decreases with the degree of spin polarization, reaching as high as 2.35 Mo with a related radius 12.33 km. Furthermore, the model predictions for mass, radius, and surface redshift are in excel lent conformance to observational limitations for the massive pulsar PSR J0952-0607. These results highlight the crucial role of quasiparticle medium effects and strong magnetic fields in describing dense matter.
