papers.title: Pythia-Contrib: a modular contribution framework for the Pythia 8 event generator
papers.summary: Pythia is a general-purpose Monte Carlo event generator used in particle, astroparticle, and nuclear physics, by theorists and experimentalists, to simulate particle collisions. Because of the size and diversity of the user community, it is challenging to address all of the needs for new and varied physics models. This paper describes the Pythia-Contrib system, which allows for third-party developers to contribute code to Pythia without introducing external software dependencies to the Pythia code base.

papers.title: Bottom-Charm $[bc]$ Diquark Masses from QCD Laplace Sum-Rules
papers.summary: Constituent mass predictions for bottom-charm $[bc]$ color-antitriplet diquarks are generated using QCD Laplace sum rules. We calculate the diquark correlator within the operator product expansion to next-to-leading-order (NLO), including terms proportional to the four- and six-dimensional gluon and six-dimensional quark condensates. Existing analytic expressions for the resulting multi-scale master integrals are insufficient for these calculations, so we utilize numerical $D$-dimensional loop integration techniques. The sum rule analyses stabilize in all four channels yielding constituent masses in GeV of: scalar ($0^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$, pseudoscalar ($0^-$) $(6.04\pm0.60)$, axial vector ($1^+$) $(5.60\pm0.56)$ and vector ($1^-$) $(5.99\pm0.60)$. These constituent mass results are discussed in comparison with values used in diquark models of tetraquark hadronic states. We also summarize QCD sum rule predictions for diquark masses for all possible quark-flavor combinations, providing QCD-based criteria for assessing the diquark mass parameters used in constituent diquark models of hadrons.

papers.title: Constraints on pion parton distributions at small $x$ from leading-neutron electroproduction data
papers.summary: We revisit the extraction of parton distribution functions (PDFs) in the pion in a global QCD analysis of pion--nucleus Drell--Yan and leading-neutron (LN) electroproduction data, in view of recent suggestions that uncertainties on the pion PDFs at small parton momentum fraction $x$ are dramatically underestimated. We perform a set of controlled fits that vary the LN data coverage, PDF parametrization, and positivity constraints, determining both the PDFs and pion-nucleon splitting functions simultaneously. While the use of a restricted H1 LN data sample used by the Fant\^omas group is found to enlarge the PDF uncertainties and admit solutions with vanishing gluon PDFs, our global analysis provides a good description of an extended H1 and ZEUS LN database, significantly reducing the parametrization dependence and strongly disfavoring a zero gluon distribution.

papers.title: Thermal spectral functions of heavy and exotic Mesons from a hQCD at finite density
papers.summary: In this work, we study spectral functions of heavy and exotic mesons in a self-consistent Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton model at finite temperature and chemical potential, where the dilaton is allowed to back-react on the geometry. A non-quadratic dilaton profile is introduced to reproduce the nonlinear Regge trajectories of heavy-flavor mesons, and the corresponding spectral functions are computed for charmonium, bottomonium, tetraquark, and hybrid channels. In all cases, increasing either temperature or chemical potential suppresses and broadens the quasiparticle peaks, signaling sequential in-medium dissociation; for each radial family, the 2S-like state melts before the 1S-like state. The predicted melting temperatures obey the mass ordering $T_{\rm melt}^{\pi_1(1400)}<T_{\rm melt}^{J/\psi}<T_{\rm melt}^{Z_c(3900)}<T_{\rm melt}^{\Upsilon(1S)}$, with $T_{\rm melt}\simeq 1.08,\ 2.96,\ 4.44$, and $5.93\,T_c$, respectively, so heavier states remain bound up to higher temperatures. These results provide quantitative, testable predictions for heavy-ion experiments probing tetraquark and hybrid mesons in hot and dense QCD matter.

papers.title: Superhorizon enhancement of the hydrodynamic GW tail in Standard Model embedded warm inflation
papers.summary: Hydrodynamic fluctuations in the primordial plasma generate a gravitational-wave (GW) background that grows like $f^3_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ in terms of the current frequency. However, within the ($10^{-4}_{ } ... 10^4_{ })\,$Hz band of upcoming interferometers, the modes likely re-entered the Hubble horizon when the hydrodynamic noise was no longer at its maximal value. To address this situation, we define a model-independent transfer function for GWs generated by hydrodynamic (or other white-noise) fluctuations at any time. Employing appropriate variables, we show how this transfer function, together with the simpler vacuum one, can be determined numerically for a general expansion history. The results are illustrated for Standard Model embedded warm inflation scenarios, including both the vacuum and hydrodynamic parts. Following previous estimates, we find that a pre-exit-generated hydrodynamic tail becomes almost flat below $(10^5_{ } ... 10^7_{ })\;$Hz. Its small-$f^{ }_\mathrm{\scriptscriptstyle 0}$ intercept remains finite, and can then moderately influence observational constraints through the tensor-to-scalar ratio ($r$).

papers.title: Decoherence as a Detector-Resolution Flow
papers.summary: We consider the QED final-state radiation modeled by $\gamma\gamma^\ast\to\pi^+\pi^-+X$, including its finite-temperature generalization, as an open quantum system, and study the evolution of the pion-pair momentum density matrix as the detector resolution scale is varied. We derive an explicit relation between the Lindblad jump operator and the Wilson line associated with soft photon radiation. We find that real emission and virtual correction serve as two separate contributions to momentum decoherence, and together they give rise to the real--virtual cancellation at the density-matrix level. The external finite-temperature photon bath modifies the decoherence rate by a Bose factor consistent with the Feynman--Vernon influence-functional approach. We emphasize that our conclusions also apply to hard fermion production thanks to the universality of the soft radiation.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced Search for Galactic Dark Photons Using Cat-State Cavities
papers.summary: We present a quantum-enhanced search for the Galactic dark-photon background (GDPB), a relativistic and anisotropic vector field that can be produced by dark-matter decay or annihilation in the Milky Way halo. We reinterpret an existing quantum-enhanced dark-photon dataset obtained with a superconducting circuit QED platform originally developed for wave-like dark-photon dark-matter searches, consisting of a high-$Q$ niobium cavity in the $\mathrm{TM}_{010}$ mode dispersively coupled to a transmon qubit. By preparing four-component cat states and performing repeated quantum non-demolition parity measurements, analyzed with a hidden Markov model, we extract photon-transition probabilities for multiple cat amplitudes and integration times. The coupling to the GDPB is governed by a polarization- and angle-dependent cavity overlap function, which predicts a distinctive diurnal modulation of the excitation rate for both longitudinal and transverse polarizations. From the absence of such modulation, we set 90\% confidence-level bounds on the kinetic-mixing parameter $\epsilon$ for two benchmark production mechanisms (parametric and cascade decay) over the relativistic mass range $m_X \ll \omega_c$.

papers.title: The Semileptonic B Frontier: LHC, B-factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision
papers.summary: This review document summarizes the main outcomes and key theoretical and experimental developments discussed at the workshop ``The Semileptonic $B$ Frontier: LHC, $B$-Factories, Lattice QCD & the Hunt for Precision'', held at Laboratori Nazionali di Frascati on 16--18 February, https://agenda.infn.it/event/49469/. Bringing together experimentalists and theorists, the meeting addressed recent advances and outstanding challenges in both charged-current ($b \to c/u\,\ell\nu$) and neutral-current ($b \to s\,\ell^+\ell^-$) semileptonic $b$-hadron decays. We synthesize current experimental measurements from Belle, Belle~II, and LHCb with state-of-the-art theoretical inputs---including Lattice QCD determinations, Heavy Quark Expansion (HQE) frameworks, and QED radiative corrections. In addition to reviewing the status of CKM matrix elements, hadronic form factor extractions, and Lepton Flavor Universality (LFU) tests, this report highlights novel observables and fitting techniques designed to maximize the sensitivity of future analyses and guide upcoming data-taking campaigns.

papers.title: The dead-cone effect in charm, bottom and top quark jets in angular and momentum space
papers.summary: The dead-cone effect reflects the mass dependence of QCD radiation from heavy quarks. We investigate this phenomenon from charm and bottom to top quarks using two-dimensional angular distributions and single-particle inclusive momentum spectra. The angular distributions illustrate the depletion of radiation around the heavy-quark direction, while the momentum spectra provide a quantitative observable of the effect. For charm and bottom jets, fragmentation functions reconstructed from LEP data at the $Z$ pole exhibit a strong suppression of high-momentum particles, quantitatively described within the Modified Leading Logarithmic Approximation of perturbative QCD. The analysis is extended to $\sqrt{s}=1$ TeV using Monte Carlo simulations. A hypothetical stable-top sample isolates the primary top-quark radiation pattern, whereas the physical decay $t\to bW$ introduces coherent radiation from the $tb$ colour dipole, obscuring the primary dead cone. By exploiting the dependence on the $b$-quark emission angle $\Theta_b$, we reconstruct the primary top-quark parton momentum spectrum through extrapolation to $\Theta_b\to0$. In contrast, the small-angle gluon and parton distributions do not converge to the stable-top dead-cone pattern because of radiation from the decay $b$ quark. These findings establish the inclusive momentum spectrum as a robust quantitative observable of the top-quark dead-cone effect and provide a unified description of mass-dependent QCD radiation from charm to top.

papers.title: Transport of hard probes in the glasma
papers.summary: The quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formed in relativistic heavy-ion collisions at RHIC and the LHC thermalizes from an out-of-equilibrium state of strong classical gluon fields known as the glasma. Jets and heavy quarks, produced in the initial scatterings, traverse these pre-equilibrium fields, but the glasma stage is neglected in phenomenology, which may bias the extracted QGP transport coefficients. This thesis studies its impact on jet and heavy quark transport. The glasma is described in the Color Glass Condensate framework by solving the classical Yang-Mills equations on a real-time lattice. The fields initially form longitudinal electric and magnetic flux tubes whose transverse correlation length is set by the saturation scale $Q_s$. Probes are studied with both classical transport equations and quantum evolution in the light-front Hamiltonian approach. The transport coefficients for jets and heavy quarks are much larger than in the QGP and anisotropic between transverse and longitudinal directions. The azimuthal decorrelation of back-to-back $c\bar{c}$ pairs in the glasma is comparable to that from the QGP, making $D\bar{D}$ angular correlations a potentially measurable glasma signature. The glasma also modifies the nuclear modification factor $R_{AA}$, though the effect is moderate compared to the nuclear parton distribution contribution. A systematic gauge-invariance analysis shows that the distinction between kinetic and canonical momenta is essential when comparing classical and quantum results, and that Coulomb gauge fixing largely reduces gauge artifacts. Finally, the eikonal quantum evolution of a high-energy quark is studied with time-dependent Basis Light-Front Quantization. The resulting momentum broadening agrees with the classical estimates and lays the groundwork for including quantum radiation.

papers.title: Thermal properties of the $\rho$ meson from a machine-learning-improved holographic QCD model
papers.summary: The thermal properties of the \(\rho\) meson are revisited within the soft-wall AdS/QCD framework. The dilaton background is calibrated against lattice QCD screening-mass data through a neural-network-assisted inverse procedure. Using this calibrated background, we compute the temporal vector spectral function and the lowest vector quasi-normal modes. The pole mass \(m_{\mathrm{pole}}(T)\) and thermal width \(\Gamma(T)\) are then extracted from the corresponding complex quasi-normal mode frequencies. Adopting the vanishing real part of the quasi-normal mode frequency, \(\omega_{\mathrm{Re}}(T_d)=0\), as a criterion for meson dissociation, we estimate \(T_d\approx168\,\mathrm{MeV}\). As the temperature increases, the thermal width grows, and the spectral function evolves from a narrow Breit-Wigner-like resonance peak into a transport peak, confirming the QNM prediction that the vanishing of the pole mass is accompanied by the emergence of a transport peak and making it difficult to identify a quasiparticle peak. A numerical extraction of the dispersion relation shows that the propagator can be described by a finite-temperature simple-pole form with momentum-dependent thermal width, characterized by a diffusion coefficient \(D(T)\) and an effective propagation speed \(u(T)\), whose temperature dependences are also extracted. This form modifies the usual relation between the screening and pole masses. These results may provide a useful reference for effective studies of the hot hadronic medium.

papers.title: Displaced tracks as a signal of dark matter co-annihilation: a case study using inert doublet model at $e^+e^-$ collider
papers.summary: Dark sector containing heavy (charged) particles with small mass splitting with dark matter (DM) can co-annihilate and produce correct relic density, evading direct detection bounds. In such compressed spectra, the charged state can be long-lived and decay to DM along with a very soft charged particle, giving rise to distinctive disappearing or kink track signatures at colliders. As an example, we consider the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), where the charged scalar $H^\pm$ can be nearly degenerate with the neutral DM state ($H^0$), and produce a soft pion ($\pi^\pm$) when it decays. We investigate this signature at a future $e^+e^-$ collider, focusing on electroweak $H^+H^-$ pair production and its displaced decays. By varying the mass splitting, we explore the transition from prompt soft-particle signatures to long-lived and disappearing-track signatures. Our analysis demonstrates the potential of future lepton colliders to probe the interplay between the charged-particle lifetime, its decay probability within the tracking volume, and the production rate sensitivity to the compressed DM scenarios over a broad range of masses, allowed by cosmological constraints.

papers.title: Strangeness suppression, the $\phi$ meson and $\Lambda\bar\Lambda$ spin correlations from exact strangeness conservation at the quark level
papers.summary: In small collision systems strange hadrons are suppressed, and the suppression grows with the number of strange quarks. Exact strangeness conservation in a finite volume accounts for this, but when it is imposed on hadrons it leaves the $\phi$ meson unsuppressed, contrary to observation. We impose the conservation law on the strange quarks in a causally connected cluster, before hadronization, and count separately the combinations of a strange quark with the antiquark created together with it. A pair created from the vacuum cannot form a $\phi$, a pair created from a gluon can only if it loses its color. With one function of multiplicity, the mean number of strange quarks per cluster, the model describes kaons, $\phi$, $\Xi$ and $\Omega$ in pp and p--Pb collisions at the LHC; the data require that about half of the same-pair combinations are excluded from the $\phi$, and reject both an unsuppressed $\phi$ and a $\phi$ built only from different pairs at about five standard deviations. The same-pair combinations are those that carry the spin correlation observed in $\Lambda\bar\Lambda$ production, whose dilution is thereby tied to the $\phi$ suppression and is predicted to decrease with multiplicity

papers.title: Brownian GPDs: A Stochastic Calculus Approach to Generalized Parton Distributions from Integral Constraints
papers.summary: We present a stochastic calculus approach for modeling generalized parton distribution functions using information provided from lattice QCD calculations of Mellin moments, without assuming a functional form. Reconstructing the underlying dependence on the partonic momentum fraction from a limited number of moments constitutes an intrinsically non-unique inverse problem. Our goal is to provide a model agnostic way to determine GPDs subject to integral constraints. Thus, we derive and show usage of a controlled Langevin approach based on stochastic calculus and Brownian motion. The method combines a variational formulation, based on minimizing a Dirichlet action subject to the imposed constraints, with stochastic dynamics that generates an ensemble of admissible functions. The resulting ensemble provides a preferred reconstruction and characterizes the variability associated with incomplete integral information within the chosen stochastic model. The framework can accommodate general integral kernels and prescribed function values, offering a flexible approach to reconstructing functions from indirect constraints. Beyond its application to GPD phenomenology, the method provides a general strategy for investigating inverse problems in which integral observables are known but the underlying functional dependence remains undetermined. The approach may have more general applications beyond the scope of studying 3D hadron structure, and it is particularly useful in situations where we know definite integrals of functions with kernels, but do not know the underlying function.

papers.title: Effects of quadratic frequency chirping and carrier-envelope phase on Schwinger pair production in polarized electric fields
papers.summary: We investigate electron-positron pair production in spatially homogeneous, time-dependent polarized electric fields using the Dirac-Heisenberg-Wigner formalism, focusing on the effects of symmetric and asymmetric quadratic frequency chirping and the carrier-envelope phase (CEP). Our analysis reveals how these field parameters govern both the momentum-space structure and the overall yield of the produced pairs. Frequency chirping substantially reshapes the momentum distributions by modifying their interference patterns and peak occupations. The momentum distributions are particularly sensitive to weak chirping, whereas strong chirping produces pronounced oscillatory and ring-like structures across all polarization states. The total pair yield increases with chirp strength, with symmetric chirping consistently producing a higher yield than asymmetric chirping for the parameter range considered. Moreover, the sensitivity of the total number density to polarization decreases progressively with increasing chirp strength, becoming negligible in the strongly chirped regime. The CEP further modifies the momentum distributions by altering their shapes and relative peak occupations, with the extent of these changes depending on the polarization state. Our findings establish a theoretical framework for exploring external-field configurations that optimize the yield of Schwinger pair production.

papers.title: Top-Quark Mass Scheme Uncertainties in Higgs Boson Pair Production via Gluon Fusion
papers.summary: We investigate theoretical uncertainties arising from the choice of the top-quark mass scheme in Higgs boson pair production via gluon fusion. First, we implement the resummation of the top-quark mass logarithms obtained for the $gg\to HH$ amplitude at high energy and study its phenomenological impact on cross sections. Second, we formulate a threshold-aware treatment of the top-quark mass based on short-distance mass definitions, combining an MSR description near the top-pair threshold with an $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ treatment in the high-energy regime. Within the dynamical prescription, the combined mass-scheme variation of the SM inclusive NLO cross section at $\sqrt{s}=14$ TeV is $^{+5.2\%}_{-0.2\%}$. This estimate provides an alternative to the conventional OS-$\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ envelope.

papers.title: A global analysis of ${\bar B}\to DP$ and ${\bar B} \to {\bar D} P$ decays
papers.summary: Recently, a fit to the 15 measured branching ratios of ${\bar B} \to D P$ decays ($B = \{B^+, B^0, B_s^0\}$, $D = \{D^0, D^+, D_s^+\}$, $P \in \{\pi, K\}$) was performed under the assumption of flavor SU(3) symmetry [SU(3)$_F$]. A terrible fit was found: there was a $> 5\sigma$ disagreement with the SU(3)$_F$ limit of the Standard Model [SM$_{\rm{SU(3)}_F}$]. It was also found that this discrepancy can be removed by adding $\sim 20\%$ SU(3)$_F$-breaking effects. Now, the ${\bar B} \to D^0 P$ amplitudes can contribute to other observables (direct and indirect CP asymmetries) if they interfere with the amplitudes for ${\bar B} \to {\bar D}^0 P$ decays. This happens if the $D^0$ and ${\bar D}^0$ decay to the same final state (e.g., $K^+ K^-$, $\pi^+ \pi^-$, $K^\pm \pi^\mp$, etc.). In this paper, we perform a combined fit of ${\bar B} \to D P$ and ${\bar B} \to {\bar D} P$ decays, including all observables. We again find a $> 5\sigma$ disagreement with the SM$_{\rm{SU(3)}_F}$, and we find that the data can be explained if $\sim 60\%$ SU(3)$_F$-breaking effects are included.

papers.title: Audible curvaton: modulated phase transition as the origin of large-scale curvature perturbations and gravitational wave anisotropies
papers.summary: We propose a post-inflationary first-order phase transition modulated by a light spectator field as the origin of primordial large-scale curvature perturbations. Spectator fluctuations acquired during inflation modulate the bubble nucleation history, generating curvature perturbations together with correlated intrinsic gravitational-wave (GW) anisotropies. We show that this mechanism can reproduce the observed amplitude of curvature perturbations while producing a loud stochastic GW background in the frequency bands of space-based detectors such as LISA, Taiji, and TianQin. A concrete benchmark yields strongly enhanced intrinsic GW anisotropies and a local primordial non-Gaussianity signal within reach of future large-scale-structure surveys.

papers.title: Chandra-JWST Probing the Effects of Moderate X-Ray Superflares on Protoplanetary Disks
papers.summary: Powerful X-ray flares from young stars may rapidly alter the physical and chemical conditions of their planet-forming disks, but direct observational tests remain scarce. We present a Chandra-JWST/NIRSpec study of infrared spectral variability associated with pre-main-sequence (PMS) X-ray flares in the Orion Nebula. Combining six Chandra/ACIS-I observations with three NIRSpec-MOS visits, we analyze two-epoch spectra of 10 X-ray Flare stars and 12 matched non-flaring Controls among 84 observed disk-bearing PMS stars. We investigate three diagnostics: narrow 2.8-4.3 micron features, HI Br-alpha, and the CO fundamental band. Flare stars show tentative evidence for relatively fewer variable narrow features at longer wavelengths than Controls, while feature incidence decreases strongly with projected distance from the dominant ionizing O star Theta1 Ori C. Most classifiable features appear in absorption. These properties suggest that at least some features may arise in externally irradiated disk atmospheres and/or associated photoevaporative flows, with their apparent epoch-to-epoch variability potentially reflecting spatial sampling of such locally structured material rather than intrinsic temporal changes. Br-alpha behaves differently: flare stars show systematically stronger variability and uniquely exhibit absorption-core profiles, suggesting control by magnetospheric accretion and stellar magnetic processes rather than disk irradiation. The CO fundamental band shows no significant flare-associated variability, consistent with thermochemical models predicting weak responses to moderate X-ray superflares. This pilot study demonstrates the potential of coordinated Chandra-JWST observations to probe how young stellar magnetic activity affects planet-forming environments, motivating future monitoring to build larger superflare samples and extend them into the rare X-ray mega-flare regime.

papers.title: Binding energies in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ fermion--antifermion channels from the ladder Bethe-Salpeter and Schr\"odinger equations
papers.summary: In this work, we calculate the binding energies of an equal-mass fermion--antifermion system in the $0^{-+}$ and $1^{--}$ channels from the ladder Bethe--Salpeter (BS) equation with scalar, pseudoscalar, and vector exchange. The results are compared with those of the Schr\"odinger equation with the corresponding leading static interaction in two regimes: pointlike massless exchange at weak coupling and finite-mass exchange with monopole form factors at stronger coupling. For the BS calculation, we use two independent numerical methods based on momentum-space integral equations and coordinate-space differential equations. The differential-equation method gives estimated relative binding-energy errors below $10^{-9}$ in both regimes. For massless vector exchange in Coulomb gauge, the numerical results are consistent with the uncrossed-ladder perturbative spectrum through the $O(m\alpha^5)$ terms. The results for massless scalar exchange and vector exchange in Feynman gauge are consistent with the common Wick--Cutkosky expansion through order $m\alpha^3$. For finite exchange masses, the differences from the leading static Schr\"odinger spectra at the same masses, couplings, and form factors depend strongly on the exchange and channel. Scalar exchange gives nearly degenerate channels with much weaker binding than the Schr\"odinger reference. In contrast, vector exchange with only the metric term retained gives stronger binding than the Schr\"odinger reference in $0^{-+}$ and weaker binding in $1^{--}$. Notably, retaining the full Proca numerator substantially increases the vector binding in both channels. Pseudoscalar exchange also supports bound states and favors $1^{--}$, although its leading static central interaction vanishes.

papers.title: Correlation of galactic very-high-energy gamma-ray sources detected by LHAASO with high-energy neutrinos
papers.summary: We conducted an investigation into the possible correlation between very-high-energy (VHE, $E>$ 0.1 TeV) gamma-ray sources, as identified by the Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory (LHAASO), and high-energy neutrino events captured by the IceCube Neutrino Observatory. For this analysis, we utilized the First LHAASO catalog, which comprises 90 VHE gamma-ray sources, and the IceCube Event Catalog of Alert Tracks (IceCat-1), which includes 348 track-like neutrino events. Through Monte Carlo simulations, we assessed the correlations between the neutrino events and LHAASO sources, achieving the best p-values of 0.237, 0.312, and 0.115, respectively, for all LHAASO sources, KM2A sources, and WCDA sources. These findings imply that the spatial coincidence between LHAASO sources and neutrino alerts is relatively weak. Furthermore, under the assumption that gamma-rays are exclusively generated through hadronic interactions, we estimated the most optimistic theoretical neutrino fluxes from LHAASO sources and compared them with the IceCube observed fluxes. The results indicate that the majority of these sources are improbable counterparts to the detected neutrinos. In conclusion, LHAASO sources could be potential galactic neutrino emitters but currently do not exhibit compelling evidence, thereby underscoring the necessity for elevated sensitivity levels in forthcoming detection instruments like IceCube-Gen2.

papers.title: Constraint on particle mass of dark matter based on XTE J1814-338 observation and DANS model
papers.summary: The small observed radius of neutron star XTE J1814-338 (with mass of $1.21_{-0.05}^{+0.05}$ $M_{\odot}$ and radius of $7_{-0.4}^{+0.4}$ $\rm{km}$) poses a great challenge to the traditional neutron star model composed of normal nuclear matter. The dark matter admixed neutron star (DANS) model provides a clue to solve this challenge. By employing the self-interacting fermionic dark matter model, we investigate the effects of dark matter parameters including the particle mass, self-interaction strength, and mass fraction of dark matter on the properties of DANSs. Our results indicate that the joint constraints from the observation of XTE J1814-338 and the astrophysical limits on the dark matter self-interaction cross section derived from observations of different colliding galaxy clusters can provide effective constraints on the particle mass of dark matter. Specifically, to simultaneously satisfy the small radius of XTE J1814-338 and the self-interaction limit, the particle mass of self-interacting fermionic dark matter is constrained to the range from sub-GeV to a few GeV.

papers.title: Excited-State Effects in Nucleon Sigma Terms from a Variational Analysis
papers.summary: We investigate excited-state effects in nucleon sigma-terms in lattice QCD using twisted-mass clover-improved fermion ensembles. We study correlation functions with nucleon and multihadron nucleon-$\sigma$-meson interpolating operators. The analysis is performed using three gauge ensembles, including one ensemble simulated with two degenerate light, a strange, and a charm quark with quark masses tuned to approximately their physical value. We solve the generalized eigenvalue problem that arises from the matrix of correlators and show that the three-point function for the light sigma-term obtained using the optimal linear combination of interpolating operators has substantially reduced time dependence without loss of statistical precision. We apply Laplace filtering and investigate residual excited-state contributions in the extraction of $\sigma_{\pi N}$. Using the same optimal linear combination of correlators as for $\sigma_{\pi N}$ for the strange sigma-term we also observe suppressed excited state contributions over an extended range of source--sink time separations. For the charm sigma-term, we observe negligible time dependence within the large statistical uncertainties, and these improvements show no significant effect.

papers.title: Can bosenovae deplete the galactic dark matter?
papers.summary: No: neither through the bosenovae of gravitational atoms formed around stars and compact objects, nor through those of boson stars formed in the galactic dark-matter halo. We assume that all the dark matter consists of ultralight bosons with attractive self-interactions, which can be captured in the gravitational potential of astrophysical objects or condense into self-gravitating configurations. When these systems collapse in a bosenova, part of their mass is turned into relativistic radiation that escapes the galaxy. We bound the mass that a single object can eject and sum it over realistic models of the Milky Way and of other types of galaxies. For gravitational atoms, with realistic stellar populations and stellar evolution, the stars of the Milky Way deplete at most $\epsilon^{\rm GA}_\star\simeq3\times10^{-9}$ of its halo, and the pump is equally negligible in other galaxies. The central black hole, Sgr A$^*$, could reach $\epsilon^{\rm GA}\sim10^{-3}$, but only for a boson mass disfavoured by ultrafaint dwarf galaxies and beyond the validity of the perturbative treatment, where only a geometric bound on the dark matter flux is available. For boson stars feeding on the rest of the halo, these would radiate at most $\sim3\times10^{-5}$ of the Milky-Way halo and $0.1\%$ of a DF2-like one.

papers.title: Topological Diagrams and Hadronic Rescattering: A Framework for CP Violation in Charmed Baryon Decays
papers.summary: Establishing CP violation in the charmed baryon sector remains a central challenge in particle physics. In this work, we develop a framework for CP violation in charmed baryon decays by combining quark-level topological amplitudes with the hadron-level rescattering mechanism. The two descriptions are connected through (1,1)-rank amplitudes, which are linear combinations of topological amplitudes and can be matched directly to the chiral Lagrangian. We verify that the rescattering amplitudes derived from topological amplitudes are consistent with those obtained directly from the chiral Lagrangian and show explicitly that the isospin sum rules are preserved. The $u$-, $t$-, and $s$-channel rescattering amplitudes contributing to each (1,1)-rank amplitude in the $SU(3)_F$ limit are derived. It is found that the long-distance rescattering contributions to quark-loop amplitudes can be related to those of tree amplitudes without introducing additional nonperturbative parameters. We perform global fits to available branching-fraction and decay-parameter data and predict the CP asymmetries in charmed baryon decays. The $\Lambda^+_c\to p\eta^\prime$ mode, with a predicted CP asymmetry of order $10^{-3}$, is identified as a promising channel for CP violation searches in charmed baryon sector. We also suggest measuring more observables in $\Xi^0_c$ decay modes to reduce the uncertainties in the CP violation predictions. In addition, the K\"orner-Pati-Woo theorem is found to be in tension with rescattering dynamics, casts doubt on the validity of its conventional proof. A precise measurement of the branching fraction of the $\Lambda^+_c\to \Sigma^+K^0_S$ mode would provide a stringent test the K\"orner-Pati-Woo theorem.

papers.title: Relativistic correction to the binding energies of two-body hadronic molecular states
papers.summary: This study presents a systematic estimation of the relativistic correction to the binding energies of two-body hadronic molecular states by comparing the numerical solutions of Schr{\"o}dinger, Salpeter, and Bethe--Salpeter (BS) equations derived from the same one-boson-exchange (OBE) interaction, with the OBE input couplings kept fixed and without refitting the potential to each bound state. All BS results are computed in the ladder approximation. The numerical results reveal a counterintuitive, coupling-dependent property: for MeV-scale binding with heavy exchanged mesons, the binding energies from the ladder BS and Schr\"odinger equations at the same parameters can differ by large factors. They show that shallow binding alone does not guarantee a small three-dimensional reduction effect when the interaction is short-ranged and strongly coupled. Specifically, we first benchmark the effect in a scalar model and then extend the analysis to the $D\bar{D}$ system with hadronic form factors. In the shallow $D\bar{D}$ region illustrated, the magnitude of the ladder BS binding energy amounts to only $10\%\sim 30\%$ of the Schr\"odinger result at the same couplings. Such large discrepancies show that calculations based on the Schr\"odinger or Salpeter equations should be treated with caution when fixed OBE input parameters are transferred without matching or refitting. This conclusion does not conflict with the universality of shallow bound states, which concerns low-energy observables after short-distance parameters have been matched.

papers.title: Higgs Decays at NLO in the SMEFT
papers.summary: The calculation of precise predictions for Higgs decays is a necessary ingredient for determining Higgs properties at the LHC and future colliders. We compute all two- and three-body Higgs decays at next-to-leading order (NLO) in both QCD and electroweak interactions using the dimension-6 Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT). Results for four-body Higgs decays that are accurate to NLO QCD/electroweak order in the SMEFT are obtained using the narrow width approximation. Our results are contained in a flexible Monte Carlo program, NEWiSH, that is publicly available and we illustrate the impact of the NLO electroweak corrections for HL-LHC, Tera-Z, and Higgstrahlung projections.

papers.title: $\mathbf{\gamma Z}$ Box at Low Energy
papers.summary: We calculate the 1-loop $\gamma Z$ box-graph correction to electron-quark scattering at low energy and low momentum transfer. Both electron and quark masses are kept non-zero. From our result, we extract coupling constants for the low-energy effective Lagrangian with parity-violating 4-fermion interaction terms. We study the zero-mass limits and show that a non-zero electron mass is sufficient to obtain finite, well-defined couplings which are insensitive to a hadronic mass cutoff. We finally discuss the impact of our results on the determination of the weak charge of the proton from polarized electron-proton scattering.

papers.title: Study of Form Factors and Observables in $B_c^- \rightarrow D_{s}^{*-}\ell^+\ell^-$ and $B_c^- \rightarrow D_{s}^{*-}\nu\bar{\nu}$ decays
papers.summary: We investigate the decays $B_c^- \rightarrow D_{s}^{(*)-}\ell^+\ell^-$ and $B_c^- \rightarrow D_{s}^{(*)-}\nu\bar{\nu}$ within the Standard Model (SM), employing perturbative QCD (pQCD) form factors that are sensitive to the wave functions of $B_c$ and $D_{s}^{(*)}$ mesons. We determine the shape parameters of these mesons and the $B_c \to D_s^{(*)}$ form factors at $q^2 = 0$ from available lattice QCD inputs for $B_s \to D_s^{(*)}$ and $B_c \to D_s$ transitions. To obtain the $q^2$ dependence of the $B_c \to D_s^*$ form factors, we employ heavy-quark spin symmetry (HQSS) and an appropriate parametrization scheme over the allowed $q^2$ region. Based on these inputs, we present predictions for branching ratios and lepton-flavour-sensitive observables. Furthermore, we perform a detailed angular analysis of the cascade decay $B_c^- \to D_s^{*-}(\to D_s^- \pi^0)\,\ell^+\ell^-$, providing Standard Model predictions for several angular observables.

papers.title: Quantum speed limit time for bipartite entanglement in neutrino oscillations in matter with nonstandard interactions
papers.summary: In the three-flavor neutrino oscillation framework, we investigate the transition probabilities of an initial muon neutrino flavor state in the presence of nonstandard interactions (NSIs) characterized by complex off-diagonal ($|\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}|e^{i\phi_{\alpha\beta}}$) and diagonal parameters ($|\epsilon_{\alpha\alpha}-\epsilon_{\beta\beta}|$), including a $CP$-violating phase and a constant matter potential, under both normal (NO) and inverted mass ordering (IO) scenarios. Within these scenarios and through the lens of mode entanglement, bipartite entanglement measures such as entanglement entropy and capacity of entanglement are quantified in terms of the transition probabilities, which can be measured in neutrino oscillation experiments. Using these two bipartite entanglement measures, we further explore the quantum speed limit (QSL) time, which describes how rapidly bipartite entanglement evolves during neutrino oscillations. We illustrate our results using the baseline lengths and energies corresponding to ongoing long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments, such as T2K, NO$\nu$A, and the upcoming DUNE experiment. In the presence of a $CP$-violating phase and a constant matter potential, both with and without NSI effects, we compare the QSL time behavior for bipartite entanglement in neutrino oscillations for NO and IO. The most pronounced discrepancies in the QSL time for bipartite entanglement arise from the off-diagonal NSI parameter $\epsilon_{\mu\tau}$ across both the NO and IO scenarios. We emphasize that among all the experiments considered, NO$\nu$A and DUNE exhibit a rapid suppression of bipartite entanglement in neutrino oscillations in the standard oscillation scenario with NO at the end of their baseline lengths for the corresponding best-fit value of $CP$-violating phase. Our results hint at a possible imprint of new physics in neutrino oscillations.

papers.title: Momentum fraction and hard scale dependence of double parton scattering in heavy-ion collisions
papers.summary: In a previous work, we studied the momentum fraction and hard--scale dependence of double parton scattering (DPS) in proton--proton collisions and the resulting dependence of the effective cross section on the final--state observables. In this paper, we extend those results to heavy--ion ($pA$ and $AA$) collisions, accounting for nuclear effects in the relevant kinematic region, namely shadowing and antishadowing. In addition to modifying the longitudinal parton distributions, these effects also alter the transverse parton distribution of the nucleus, for which we propose a simple new nuclear profile. We further hypothesize that partons inside a bound nucleon are more widely separated than in a free proton. We compute the effective cross section for the available $p$Pb data, obtaining reasonable agreement, and provide predictions for future measurements at the LHC. The observed dependence of our predictions on the final state indicates that DPS in heavy--ion collisions can be used to probe the transverse profile of the free proton and the bound nucleon, primarily in $pA$ collisions, as well as the transverse structure of the nucleus, mainly in $AA$ collisions.

papers.title: $\gamma Z$-exchange contribution in elastic $ep$ scattering by perturbative QCD
papers.summary: In this study, we calculate the $\gamma Z$-exchange contribution to elastic $ep$ scattering at large momentum transfer within perturbative QCD. We present analytical expressions for the $\gamma Z$-exchange contributions to the amplitudes. We also estimate the asymptotic behaviors of the amplitude contributions and of the physical quantity $A_{\text{PV}}$ at high momentum transfer. These asymptotic behaviors determine the subtraction order in the dispersion relations (DRs) satisfied by the amplitudes. \textcolor{black}{At high $Q^2$ beyond the forward limit, our pQCD analysis shows that this subtraction order is fixed by the high-$\nu$ behavior of the amplitude coefficients $c_i^{\gamma Z,\text{PV}}$, and that $c_{3,A}^{\gamma Z,\text{PV}}$ requires a once-subtracted DR.} Within the present pQCD framework and the adopted proton distribution amplitudes, these high-energy results also provide nontrivial constraints on low-energy DR assumptions.

papers.title: Baryon enhancement in jets
papers.summary: The enhancement of the baryon production relative to mesons in small-collision systems is considered a breakthrough result of the Large Hadron Collider since a similar effect in heavy-ion collisions is understood by invoking the formation of the strongly-interacting quark--gluon plasma. In this paper, a baryon enhancement is reported for $p_{\rm T}^{\rm ch,jet}>15$ GeV/$c$ jets produced in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV simulated with PYTHIA8. The effect can be explained as a transition between quark-initiated jets (low jet multiplicities) to gluon-initiated jets (high jet multiplicities). The present result contributes to a deeper understanding of the multiplicity dependence of baryon enhancement across different collision systems.

papers.title: New Determinations of the Charm and Bottom Quark Masses Using QCD Quarkonium Sum Rules
papers.summary: We reanalyze the perturbative QCD (pQCD) corrections to quarkonium QCD sum rules and extract the heavy quark masses $\overline{m}_{q}(\overline{m}_{q})$ ($q=c,b$). At present, the pQCD corrections to the correlation functions of two heavy-quark pseudoscalar and vector currents at zero momentum transfer, denoted as $M_{n,q}^{X,\rm th}$ ($X = P, V$), are calculated up to the $\mathcal{O}(\alpha_s^3)$ order. These corrections exhibit significant renormalization scheme and scale dependence, which introduces large theoretical uncertainties and deteriorates the precision of heavy quark mass determinations. In this work, we eliminate the renormalization scheme and scale ambiguities in the perturbative part of $M_{n,q}^{X,\rm th}$ by adopting the Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) within the characteristic operator (CO) approach. The CO approach, a novel extension of the standard PMC procedure, simultaneously determines the effective coupling $\alpha_s(Q_*)$ and the effective quark mass $\overline{m}_q(Q_*)$. It systematically absorbs the nonconformal $\{\beta_i\}$-terms and $\{\gamma_i\}$-terms via the renormalization group equations, yielding a strictly scheme- and scale-independent conformal perturbative series. Based on the improved PMC conformal series, we further provide reliable estimates for the unknown $\mathrm{N^4LO}$ contributions using the Pad\'e approximation method. {The final predicted heavy quark masses in the $\overline{\mathrm{MS}}$ scheme read: $\overline{m}_c(\overline{m}_c)=1278.8\pm 3.9~\text{MeV}$, extracted from the second moment of the charmed pseudoscalar correlator $M_{2,c}^{P}$; and $\overline{m}_b(\overline{m}_b) = 4161.0\pm 9.0~\text{MeV}$, extracted from the second moment of the bottom vector correlator $M_{2,b}^{V}$. Both results agree well with the PDG world averages with deviations smaller than $2\sigma$.

papers.title: A Phenomenological Study of Semileptonic $B^+$ and $B_s^0$ Decays into Axial-Vector Mesons $\big(D_1(2420),\, D_1^\prime(2430),\, D_{s1}(2460),\, \text{and } D_{s1}^\prime(2536)\big)$ within the Standard Model
papers.summary: We study semileptonic $B$ meson decays $B^+ \to D_1^{(\prime)}\ell^+\nu_\ell$ and $B_s^0 \to D_{s1}^{-(\prime)}\ell^+\nu_\ell$, where $\ell=\mu,\tau$. The final state axial vector mesons are treated as mixtures of the heavy quark basis states with light degree of freedom angular momenta $j_\ell=1/2$ and $j_\ell=3/2$, parametrized by the mixing angle $\theta_{D_1}$. Using form factors obtained in the covariant light front quark model, we analyze the dependence of various observables on $\theta_{D_1}$ such as polarized and unpolarized branching ratios, the lepton forward-backward asymmetry, the longitudinal polarization fraction, and the lepton flavor universality ratios. In addition, we also discuss correlations among different observables. We study these observables in the experimentally motivated mixing angle regions as well as over a wider range of $\theta_{D_1}$. Our results show that branching ratios and other observables are sensitive to the axial-vector mixing structure. These predictions provide useful Standard Model benchmarks for future measurements of semileptonic $B_{(s)}$ decays into orbitally excited mesons and may help to clarify the long standing $1/2$ vs. $3/2$ puzzle through semileptonic $B$ decays.

papers.title: Exploring the SMEFT landscape: Bayesian Model Selection for indirect discovery
papers.summary: We develop a framework for indirect discovery in the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) based on Bayesian model selection over operator subsets. We argue that SMEFT should be understood as a structured space of competing hypotheses rather than a single high-dimensional model, with each operator subset corresponding to a physically distinct low-energy realisation of new dynamics. Bayesian inference is applied at the level of model space itself, assigning posterior probabilities to operator subsets and marginal inclusion probabilities to individual operators. A genetic algorithm efficiently navigates the high-dimensional discrete model space, concentrating evaluations in the high-posterior region, while the Bayesian Information Criterion provides a tractable approximation to the Bayesian evidence. We apply this framework to a dataset comprising electroweak precision observables from LEP and Higgs, top-quark, and diboson measurements from LHC Run 2, at both linear and quadratic order in the Wilson coefficients, with one-loop renormalisation group evolution systematically included. The analysis finds no statistically significant evidence for any departure from the SM, and demonstrates that Bayesian Model Average posteriors on Wilson coefficients carry substantially improved characterisation potential compared to traditional global fits. The operator correlation matrix encodes the relational structure of the model posterior, identifying operator pairs that co-appear in high-posterior models and flat directions where additional measurements would be most valuable. The sensitivity of all results to the choice of matching scale $\mu_0$ is assessed, and its promotion to a continuous parameter of inference is identified as a natural extension of the framework.

papers.title: Fully-heavy multiquarks in neural-network quantum states
papers.summary: Exotic hadrons beyond the conventional quark model provide a direct window into the dynamics of strong interaction. However, extracting the multiquark spectroscopy has to face the quantum many-body problem, which is still a theoretical challenge. In this case, diquark-antidiquark model is proposed as an approximation. Although this model can describe the spectroscopy roughly, it cannot describe the detailed dynamics. Furthermore, the methods aiming at dealing with many-body problem, e.g. the Gaussian expansion method and Diffusion Monte Carlo, are proposed, but face severe computational bottlenecks. In this work, we introduce the neural-network quantum state (NNQS) approach to investigate the spectra of fully-heavy multiquark states within the non-relativistic potential quark model. By employing deep neural networks to represent the complex many-body spatial wave function, and constructing the color-spin part exactly from group theory to enforce fermionic antisymmetry, our approach effectively overcomes the dimensionality obstacles inherent in traditional methods. The results are compared with various model calculations, demonstrating that NNQS offers superior accuracy and flexibility, particularly in treating high-dimensional correlations. This work establishes NNQS as a promising tool for exploring the spectroscopy of exotic hadrons.

papers.title: Collider Probes of Dark Energy Microphysics
papers.summary: The physical origin of dark energy remains one of the most profound open questions in modern physics. Although cosmological observations tightly constrain the equation of state parameter $w$, this information alone does not reveal the underlying microphysics, as many distinct theoretical models can reproduce the same expansion history. A key discriminator among these models is the sound speed of dark energy perturbations, yet this quantity remains largely unconstrained by current astrophysical observations. In this work, we propose a fundamentally new approach: using collider measurements of beyond-the-Standard-Model (BSM) mediator resonances as a probe of dark energy microphysics. We construct a unified effective-field-theory framework in which a dynamical dark energy scalar is coupled, through symmetry-motivated derivative interactions, to a pseudoscalar mediator in the 2HDM+$a$ model. These interactions naturally induce invisible decays and modify the propagation of the BSM mediator in a dark energy background, leading to measurable distortions of resonance properties at colliders such as the LHC. We show that the decay widths, branching ratios, and kinematic structure of the mediator resonance become sensitive to the propagation properties of dark energy fluctuations, in particular the sound speed. As a result, collider observables provide a direct and complementary handle on dark energy microphysics, with the potential to distinguish between models that are otherwise indistinguishable through cosmology alone. Our results establish a new paradigm in which high-energy collider experiments can probe the physics of cosmic acceleration, revealing a connection between the smallest and largest scales in nature and opening a novel experimental pathway to uncover the fundamental origin of dark energy.

papers.title: Axion Misalignment Across First-Order Phase Transitions
papers.summary: When the axion mass is generated during a first-order phase transition and becomes non-vanishing only inside expanding true-vacuum bubbles, the standard picture of misalignment production is qualitatively modified. Using lattice simulations in an expanding universe, we study dark matter production within such a framework and identify two distinct regimes. For rapid transitions, the onset of oscillations is delayed until bubble percolation, enhancing the relic abundance. For slower transitions, spatial gradients generated by expanding bubbles suppress the effective misalignment angle through the bubble misalignment mechanism. We derive a semi-analytical expression for the relic density that provides a unified description of both regimes and accurately reproduces the simulation results. Finally, we show how this mechanism also modifies isocurvature perturbations and the small-scale matter power spectrum, with important implications for axion minicluster formation.

papers.title: Fully-beauty tensor tetraquark
papers.summary: Parameters of the fully-beauty tensor tetraquark $T=bb\overline{b}\overline{b }$ are computed using QCD sum rule method. The mass $m$ and coupling $ \Lambda $ of this state are evaluated by means of two-point sum rule approach. Prediction $m=(18530 \pm 86)~\mathrm{MeV}$ for the mass demonstrates that $T$ is stable against decays to pairs of $\eta_b \eta_b$ and $\Upsilon \Upsilon$ mesons. But it transforms to conventional particles due to $\overline{b}b$ annihilations to light quarks $\overline{q} q $ and $ \overline{s}s$ followed by creation of mesons $B^{(\ast)+}B^{( \ast)-}$, $ B^{(\ast)0}\overline{B}^{(\ast)0}$ and $B_s^{(\ast)0}\overline{B} _s^{(\ast)0}$. Partial width of these decay channels are calculated by invoking technical tools of three-point sum rule method. The latter allows us to estimate strong couplings at relevant tetraquark-meson-meson vertices and, hence, a width of the process under consideration. Our prediction $ \Gamma=(48 \pm 6)~\mathrm{MeV}$ along with the mass of this state can be valuable for experimental studies of all-heavy resonances.

papers.title: Thermal Leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze Model of Neutrino Mass
papers.summary: We investigate neutrino mass and thermal leptogenesis in the Babu-Nandi-Tavartkiladze (BNT) model featuring a scalar quadruplet ($\Phi$) and a pair of vector-like fermion triplets ($\Sigma$). In this framework, neutrino masses are generated via an effective dimension-7 operator $LLHH(H^{\dagger}H)/\Lambda^3$ at the tree level and via the dimension-5 operator $LLHH/\Lambda$ at the one-loop level. It naturally accommodates sub-eV neutrino masses even if the new physics scale $\Lambda$ is $\mathcal{O}(\rm TeV)$, thus making the model a compelling target for experimental searches. We explore the viability of thermal leptogenesis in this model, which is distinct from the canonical seesaw-based leptogenesis due to the presence of vector-like fermions. We find that leptogenesis is viable for $M_\Sigma \gtrsim 10^{7}$ GeV for a hierarchical spectrum of fermion triplets. However, in the quasi-degenerate regime, resonant enhancement of the $CP$ asymmetry lowers this scale down to $\mathcal{O}({\rm TeV})$, reconciling successful leptogenesis with the originally motivated TeV-scale phenomenology and testability of the model at colliders.

papers.title: Bare effective potential and Goldstone boson anti-resummation
papers.summary: I discuss the evaluation of the effective potential and related quantities starting from bare perturbation theory followed by $\overline{\rm{MS}}$ renormalization. The advantages of this method include a simple new way of avoiding infrared problems associated with Goldstone bosons, by treating their bare squared masses as two-point interaction vertices instead of incorporating them into the propagators. Thus, only positive integer powers of the Goldstone-boson squared masses appear at every stage of calculation, avoiding the imaginary parts and singularities encountered in intermediate steps of previous resummation methods for the minimization conditions. This Goldstone boson anti-resummation approach is implemented using simple rules provided through three-loop order in terms of the master vacuum integrals. Explicit results are given for the Standard Model at three-loop order. The method is shown to give effective potential minimization conditions that are consistent with previous resummation methods, but in a form more directly useful for related future multi-loop calculations of observables in the tadpole-free scheme.

papers.title: Atmospheric neutrino up-scattering explanation of LZ 2026 excess
papers.summary:
The recent observation of an isolated nuclear recoil at $248\pm 23\pm 23$ keV energy by the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment has motivated the community to look for a new physics explanation, as the Standard Model background estimation fails to accommodate it. Most of the existing literature hitherto considers a galactic halo dark matter with a heavier partner. In this work, we traverse the alternate route of atmospheric neutrino ($
u$) up-scattering, thus producing a massive beyond standard model (BSM) particle $\chi$ with mass $m_\chi$. The kinematic requirement of such a scattering demands a higher energy of the incoming neutrinos than elastic scattering, explaining the absence of excess events from solar $
u$ scattering. However, for high energy neutrinos in the tail of the atmospheric neutrino flux, the kinematic threshold no longer prevents events at low recoil energies. To avoid an excess of such events, we consider a momentum dependent operator, which suppresses the event rate at low recoil energies and allows a single event in the high recoil energy window. Such up-scattering on nuclei ($\mathcal{N}$), $
u \mathcal{N}	o \chi \mathcal{N}$, can be naturally realized in sterile neutrino models, though we keep our analysis generic without specifying $\chi$. We identify the region of parameter space that can produce such an isolated event, assuming a pseudoscalar mediator with mass $m_\phi$ that couples to the $
u$-$\chi$ pair with strength $y_\chi$ and to up quarks with strength $y_u$. For example, $m_\chi \simeq 1.13$~GeV, $m_\phi \simeq 494$~MeV and $\sqrt{y_\chi y_u} \simeq 0.33$ can account for the observed event while remaining allowed by other existing constraints.

papers.title: Measuring Dual-Superconductor Length Scales in the QCD Vacuum at HERA
papers.summary: In the dual-superconductor picture, the QCD vacuum behaves like a superconductor for chromoelectric fields, with characteristic penetration and coherence lengths. These scales have so far been studied primarily through lattice calculations of static flux tubes. We show that they are also imprinted on exclusive diffraction, where the transverse profile of a gluonic hotspot reflects the response of the vacuum to a localized color source. Using the Clem vortex profile, we fit all 104 H1 and ZEUS measurements of exclusive $J/\psi$ photoproduction and find $\chi^2/{\rm ndf}=0.72$, the penetration depth $\lambda=0.19(2)~{\rm fm}$, the hotspot core size $\xi_v=0.087(13)~{\rm fm}$, and the Ginzburg--Landau parameter $\kappa=2.7(7)$, placing the effective vacuum description in the type-II regime. The corresponding vector mass $1/\lambda=1.03(11)~{\rm GeV}$ agrees with the lattice gluelump mass, and the extracted parameters reproduce the QCD string tension with no free normalization.

papers.title: Hadronic light-by-light scattering in AdS/QCD and the muon $g-2$: tensor meson contributions
papers.summary: We briefly review the predictions of holographic QCD in hard-wall AdS/QCD models for the contribution of pseudoscalars and axial-vector mesons to the hadronic light-by-light amplitude and consequently to the muon anomalous magnetic moment, which allows one to satisfy the Melnikov-Vainshtein constraint in a purely hadronic model. Moreover, we discuss the role of tensor mesons in satisfying the remaining short-distance constraints, and provide details for a minimal model of tensor mesons that turns out to agree remarkably well with available data from BELLE as well as preliminary low-$Q^2$ data from BESIII. In an appendix, we also provide analytical results for the short-distance limits in hQCD and compare with the leading-order OPE result as given by the massless quark loop.

papers.title: Dark matter bound states made easy
papers.summary: A light force carrier can mediate long-range interactions between dark matter particles and facilitate the formation of bound states. Models incorporating these features have attracted considerable attention in recent years, with significant advances in both the theoretical understanding of such bound states and their impact on the parameter space consistent with the observed dark matter relic abundance. However, the relevant results and their consistent implementation in Boltzmann equations remain technically intricate, requiring careful treatment or the use of specialized tools. This complexity has hindered broader adoption of these findings and restricted their use to a small number of expert groups. To address this challenge, we propose a simple prescription based on the analytic limits of the relevant rates, which allows standard freeze-out computations to be refined through a straightforward semi-analytical prescription that captures the main features of the full calculation. We illustrate this approach for a $U(1)$ dark matter model with a light force carrier, including Sommerfeld enhancement and bound-state effects.

papers.title: Minimally modified Frampton--Glashow--Yanagida ansatz and its leptogenesis consequences: in light of recent JUNO's result
papers.summary: Motivated by the recent JUNO indication favoring normal neutrino mass ordering, we study two realizations of the minimally modified Frampton--Glashow--Yanagida (MMFGY) framework in the minimal type-I seesaw with two right-handed neutrinos. Both retain one exact Yukawa texture zero, supplemented by either a single physical CP-violating phase or a remnant CP symmetry. The explicit-CP realization yields twelve high-energy Yukawa configurations that reduce to three low-energy classes, with correlated CP phases and predictions for neutrinoless double-beta decay. In both realizations, a strongly suppressed second Yukawa entry can emerge, although the full-matrix hierarchy remains moderate in the quasi-degenerate regime. We analyze leptogenesis for a non-degenerate benchmark, quasi-degenerate TeV-scale right-handed neutrinos, and lower masses where coherent production, oscillations, and electroweak sphaleron freeze-out become important. Successful leptogenesis is obtained across a broad range of the scanned benchmarks, with increased sensitivity to the initial right-handed-neutrino abundance at the lowest mass scale. Requiring successful leptogenesis restricts the allowed phases while preserving the possibility of an approximate second zero. The two realizations exhibit distinct approximate-zero patterns and leptogenesis predictions, demonstrating how different restrictions on the high-energy Yukawa structure affect baryogenesis.

papers.title: Implication of multimessenger observations on the relativistic mean-field equation of state of dense nuclear matter and skin thickness of nuclei
papers.summary: The composition and properties of infinite nuclear matter under extreme conditions of temperature and pressure remain incompletely understood. In this work, we constrain the equation of state (EoS) of nuclear matter$-$constructed within the framework of the Relativistic Mean Field (RMF) model$-$by combining results from chiral effective field theory and multimessenger observations of neutron stars. Using the saturation properties of nuclear matter, we generate a wide ensemble of EoS, which are subsequently constrained within a Bayesian framework. The resulting posterior distributions provide tight bounds on both the saturation parameters and the coupling constants of the RMF model. The radius of a $1.4\,M_\odot$ neutron star is tightly constrained to $12.471_{-0.394}^{+0.427}\,\mathrm{km}$, while the maximum mass reaches $2.156_{-0.120}^{+0.175}\,M_\odot$. Furthermore, our analysis reveals that the $\omega$-$\rho$ coupling, which governs the density dependence of the symmetry energy, becomes increasingly significant under successive astrophysical constraints. Finally, the predicted $\rm r_\mathrm{skin}$ of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$ agrees well with the CREX measurement, whereas that of $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ remains in tension with PREX-II. In contrast to earlier studies, we do not observe a clear correlation between the $\rm r_\mathrm{skin}$ of $^{208}$Pb and the symmetry energy slope parameter $L$.

papers.title: Pion emission source shape in UrQMD Au + Au collisions at STAR energies
papers.summary: Femtoscopic measurements of two-pion Bose--Einstein correlations have established that particle-emitting sources in heavy-ion collisions are well described by L\'evy $\alpha$-stable distributions, motivating systematic studies across a wide range of collision energies. In this work, we present a three-dimensional femtoscopic analysis of pion pairs in Au+Au collisions simulated with the UrQMD model for collision energies $\sqrt{s_{NN}}=3$--$27\,\mathrm{GeV}$, taking the RHIC BES-II range of collider and fixed target experiment energies for reference. Using L\'evy-type source parameterisations, we extract the L\'evy index $\alpha$, the three-dimensional radii $R_\mathrm{out}$, $R_\mathrm{side}$, $R_\mathrm{long}$, and the pair multiplicity parameter $\lambda^{*}$ (related to the correlation strength $\lambda$). We investigate their dependence on the transverse mass ($m_T$) and collision energy, along with derived quantities such as the radius difference $R_{\mathrm{diff}}^2=R_{\mathrm{out}}^2-R_\mathrm{side}^2$ and the ratio $R_\mathrm{out}/R_\mathrm{side}$. We find that $R_\mathrm{out,side,long}$ all decrease with increasing $m_T$ and increase with collision energy, consistent with collective expansion, $R_\mathrm{long}$ showing the strongest and $R_\mathrm{side}$ the weakest energy dependence. The L\'evy index $\alpha$ decreases with collision energy, with a larger $m_T$-dependence towards higher energies. The $\lambda^{*}$ parameter is consistent with a constant close to unity in the absence of pions from long-lived resonances. These results provide a baseline for future comparisons with experimental measurements from the STAR Collaboration, contributing to constraints on the QCD phase diagram.

papers.title: Achieving a 0.49 keV threshold in the COSINE-100 dark matter experiment
papers.summary: The COSINE-100 experiment searched for weakly interacting massive particles (WIMPs) with NaI(Tl) crystals at the Yangyang Underground Laboratory. Using its full 6-year dataset, we lower the analysis threshold to 0.49 keV. A multi-layer perceptron classifier separates scintillation events from photomultiplier tube noise. It is trained with approximately $3\times10^{6}$ simulated scintillation waveforms per crystal, separately for groups of events with similar numbers of photoelectron clusters. The selection keeps more than 10% of scintillation events at 0.49 keV while limiting noise contamination to below 1%. The selection efficiency is validated with $^{22}$Na-calibration data and internal $^{22}$Na events, and the selection performance is stable over the six years of data taking. With this threshold, the median expected upper limit on the spin-dependent WIMP-proton cross section reaches $1.1\times10^{-36}$ cm$^2$ at a WIMP mass of 2.5 GeV/$c^2$, probing previously unexplored parameter space in the 2.0-2.8 GeV/$c^2$ mass range.

papers.title: Measurement of Born cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar\Sigma^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.5-4.9 GeV and partial wave analysis at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV
papers.summary: Using $e^+e^-$ collision data collected by the BESIII detector at BEPCII corresponding to a total integrated luminosity of 44.6 $\rm fb^{-1}$, we present the first measurement of the Born cross sections for the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. at fifty-six center-of-mass energies between 3.51 and 4.95~GeV. By fitting the dressed cross sections of $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. with the assumption of a power-law function plus a charmonium(-like) resonance, i.e., $\psi(3770)$, $\psi(4040)$, $\psi(4160)$, $Y(4230)$, $Y(4360)$, $\psi(4415)$, $\psi(4500)$, $Y(4660)$ or $\psi(4710)$, no significant charmonium(-like) state decaying into $pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. is observed. The product of branching fractions and electronic partial widths including their upper limits at the 90\% confidence level are provided for each decay. In addition, a partial wave analysis of the process $e^+e^-\to pK^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ + c.c. at $\sqrt{s}$ = 3.773 GeV is performed to investigate $N^{*}$, $\Lambda^{*}$ and $\Sigma^{*}$ resonances in the $K^{-}\bar{\Sigma}^{0}$ and $pK^{-}$ invariant mass spectra. Significant contributions are found from the $\Lambda(1520)$, $\Sigma(1670)$, $\Sigma(1915)$, $N(1900)$, $N(2300)$ and $N(2570)$. The masses, widths and production fractions for each component are determined.

papers.title: Measurement of electromagnetic transition form factors in two-photon collisions at BESIII
papers.summary: The muon anomalous magnetic moment, $a_\mu = (g-2)_\mu/2$, shows a sizeable discrepancy between Standard Model (SM) predictions and direct measurements, hinting at either New Physics or limitations in modeling low-energy strong interactions. As the uncertainty in the SM predictions currently exceeds the experimental uncertainty by a substantial margin, further improvements in theoretical precision are essential to clarify the origin of this discrepancy. The SM theoretical uncertainty is dominated by hadronic processes. The hadronic light-by-light (HLbL) scattering contribution relies on highly accurate data for hadron production via two-photon fusion. Operating at $\sqrt{s}=3.773\,\text{GeV}$ with over $20\,\text{fb}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity, the BESIII experiment is ideally suited to probe these processes at small momentum transfers. By precisely measuring channels like $e^+e^-\to e^+ e^-\pi^0$ and $e^+e^-\to e^+ e^-\pi^0\pi^0$, BESIII provides the critical experimental input necessary to sharpen the SM prediction and clarify the true nature of the $a_\mu$ anomaly.

papers.title: Search for resonant and nonresonant production of pairs of dijet resonances in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A search for pairs of dijet resonances with the same mass is conducted in final states with at least four jets. Results are presented separately for the case where the four jet production proceeds via an intermediate resonant state and for nonresonant production. The search uses a data sample corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the CMS detector in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV. Model-independent limits, at 95% confidence level, are reported on the production cross section of four-jet and dijet resonances. These first LHC limits on resonant pair production of dijet resonances via high mass intermediate states are applied to a signal model of diquarks that decay into pairs of vector-like quarks, excluding diquark masses below 7.6 TeV for a particular model scenario. There are two events in the tails of the distributions, each with a four-jet mass of 8 TeV and an average dijet mass of 2 TeV, resulting in local and global significances of 3.9 and 1.6 standard deviations, respectively, if interpreted as a signal. The nonresonant search excludes pair production of top squarks with masses between 0.50 TeV to 0.77 TeV, with the exception of a small interval between 0.52 and 0.58 TeV, for supersymmetric $R$-parity-violating decays to quark pairs, significantly extending previous limits. Here, the most significant excess above the predicted background occurs at an average dijet mass of 0.95 TeV, for which the local and global significances are 3.6 and 2.5 standard deviations, respectively.

papers.title: Long-Delayed Afterpulse Measurement of JUNO 20-inch Photomultiplier Tubes
papers.summary: In large-scale liquid scintillator detectors such as the Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory (JUNO), high-intensity events like cosmic muons induce photomultiplier tube (PMT) afterpulses that can interfere with the analysis of delayed physics signals. To systematically evaluate this instrumental background, we present a dedicated measurement of long-delayed afterpulses in two types of JUNO 20-inch PMTs: a dynode-based PMT and a microchannel-plate (MCP) PMT. The afterpulse time profiles were first characterized within a direct 1.8~ms waveform window and were further extended to 20~ms using a sliding-window readout strategy. Distinct long-delayed components are observed, revealing a strong dependence on the PMT multiplication structure. The dynode PMT exhibits a broad afterpulse component peaking at approximately 260~$\mu$s, whereas the MCP-PMT shows a pronounced peak around 90~$\mu$s, an additional component around 550~$\mu$s, and a much smaller, broadly distributed millisecond-scale component. For the microsecond-scale components, the afterpulse yield per primary photoelectron is at the $10^{-3}$ level in the selected delayed windows and increases approximately linearly with the primary light intensity. The accumulated delayed activity can therefore become non-negligible following high-intensity events. These quantitative findings provide critical inputs for PMT response characterization and for the accurate modeling of delayed correlated backgrounds in high-precision neutrino experiments.

papers.title: A Nontrivial Lattice Scalar Quantum Field Model
papers.summary: We introduce a new Euclidean quantum model with zero-spin scaled scalar fields on a spacetime hypercubic lattice, which we refer to as the hybrid model. The model coupling parameters are the hopping parameter $\kappa^2>0$ and the field interaction coupling $\alpha>0$. Using the technique of lattice scaled fields, with a noncanonical scaling that corresponds to a partial renormalization (wave function renormalization), we show that the partition function of this model satisfies both thermodynamic and ultraviolet stability bounds, with constants which are uniform in the lattice volume $\Lambda_s$ and the lattice spacing $a\in(0,1]$. As a consequence, the model has a finite free energy per degree of freedom in the thermodynamic limit $\Lambda_s\nearrow\infty$, at least in the subsequential sense. Subsequently, we can also take the ultraviolet or continuum limit $a\searrow 0$. Besides the finiteness property of the free energy, for sufficiently small values of the model coupling parameters $\kappa^2$ and $\alpha$, we show the model satisfies Osterwalder-Schrader positivity and construct the underlying physical quantum mechanical Hilbert space, and, using a polymer expansion, we show correlations also remain bounded in the thermodynamic limit. Finally, we perturbatively compute an infinite volume truncated four-point correlation showing it is nonzero. Noting that, for fixed $a$, perturbation series in $\kappa^2$ and $\alpha$ converges, these results are sufficient to show that our hybrid model makes sense as a lattice quantum field theory in spacetime dimension $d=3,4$, with possible extensions to other higher values of $d$.

papers.title: Constraining three-nucleon forces in nuclear lattice effective field theory
papers.summary: We study short-range three-nucleon forces (3NFs) in nuclear lattice effective field theory with a chiral two-nucleon interaction at N${}^3$LO. The one-pion-exchange ($c_D$) and contact ($c_E$) terms of the leading 3NF are decomposed into locally and non-locally smeared components and supplemented by partial-wave-resolved pair contacts coupled to the density of a third nucleon. We determine their coefficients from nuclear binding energies for nuclei in the mass range from $A=3$ to $A=40$ and neutron--alpha finite-volume energies. This allows to work out the minimal three-nucleon force that can be used for future precision studies in NLEFT.

papers.title: Extraction of spectral densities from lattice correlators: decoupling signal from noise
papers.summary: We expand the treatment of the problem of the extraction of smeared spectral densities from Euclidean correlators introduced in [Phys. Rev. D 99, 094508], providing an alternative which does not rely on the Backus-Gilbert regularization. This is possible due to the observation that the solution can be decomposed into a sum of terms, in the spirit of the singular value decomposition, where those with the largest contribution to the statistical noise happen to contribute the least to the central value of the smeared spectral density. The analysis of the systematics of the inverse problem is then shifted to finding the optimal truncation of such summation, so that the signal is saturated before the noise explodes. We scrutinise the performance and systematics of this approach either as a standalone procedure, or to complement the stability analysis required to extrapolate the unbiased result in the Backus-Gilbert regulated version of the solution.

papers.title: Renormalization-guided inverse blocking for lattice field generation: construction and validation
papers.summary: We propose an algorithm for generating lattice field configurations based on the approximate inversion of a renormalization-group blocking transformation. We optimize the blocking transformation using a ``perfect blocking'' condition so that the blocked lattice distribution is well approximated by a simple coarse action. The blocking is separated into an invertible smoothing transformation followed by decimation. Machine learning, in the form of a conditional normalizing flow, is used to reconstruct the short-distance degrees of freedom removed by the decimation. A short fine-action rethermalization then removes the residual mismatch. Because the coarse ensemble supplies the long-distance modes, the same blocking transformation and conditional flow can be reused recursively on larger lattices, producing a cascade of configurations from an initial small-volume ensemble. We test the method in two-dimensional $\phi^4$ theory with $\lambda=1$ at criticality and demonstrate stable cascade upscaling from $16^2$ to $2048^2$ lattices on local computational resources. Controlled rethermalization tests show that short-distance mismatches relax rapidly, whereas a deliberately introduced mismatch in the relevant thermal direction relaxes much more slowly. The construction uses ingredients that admit natural extensions to higher-dimensional systems and, ultimately, to gauge and fermionic degrees of freedom.
