papers.title: A Parsec-Scale Transient High-Frequency-Peaked Radio Source in the Very Large Array Sky Survey Brightening and Fading over a Decadal Timescale
papers.summary: A subset of active galactic nuclei (AGN) manifests as compact radio sources with peaked radio spectra, commonly referred to as peaked-spectrum (PS) sources. Generally, PS sources are interpreted as young radio jets, but the early evolution of the jet is rarely observed and not fully understood. Here, we present VT J182357-234511 (VT J1823-2345), a radio transient in the Very Large Array Sky Survey (VLASS) that resembles a PS source. Notable properties of VT J1823-2345 include: (i) brightening by a factor of 3 between 1996 and 2021 at 1.4 GHz, (ii) peaked spectra with high frequency peaks at $\nu_{\mathrm{p,obs}}\gtrsim6\,\mathrm{GHz}$, (iii) a peaked 3 GHz light curve that has been fading since 2023, (iv) a resolved Gaussian (major-axis) size of 0.4 mas in 2024, and (v) a linear polarization fraction $p_{\mathrm{L}}\simeq0.73\%$ at 8.8 GHz with an extreme Faraday rotation measure $\mathrm{RM_{\mathrm{obs}}} \sim +12,000\,\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{m}^{-2}$. On the sky, VT J1823-2345 coincides with a supernova remnant and an F-type star, but no background galaxy is seen. Based on the multi-wavelength properties, we disfavor Galactic transients, explosive extragalactic transients, and blazar variability as plausible explanations. We argue that VT J1823-2345 is consistent with a "short-lived" parsec-scale PS source with a decades-old jet that does not grow into a large-scale radio galaxy. From comparing the full VLASS light curves, we speculate that VT J1823-2345 is similar to many VLASS nuclear transients reported in the literature, which may represent an emerging class of transient radio jets, perhaps related to episodic AGN activity or jetted tidal disruption events.

papers.title: A Step-Like Transition Underlying the Life and Death of Galaxies
papers.summary: How galaxies stop forming stars is a complex and central problem in astrophysics. Numerous physical mechanisms have been proposed, yet a simple, unified framework connecting these mechanisms remains lacking. Here, we derive a step-function quenching response from the fundamental principle of gas mass conservation, governed by the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales. This response also enables the gas-supply timescale to be inferred from the observed quenched fraction. Applying this method to approximately 350,000 galaxies, we find a characteristic gas-supply timescale of ~1 Gyr, reveal distinct inside-out and outside-in quenching signatures associated with supermassive black holes and dark matter halos, respectively, and identify galaxies with intermediate stellar surface mass densities as occupying a critical state for quenching and rejuvenation. Our work establishes a unified physical framework in which a simple step-function response captures how diverse physical processes regulate galaxy quenching and the resumption of star formation through their effects on the competition between gas-supply and gas-depletion timescales.

papers.title: Modelling the 6.7 GHz Methanol Flaring in G358.93-0.03 Using the Maxwell-Bloch Framework
papers.summary: We model selected 6.7 GHz methanol flare profiles in G358.93-0.03 using the one-dimensional Maxwell-Bloch framework. The 2019 non-periodic flare, associated with an accretion burst, produced complex single-dish light curves characterized by sharp rises, multiple peaks, secondary structure, and extended decays. For six representative velocity channels, we model each light curve as a sum of scaled intensity responses from effective emitting systems driven by phenomenological pump pulses of fixed width but with component-dependent background rates, amplitudes, and arrival times. The inferred initial inverted column densities correspond to characteristic superradiance timescales $T_{R,0} \simeq 0.3$-$1.4~{\rm d}$, which are shorter than the adopted dephasing and relaxation timescales, $T_2 = 6.9~{\rm d}$ and $T_1 = 144.4~{\rm d}$. The fitted components therefore lie in the fast-transient superradiance regime. Existent VLBI observations motivate the possibility that a single-dish velocity channel blends emission from multiple unresolved flaring regions, although these observations are not used as direct fitting constraints. Although the decomposition is not unique, it provides a physically motivated description of the complex flare morphology within a unified Maxwell-Bloch framework.

papers.title: Dynamics of a switchback-like magnetic deflection induced by a propagating coronal jet
papers.summary: Parker Solar Probe (PSP) revealed the ubiquity of switchbacks (SBs), sharp, localised magnetic deflections in the nascent solar wind, renewing interest in their origin. One proposed mechanism involves solar jets: collimated, impulsive features driven by magnetic reconnection that launch Alfv\'enic torsional wavefronts into the heliosphere. We test whether realistic spacecraft sampling of a propagating solar jet produces in-situ signatures consistent with PSP observations. We also examine the 3D magnetic topology of the resulting structures and how deflection amplitudes evolve with the ambient plasma environment. We perform a 3D magnetohydrodynamic simulation of a solar jet in the ambient solar wind, embedding a virtual spacecraft trajectory based on PSP's actual 22nd-perihelion orbit to generate synthetic measurements. The simulation reproduces SB-like signatures with durations and profiles consistent with PSP observations, confirming earlier results from simplified trajectories. We visualise the fully 3D magnetic topology of a jet-driven SB region, identifying two field-line families: one with a single deflection and another with two sequential deflections along the same field line. Both are outward-propagating Alfv\'enic structures. Deflection amplitudes depend strongly on background plasma $\beta$, increasing substantially in low-$\beta$ regions and evolving more moderately where $\beta \sim 1$. These results show that solar jets can produce Alfv\'enic, SB-like structures along realistic spacecraft trajectories. Their topology is inherently 3D and structurally diverse, and their evolution depends on ambient plasma $\beta$. Complete magnetic reversals would require longer residence times in low-$\beta$ environments. Our findings support a solar origin for a fraction of SBs and constrain interpretations of their underlying magnetic structure.

papers.title: Refurbishment and Cryocooler Upgrade of the CPAPIR Wide-Field Near-Infrared Camera: Design, Integration, and Lessons Learned
papers.summary: The CAmera PAnoramique Proche Infrarouge (CPAPIR) is a wide-field near-infrared imager that has been operating at the Observatoire du Mont-M\'egantic (OMM) since 2004. After more than two decades of service, the instrument required a major refurbishment due to detector degradation, including the loss of one quadrant, as well as operational constraints associated with its liquid-nitrogen cooling system. To extend the instrument's lifetime and reduce maintenance requirements, the detector was replaced and the cooling system upgraded through the integration of a Sunpower CryoTel DS30 cryocooler. This paper presents the thermal and mechanical redesign of the instrument, including finite element analysis (FEA), three-dimensional CAD modeling, hardware selection, and laboratory validation. Particular attention is given to the challenges encountered during integration and testing, notably vibration mitigation and cryogenic system implementation. The resulting performance improvements and lessons learned from the upgrade are discussed. The upgraded instrument is scheduled for on-sky commissioning at the Observatoire du Mont-M\'egantic in summer 2026.

papers.title: Binary-lens amplification of starlight: from magnification flares to quasi-periodic tracking of orbital evolution
papers.summary: Supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHB) are expected at the center of galaxies as a result of galaxy mergers. The dynamics and evolution of SMBHBs shed light on the evolution and formation of galaxies, the gravitational wave background and the nature of gravity. Many methods have been proposed to identify sub-parsec SMBHBs via the detection of gravitational waves or the modulation of the emission from the surrounding gaseous environment. In a previous study, we proposed a new method of identifying SMBHBs in non-active galactic nuclei via gravitational lensing. The caustics, i.e. the source positions with a divergent magnification, exhibit a complex extended geometry which rotates with the binary period. Each caustic-crossing produces an extreme magnification by up to a factor of $10^{6}$. In this work, we generalize the previous study and describe the rich phenomenology of binary-lens amplification of starlight (BLAST). We explore the electromagnetic transients produced when accounting for the relative proper motion of the source, either a single or a binary star, the eccentricity and precession of the SMBHB, and the relative inclination. Systems where a star rapidly drifts across the caustic produce a single- or double-peaked flare. In the opposite limit, a star with no relative proper motion produces quasi-periodic lensed starlight (QPLS), i.e., repeated peaks that track the system's orbital evolution. We determine the expected magnification and peak duration in different circumstances, and calculate the magnification curves and their Fourier transforms. This study may help construct search pipelines to identify SMBHBs in electromagnetic time-domain surveys.

papers.title: GRB 181201A: Spectropolarimetric Constraints on Prompt Emission and Magnetic Field Structure
papers.summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) have served as testbeds for high-energy astrophysical phenomena since their discovery over 50 years ago. GRB detections reveal diverse properties across events, complicating efforts to constrain their emission mechanisms, magnetic fields, jet structures, and compositions. Spectropolarimetry is a powerful tool utilized to disentangle these properties. INTEGRAL/IBIS has previously detected three polarized GRBs 041219A ($65\pm 26$%), 061122 ($>$33%) and 140206A ($>$28%). We present the time-integrated and time-resolved analyses of the fourth-polarized GRB 181201A. This GRB exhibits high polarization ($81.5^{+17.2}_{-15.7}$%) over three time bins with the highest signal-to-noise ratio, and the polarization angle (PA) shows a modest temporal evolution. The photon index does not cross the synchrotron line-of-death and shows a hard-to-soft evolution. A high degree of polarization (PD) tends to disfavor a photospheric emission model, as previous studies indicate that this model yields PD $<$ 20%. A modest evolution in the PA points towards a non-axisymmetric jet with a multi-patch emission. Our results indicate that under standard synchrotron conditions, the magnetic field is coherent but lacks global structure. Moreover, the field has multiple patches, but only one or a few dominate due to high degrees of polarization, which overlap with the intrinsic maximum of synchrotron emission within 3$\sigma$ errors. The high PD is also indicative of the Compton Drag scenario, but only under certain conditions, such as viewing the relativistic jet near its edge. However, given our error bars and the scope for improvement in our pipeline, we cannot strongly favor either scenario; both may remain viable.

papers.title: Nonlinear Perturbations of Relativistic Stars
papers.summary: We extend the general relativistic Lagrangian perturbation formalism of Friedman and Schutz [Astrophys. J. 200, 204 (1975)] beyond linear order, retaining full time dependence of the perturbations. We provide general formulae to relate the Lagrangian and Eulerian perturbations to any general perturbative order. As a proof of principle, we apply the framework to tidally perturbed relativistic stars in Regge-Wheeler gauge and reduce the second-order field and conservation equations to master equations with a nonlinear source. Projecting the source onto the star's eigenmodes, we obtain a nonlinear equation of motion for the mode amplitudes and the coupling coefficients, which describe the interactions among the eigenmodes and with the external tidal field. Approximating the tidal field and the coupling coefficients, we compute the static quadratic Love number from the quadrupolar fundamental mode alone and find that it reproduces the direct metric-matching value to a reasonable accuracy of $4\%$, up to a further correction arising from the Hamiltonian and momentum constraints of the second-order tidal field.

papers.title: Spinformation: do gravitational-wave events carry information beyond effective spins?
papers.summary: While the spin vectors of binary black holes offer insight into the astrophysical formation channels of these systems, individual spins are less precisely measured through gravitational-wave observations than the effective inspiral spin $\chi_\mathrm{eff}$ and the effective precession spin $\chi_\mathrm{p}$. Reducing to effective parameters discards information in the data, but how much information is lost has yet to be demonstrated. Here we show how to quantify whether individual mergers carry information about component spins beyond the constraints implied by effective parameters (a.k.a. spinformation) and apply the technique to GWTC-5. Thresholding on information loss $\gtrsim 0.25$ bits, over $80\%$ of gravitational-wave events in GWTC-5 have component spin posteriors described by $\chi_\mathrm{eff}$ alone. Only $\sim3\%$ of gravitational-wave events have substantial spin information not explained by $\chi_\mathrm{eff}$ and $\chi_\mathrm{p}$. The catalog's component spin information is effectively two-dimensional in $\chi_\mathrm{eff}$ and $\chi_\mathrm{p}$. Using simulated signals, we find the noise realization can create or destroy over a bit of beyond-$\chi_\mathrm{eff}$ information: the structure in real data may therefore be driven by noise. At current sensitivity, component spins provide interpretive\textemdash rather than informational\textemdash advantage over effective parameters.

papers.title: Strong-Field Gravitational-Wave Lensing from Ray-Traced Arrival-Time Surfaces
papers.summary: The diffraction integral formalism has been greatly successful in describing gravitational wave lensing effects in scenarios where the wavelength of the signal is comparable to the characteristic length scale of the lens, known as the wave optics regime. However, the assumptions required to construct its integrand break down as the source approaches the strong gravity region of a black hole lens. In particular, we are interested in the lensed signal from a binary (the source) near a massive black hole (the lens). We present a new formalism for obtaining low frequency corrections to sources being lensed in the strong field regime of gravity by leveraging the fact that null geodesics obey the Hamilton--Jacobi equations. In doing so, we are able to construct a time delay surface without relying on the thin lens approximation, and solve the diffraction integral for the resulting surface directly. For a stationary source at $10M$, deep in the strong field regime, when comparing the results with a relativistic wave scattering model, we find $6.5\%$ and $0.3\%$ agreement in the peak amplification and first diffractive fringe, respectively. Furthermore, we find a $< 1\%$ agreement with the amplitude of the point mass lens with a source at $10^4 M$ in the weak field, but noticeable dephasing between the peaks of the amplification function at higher frequencies. This work allows for clean interpolation between otherwise separate regimes, valid for sources from $\sim 6M \to \infty$. It provides a transparent, physically motivated framework for computing beyond-geometric optics lensing effects in the strong field regime.

papers.title: Black Hole Fine Structure
papers.summary: In General Relativity, axial and polar black-hole perturbations share identical quasinormal-mode spectra, a property known as isospectrality. New physics can break this degeneracy, producing a spectral splitting analogous to atomic fine structure. We perform a theory-agnostic search for such splitting in gravitational-wave observations. We find no evidence for isospectrality breaking and place a combined $90\%$ upper limit of $<28.5\%$ on the relative frequency splitting. We map these constraints onto several modified-gravity theories, constraining the coupling-lengths to be $\lesssim 28\,\mathrm{km}$.

papers.title: The WDM time-frequency transform in gravitational-wave data analysis II: Evolutionary spectrum and noise covariance
papers.summary: Noise cannot be treated as stationary over the timescales required for upcoming gravitational-wave detectors, minutes for ground-based and months for space-based detectors. Nonstationarity leads to a non-diagonal frequency-domain noise covariance matrix, thus motivating a shift to the time-frequency domain. We introduce \emph{evolutionary power spectra} for describing nonstationary noise in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer time-frequency basis. Under the framework of oscillatory processes, we show that, to leading order in the ratio of the Meyer filter and the nonstationarity timescales, the evolutionary spectrum is a power-frequency distribution that can be estimated from a single noise realization. We derive the corresponding noise covariance matrix and show that it is band tri-diagonal, like its stationary counterpart. The exact covariance to all orders is positive semi-definite by construction and dense depending on the noise. We further derive the optimal tiling of the time-frequency plane that minimizes the error of a diagonal covariance approximation and show that coarse-graining the plane suppresses correlations quadratically. Using simulated data with a LISA Galactic foreground and a drifting powerlaw spectrum, we show that the stationarity approximation leads to signal-to-noise ratio loss and severely biases inference. For realistic LISA data, approximating the covariance as diagonal in the Wilson-Daubechies-Meyer domain is accurate for the narrow-band analysis of a single resolved Galactic binary, but insufficient for a broad-band analysis. Finally, we provide mitigation strategies for the wraparound correlations induced across the data time edges whenever the spectrum differs between the start and the end of the data.

papers.title: Quantum noise and torque correlations in a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter
papers.summary: Quantum fluctuations entering through weakly transmitting mirrors can limit a torsion-bar Sagnac speed meter for low-frequency gravitational-wave detection, even when its optical layout suppresses radiation-pressure back action. We show that, in the Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS), vacuum fields entering from behind the end and middle test masses can dominate the low-frequency quantum noise despite cancellation of the torques on opposite ends of each bar. For a reference configuration with mirror power transmissions of only $10^{-7}$, these fields contribute $89.7\%$ of the total quantum-noise power spectral density at 0.1 Hz. Omitting them would underestimate the amplitude spectral density by a factor of 3.11. Our input-output model connects the correlations produced by successive optical interactions to the forces on each bar and the measured signal. This connection shows why strong torque cancellation does not, by itself, ensure a corresponding improvement in detector sensitivity. Replacing mirror transmission with absorption at fixed reflectivity leaves the excess quantum noise essentially unchanged for the two operating points studied. The predicted signal response and quantum noise agree with independent FINESSE 3 calculations as recycling detuning and homodyne angle are varied. These results establish rear vacuum fields as a limiting noise source in this torsion-bar speed meter and provide quantitative requirements for its mirror and readout design.

papers.title: Testing Charged Black Holes Embedded in Anisotropic Matter and Surrounded by Plasma through Gravitational Lensing: Bounds from the Sloan Lens ACS Survey
papers.summary: We investigate weak gravitational lensing by a charged black hole surrounded by anisotropic matter, described by the two-component Kiselev metric, and immersed in a homogeneous plasma. We first examine the black hole geometry and horizon structure and then derive the weak-deflection angle from the Hamiltonian description of light propagation in plasma, using an expansion with a fixed turning point that we verify against direct numerical integration. Using the gravitational lens equation, we obtain the Einstein-ring angle, the image positions, the total magnification and the fractional magnifications of the primary and secondary images. We then confront the model with the Einstein radii of two galaxy-scale lenses of the Sloan Lens ACS Survey, J0008$-$0004 and J0029$-$0055. Because the Einstein angle cannot be smaller than the reduced deficit deflection, the observed radii give the mass-independent bounds $K<6.5\times10^{-6}$ and $K<4.2\times10^{-6}$, respectively. The charge correction to the Einstein radius is suppressed by $r_s/R_E\approx 5\times10^{-6}$ and is unobservable, while the plasma parameter at the optical wavelengths of the SLACS imaging is of order $10^{-22}$ and cannot be constrained. Our results show that galaxy-scale strong lensing data place stringent limits on anisotropic matter surrounding the lens, whereas plasma effects can be probed only at low radio frequencies.

papers.title: Biases in Ringdown Tests of General Relativity from Gravitational-Wave Microlensing
papers.summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) ringdown signals provide a powerful probe of the strong-field regime of general relativity (GR) through black hole spectroscopy and tests of the Kerr hypothesis. However, unmodeled propagation effects can bias the inference of remnant properties and the interpretation of ringdown features. We investigate the impact of gravitational lensing on ringdown inference and tests of GR using GW150914-like simulated signals spanning the long-wavelength, wave-optics, and geometric-optics regimes. We perform complementary time-domain post-merger and frequency-domain full inspiral--merger--ringdown analyses using unlensed waveform models. We find that lensing in the wave-optics regime can produce substantial biases in the inferred remnant mass and spin and can strongly affect the inferred modal content of the ringdown. In particular, it can spuriously favor the presence of the first overtone, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{221}_{220}\sim40$, even though the injected signal has no support for it. Parameterized ringdown tests can likewise yield strong apparent support for deviations from the Kerr quasinormal mode (QNM) spectrum, with $\log_{10}\mathcal{B}^{\rm modGR}_{\rm GR}\sim8$. In contrast, the evidence for higher-order modes remains largely unchanged for the simulated signals considered here. The parameterized analysis using the entire signal further shows that microlensing can bias the inferred frequency of the dominant $(2,2,0)$ QNM. These results demonstrate that unmodeled microlensing can produce systematic biases and spurious signatures in ringdown analyses, potentially affecting precision tests of the Kerr hypothesis.

papers.title: $^{16}$O(p,$\gamma$)$^{17}$F Reaction and the C and O Isotopic Ratios in Red Giant Branch Stars
papers.summary: The $^{16}$O/$^{17}$O isotopic ratio is a widely used tracer of nucleosynthesis and mixing processes in red giant stars. Its value depends on the rates of the proton-capture reactions responsible for the production and destruction of $^{16}$O and $^{17}$O among which the $^{16}$O(p,$\gamma$)$^{17}$F reaction plays a central role, as it involves both isotopes. This work reports on a new measurement of the $^{16}$O(p,$\gamma$)$^{17}$F cross section carried out at the Laboratory for Underground Nuclear Astrophysics (LUNA) over a center-of-mass energy range of 200 - 380 keV, a region previously unexplored by experimental studies. Two complementary techniques were employed: prompt gamma-ray detection and activation. The results obtained with the two techniques are consistent within experimental uncertainties. From the measured cross sections and existing literature data, we evaluate a new thermonuclear reaction rate, which is then used to demonstrate how simultaneous measurements of stellar carbon and oxygen isotopic ratios constrain the initial mass and the extent of the mixing events in red giant branch stars. In particular, we demonstrate how the $^{12}$C/$^{13}$C abundance ratio is primarily sensitive to the temperature T$_{\textrm{max}}$ attained during mixing, whereas the $^{16}$O/$^{17}$O abundance ratio is highly sensitive to the initial stellar mass M$_i$. Therefore, simultaneous measurements of these isotopic ratios can disentangle and place stringent constraints on M$_i$ and T$_{\textrm{max}}$, and the remaining uncertainty is now dominated by stellar abundance measurements rather than nuclear-physics inputs.

papers.title: Dark Energy Survey Year 6 Results: improved mitigation of spatially varying observational systematics with masking for the MagLim++ lens sample
papers.summary: As photometric surveys reach unprecedented statistical precision, systematic uncertainties increasingly dominate large-scale structure probes relying on galaxy number density. Defining the final survey footprint is critical, as it excludes regions affected by artefacts or suboptimal observing conditions. For galaxy clustering, spatially varying observational systematics, such as seeing, are a leading source of bias. Template maps of contaminants are used to derive spatially dependent corrections, but extreme values may fall outside the applicability range of mitigation methods, compromising correction reliability. The complexity and accuracy of systematics modelling depend on footprint conservativeness, with aggressive masking enabling simpler, robust mitigation. We present a unified approach to define the DES Y6 JOINT footprint, integrating observational systematics templates and artefact indicators that degrade mitigation performance. This removes extreme values from an initial SEED footprint, leading to the final JOINT footprint. By evaluating the DES Y6 lens sample MagLim++ on this footprint, we enhance the Iterative Systematics Decontamination (ISD) method, detecting non-linear systematic contamination and improving correction accuracy. While the mask's impact on clustering is less significant than systematics decontamination, it remains non-negligible, comparable to statistical uncertainties in certain w(theta) scales and redshift bins. Supporting coherent analyses of galaxy clustering and cosmic shear, the final footprint spans 4,031.04 deg2, setting the basis for DES Y6 1x2pt, 2x2pt, and 3x2pt analyses. This work highlights how targeted masking strategies optimise the balance between statistical power and systematic control in Stage-III and -IV surveys.

papers.title: Evidence of galaxy cluster rotation and intrahalo gas motions in the cosmic microwave background
papers.summary: We report the first robust evidence for the rotational kinematic Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (rkSZ) effect: the dipolar signal produced by the Thomson scattering of cosmic microwave background (CMB) photons off intracluster gas in dynamically active systems (including rotations and mergers). By combining CMB intensity and polarization measurements from the \emph{Planck} satellite with spectroscopic member-galaxy redshifts from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey in a sample of 25 X-ray cross-matched, low-redshift ($0.02< z< 0.09)$, massive ($10^{13.9}\lesssim M_{\rm 500c}/M_\odot \lesssim 10^{14.6}$) galaxy clusters, we detect a dipolar rkSZ signature aligned with the estimated angular momentum of each cluster, ruling out a chance fluctuation at 99.98\% confidence (3.6$\sigma$). The significance of this measurement is enhanced by several new methodological improvements for isolating the rkSZ signal from primary CMB fluctuations and noise. The amplitude and shape of the signal are qualitatively consistent with predictions from state-of-the-art hydrodynamical simulations. These results establish a new tool with which to probe the dynamical state of galaxy clusters using CMB data.

papers.title: A Very Rich Bimodal Galaxy Cluster Merger: RXC J0032.1+1808
papers.summary: The galaxy cluster RXC J0032.1+1808 has been well-studied with optical imaging and gravitational lensing mass maps, both of which reveal an elongated morphology in the north-south direction. We find that its X-ray morphology is bimodal, suggesting that it is in the process of merging; combined with a previously reported detection of a radio relic, we suggest that the system is seen after first pericenter. We extract the global X-ray temperature and unabsorbed luminosity from archival XMM-Newton data, finding $T_X=8.5^{+1.1}_{-0.9}$ keV and $L_X=1.04 \pm 0.03 \times 10^{45}$ erg s$^{-1}$ at 90% confidence in the 0.5-10 keV energy range. We conduct a redshift survey of member galaxies and find that the line-of-sight relative velocity between the two subclusters is 1002-1785 km/s at 68% confidence, although the BCGs have an even larger difference of 2466 km/s. We use publicly available hydrodynamic simulations to show that it cannot be a head-on merger; it is consistent with an impact parameter of 0.5 or 1 Mpc. We also use the simulation set to find initial constraints on the time since pericenter (${\approx}$315-550 Myr) and the locus of possible lines of sight.

papers.title: Validation of Satellite Lifetime Predictions at Leonid Space
papers.summary: This paper validates Leonid Space's satellite lifetime prediction pipeline through a backtesting campaign of 878 deorbited satellites spanning six decades of spaceflight, showing that it accurately recreates their last year of flight. The pipeline combines a custom high-speed orbit propagator, ballistic coefficient estimation from on-orbit TLE data, atmospheric density corrections from data assimilation, custom space weather forecasts, and probabilistic Monte Carlo analysis. Validation proceeds in four steps that progressively remove the benefit of hindsight: starting from a "perfect knowledge" scenario using actual space weather data and ephemerides, we gradually replace historical data with contemporary predictions to arrive at a fully predictive scenario analogous to a deorbit prediction performed for a spacecraft flying today. These forecasts are scored using the continuously ranked probability score and root mean square calibration error, yielding a median one-year prediction accuracy of 3.9 days (1.1%) with perfect knowledge and 44.9 days (12.3%) in the fully predictive scenario. Solar flux forecasts contribute 89% of the variance in our predictions, dominating all other sources of error. To our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive backtesting of long-term satellite lifetime predictions that reports quantitative results for the fully predictive case, and it establishes a new framework for scoring solar cycle forecasts by grounding forecast accuracy in operationally-relevant satellite lifetime predictions.

papers.title: The stellar-to-halo mass relation of central galaxies across three orders of halo mass
papers.summary: The stellar content of galaxies is tightly connected to the mass and growth of their host dark matter halos. Observational constraints on this relation remain limited, particularly for low-mass groups, leaving uncertainties in how galaxies assemble their stars across halo mass scales. Accurately measuring the brightest central galaxy (BCG) stellar-to-halo mass relation (SHMR) over a wide mass range is therefore crucial for understanding galaxy formation and the role of feedback processes. Here we present the SHMR spanning $M_{\rm halo} \sim 10^{12}$-$10^{15}\,M_\odot$, using halo masses derived from eROSITA eRASS1 X-ray data and BCG stellar masses based on SDSS photometry. By stacking X-ray spectra of optically selected groups, we recover robust average halo gas temperatures for each bin, which are then converted to halo masses via the $M$-$T_X$ relation. We find that the SHMR peaks near $M_{\rm halo} \sim 10^{12}\,M_\odot$, with a declining stellar fraction at higher masses. This trend reflects a combination of processes that reduce the efficiency of stellar mass growth in massive halos, such as AGN feedback, reduced cooling efficiency, and the increasing dominance of ex-situ assembly, while halos continue to grow through mergers and accretion. Our measurements are consistent over the full mass range with previous observational studies, including weak lensing, X-ray analyses of individual clusters, and kinematical and dynamical methods. Comparisons with hydrodynamical simulations show good agreement at low masses but reveal significant discrepancies in the normalization at cluster scales, highlighting the sensitivity of BCG stellar growth to feedback prescriptions and halo assembly history. These results provide the first X-ray-based observational SHMR covering three orders of magnitude in halo mass, establish a robust benchmark for testing galaxy formation models.

papers.title: CHRONOS Science Program
papers.summary: Cryogenic sub-Hz cROss torsion-bar detector with quantum NOn-demolition Speed meter (CHRONOS) is a proposed cryogenic torsion-bar interferometer for precision measurements in the 0.1-10 Hz band. A Sagnac speed-meter readout, power and signal recycling, and balanced homodyne detection provide control of the optical response and quantum measurement correlations. This White Paper describes the science program, detector design, calibration, and staged experimental development. The reference sensitivity uses a multi-input quantum model, including rear-mirror vacuum fields and measurement-back-action correlations, combined with classical noise. Two operating points are optimized for complementary power-law-integrated sensitivity objectives. Gravitational-wave forecasts use this common noise budget and state their source and observing assumptions. The program includes intermediate-mass black-hole binaries, stochastic backgrounds, quantum measurement, and terrestrial gravity perturbations. Dark-matter applications are discussed as response and feasibility studies. A differential gravitational calibrator provides a proposed Yukawa-gravity test whose systematic floor is improved by subtracting auxiliary harmonics. These are conditional projections: experimental reach requires validation of the noise, transfer functions, environmental backgrounds, and systematic uncertainties described here.

papers.title: Probing the magnetic field of a coronal mass ejection with PSR J1022+1001
papers.summary: We investigate whether low-frequency pulsar observations can provide LoS magnetic field estimates and whether these are consistent with synthetic LoS signatures extracted from a three-dimensional CME reconstruction constrained by Solar Orbiter data. We analyze a CME occultation of the LoS to PSR J1022+1001 on 20 August 2021 at a projected heliocentric distance of 24.6 R_sun, observed simultaneously with LOFAR and NenuFAR. From LOFAR, we derive time-resolved dispersion measure (DM) and rotation measure (RM) and isolate the CME contributions using background estimates for interstellar, solar wind and ionospheric components. We then infer the density-weighted LoS-averaged magnetic field component _PSR from the ratio delta-RM/delta-DM. In parallel, we reconstruct the CME using a semi-empirical 3DCORE model fitted to Solar Orbiter in-situ magnetic field observations at 0.65 au. We sample the modeled magnetic field along the pulsar LoS using fixed spatial sampling points and compute synthetic LoS-averaged signatures _3D for different flux rope configurations. The derived _PSR increases from approximately -9 nT to a peak near 63 nT during the observed interval. Comparison with synthetic signatures shows that the polarity and temporal evolution of the LoS signal are strongly dependent on the flux rope configuration and only a South-West-North (SWN) configuration (confirmed by Solar Orbiter in-situ data) reproduces the observed sign and overall evolution, whereas alternative configurations are incompatible. The modeled amplitudes, however, are systematically larger than the pulsar-derived values by roughly a factor of five. We show that simultaneous low-frequency pulsar DM and RM measurements can provide LoS magnetic field estimates for a CME and can be used to test CME magnetic structure against data-constrained three-dimensional reconstructions.

papers.title: Identifying heating processes in simulations with an entropy-based scheme: A single jet episode in a galaxy cluster
papers.summary: Understanding heating processes in galaxy clusters is essential for predicting the regulation of radiative cooling and star formation, and for clarifying the mechanisms underlying active galactic nucleus (AGN) feedback in cool-core clusters. We investigate the processes through which AGN jets deposit heat into the intracluster medium (ICM) by tracking passive entropy scalars in magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) simulations. This enables us to systematically disentangle the contributions from different heating channels. We successfully validate this method with several idealized tests, including turbulent heating, heating by anisotropic Braginskii viscosity, dissipative and adiabatic heating by shocks using in-situ shock-detection methods, and cosmic ray (CR) heating through the excitations and damping of Alfv\'en waves. Using this methodology, we simulate single-epoch outbursts of high-power jets with varying densities in a cluster environment. Light jets produce wider bubbles, displacing a larger fraction of the gas in the cluster's core, whereas comparatively denser jets propagate more efficiently to larger distances without significantly disturbing the central region. During early evolution, shock heating of the ICM prevails irrespective of jet density. At later times, light jets primarily heat the ICM through turbulently induced heating (which includes dissipation of vortices emerging from a turbulent cascade and mixing gas of different temperatures) and compressible dissipation of sound waves and very weak shocks, while denser jets continue to dissipate most of their energy via shocks. Particularly, turbulently induced heating by solenoidal-shear motions prevails inside the cocoon, whereas shocks and acoustic compressions dominate outside. In light jets, the forward shock weakens rapidly, whereas dense jets can sustain strong bow shocks to large distances.

papers.title: Delayed Radio Flares in Neutrino-associated Blazars: The Case of TXS 0506+056
papers.summary: Radio flares have been postulated to be associated with the production of astrophysical neutrinos. For example, TXS 0506+056 exhibits a 2-3 yr delay between the 2017 IceCube-170922A/gamma-ray flare and a GHz radio maximum. We quantitatively test if the delayed radio flare originates from the same compact region where neutrinos and gamma-rays are produced as it expands downstream and synchrotron self-absorption (SSA) is reduced. Starting from the 2017 flare blob parameters, we model the expanding production region and its evolving radio emission with LeHaMoC in a fully time-dependent framework, and compare our 1.2-22 GHz light curves to RATAN-600 data. We study different scenarios with increasing levels of sophistication, including continuous injection and energy re-dissipation on pc scales. While a simple expanding blob scenario fails to reproduce the radio data, a downstream dissipation episode of particles in the optically thin regime, followed by jet deceleration, successfully describes the radio evolution. The radio flare is powered by leptonic synchrotron emission and is largely insensitive to the proton population relevant for neutrino production, implying that the delayed radio flare mainly probes downstream dissipation and beaming in certain jet configurations instead of being a direct radiative counterpart of the compact neutrino-production zone.

papers.title: The DESIRED strong-line calibrations: I. New empirical metallicity relations for the local and high-redshift universe
papers.summary: We present the most comprehensive set of empirical optical strong-line metallicity calibrations to date, based on the DEep Spectra of Ionised REgions Database (DESIRED), the largest compilation of HII regions and galaxies with direct electron-temperature determinations. We construct a high-quality calibration sample of 2392 spectra: 1029 extragalactic HII regions, 1296 local star-forming galaxies, and 67 high-redshift ($z > 2$) galaxies, drawn from 201 independent literature references, spanning $12+\log({\rm O/H}) \in [6.79, 9.07]$. Physical conditions and chemical abundances are derived homogeneously using up-to-date atomic data. We derive 27 strong-line calibrations covering oxygen-, nitrogen-, sulphur-, argon-, and neon-based line ratios, including 4 previously uncalibrated diagnostics, with reported validity ranges and intrinsic dispersions (typically $\sim0.15-0.35$~dex). For the first time in a systematic calibration framework, all relations are presented for both the homogeneous temperature case ($t^2 = 0$) and a scenario including temperature inhomogeneities ($t^2 > 0$), thereby reconciling abundances from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs) and directly tackling the abundance discrepancy problem. A comparison with previous calibrations shows that the DESIRED relations span the broadest validity intervals while remaining anchored to the empirical data. Comparisons with $z>2$ galaxies show that several DESIRED calibrations remain consistent with independent high-redshift relations within their intrinsic scatter, whereas others display systematic offsets associated with elevated N/O or harder ionising conditions. Thus, DESIRED calibrations can provide reliable metallicity estimates at high redshift for a subset of diagnostics, while highlighting the need to account for diagnostic-specific redshift evolution.

papers.title: Probing the 3D Structures of Supernovae through IR Signatures of CO and SiO
papers.summary: We present a new public-domain MOlecular Fitting Analysis Tool (MOFAT) designed to probe molecule-forming regions in supernovae (SNe) through analysis of molecular features in the near- and mid-infrared. MOFAT employs a novel data-driven approach to explore the physical properties of these regions using time-independent radiative transfer simulations that include multidimensional, clump-like structures, constrained by high-precision observations. Such structures are required to reproduce the flux ratio between fundamental and overtone bands, overcoming limitations of traditional one-zone forward-modeling, such as optical-depth effects and initial configurations. Our approach enables spectral fits that can reconstruct overall abundances and temperatures and determine parameterized small-scale structures associated with physical instabilities. We systematically study the relationship between physical parameters and the profiles of CO and SiO, showing that free parameters are constrained, while detection of small-scale structure requires optically thick bands. As a demonstration, MOFAT is applied to SN2024ggi at +285 and +385 days post-explosion. We find that CO formation triggers SiO formation in the inner layers of the CO-rich region previously studied. The inner edge of the SiO-emitting region recedes from velocities of v1 from 1500 to 1000 km/s, indicating continued SiO formation. The SiO mass decreases from about (2-6)E-3 Mo by roughly an order of magnitude, suggesting ongoing evaporation. SiO features indicate clumping, but most of the flux originates from optically thin regions. SiO contributes negligibly to cooling, and we find no evidence for dust formation. Finally, we discuss observational strategies to trace the evolution of molecule formation and its connection to dust formation.

papers.title: Astrophysical Parameters of 5056 Open Star Clusters from Bayesian Nested Sampling with PARSEC Isochrones
papers.summary: We present a homogeneous catalogue of ages, metallicities, distances, and reddenings for 5056 open clusters in the Unified Cluster Catalogue (UCC), derived uniformly from Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3) colour-magnitude diagrams via Bayesian nested sampling with PARSEC isochrones. Unlike previous large-scale catalogues, metallicity is fitted as a free parameter for every cluster rather than fixed or adopted from the literature: where available, Gaia XP spectrophotometric metallicities inform the fit (1201 clusters), while the remaining clusters are constrained by broad priors from Gaia parallaxes and the Schlegel-Finkbeiner-Davis dust map. No cluster is anchored to an external open-cluster parameter catalogue, and no per-cluster manual intervention is applied. A fit-quality metric, $\eta_{\rm fit}$, identifies 3807 clusters (75 per cent) with reliable colour-magnitude solutions, spanning ages of 0.004-5.9 Gyr and distances out to 17 kpc. We validate the resulting parameters against six literature catalogues and, more critically, against independent high-resolution spectroscopic metallicities from OCCAM DR19: for 132 clusters in common we find a median absolute deviation of only 0.054 dex ($-0.021 \pm 0.132$ dex mean offset), comparable to the intrinsic systematic uncertainty of isochrone-based metallicities. As a direct consequence of this fidelity, the radial metallicity gradient recovered from our XP-informed clusters ($-0.064$ dex kpc$^{-1}$) steepens towards the spectroscopically calibrated value ($-0.079$ dex kpc$^{-1}$) for the highest-quality subset - demonstrating that a purely photometric pipeline, built without reference to spectroscopy, recovers a physically meaningful abundance scale. The full catalogue and posterior chains are publicly released.

papers.title: Cosmo-PINN: A Physics-Informed Neural Network for Cosmological Reconstruction
papers.summary: We introduce Cosmo-PINN, a Physics-Informed Neural Network for reconstruction of the cosmological theory. In this work we demonstrate the application of the Cosmo-PINN in the reconstruction of the dark energy equation of state parameter $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ directly from late-time cosmological observations. This framework overcomes the main limitation shared by Gaussian Process and Artificial Neural Network reconstruction approaches, where the recovered solution is driven by the data and it is not necessarily true that it is physically consistent, by embedding the cosmological constraints directly into the loss function as constraints, ensuring that the reconstructed quantities satisfy the physical laws at every point during the training. For the training of the network, we employed background data, and specifically the Baryon Acoustic Oscillation from DESI DR2, the Cosmic Chronometers and three different Supernova compilations, while we simultaneously introduce the cosmological parameters $% H_{0},~\Omega _{m0}$ and $r_{\mathrm{drag}}$ as trained parameters. The reconstruction shows that the trained $w_{DE}\left( z\right) $ crosses the phantom divide around $z=0.5$ in agreement with the value obtained by the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder model. In the quintessence scenario, the dark energy equation of state parameter is forced to the $\Lambda $CDM limit in the past, that is $w_{DE}\left( z\right) \rightarrow -1 $. Finally, we demonstrate the significance of imposing the physical constraints within the loss function by comparing the Cosmo-PINN reconstruction against a purely data-driven neural network with the same architecture.

papers.title: Diocotron Modes in Pulsar Magnetospheres: Charge Diffusion and Implications for Radio Emission Variability
papers.summary: The diocotron instability is a non-axisymmetric plasma instability that should occur generically in the differentially rotating equatorial plane of pulsar magnetospheres. We present a series of 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of the diocotron instability in aligned and oblique pulsars. The instability grows on timescales of the rotation period and develops a strong, stable $m=1$ mode, corresponding to a rotating, dipolar charge asymmetry in the equatorial disk. Stochastic fluctuations in the diocotron mode amplitude and pattern speed drive cross-field diffusion that can rapidly transport charges through the closed zone toward the light cylinder. In the nonlinear stage, the $m=1$ mode produces electric field perturbations which can modulate the polar cap potential drop and the emission beam angle, with possible connections to pulsar variability such as nulling, periodic amplitude modulation, and drifting subpulses.

papers.title: WaveDM.jl: An Adaptable Simulation Framework for Dynamics of Baryonic and Wave Dark Matter on Galaxy Scales
papers.summary: We present WaveDM$.$jl, an open-source Julia package for high-performance simulations of wave dark matter dynamics on galaxy scales, with a design philosophy centered on extensibility and adaptability. The code solves the time-dependent Schr\"odinger--Poisson equation (SPE) using a pseudo-spectral Fourier method. The spectral solver is tightly integrated with N-body gravitational force solvers, enabling simultaneous evolution of wave dark matter and baryonic components in galaxy-scale simulations. WaveDM$.$jl unifies shared-memory, distributed-memory, and GPU execution within a multi-level parallelization framework, enabling the same computational workflow to scale from single-node to multi-node computing environments without requiring major code changes. To further facilitate user-friendly galaxy-scale simulations, the package provides a dedicated toolbox that integrates flexible initial condition generators, trajectory lookback, tidal force calculations, and real-time visualization. Beyond astrophysical applications, the code's modular architecture and general nonlinear Schrodinger framework enable cross-disciplinary studies such as nonlinear optics and cold-atom physics. The code is open source and available on https://github$.$com/JuliaAstroSim/WaveDM$.$jl.

papers.title: Testing the prevalence of hydrogen-silicate miscibility in young sub-Neptunes
papers.summary: Hydrogen-silicate miscibility can significantly alter the interior structure and thermal evolution of sub-Neptunes. We consider the interplay between this miscibility and stellar-driven atmospheric escape. We find that, for the first $\sim 100$ Myr, sub-Neptunes store most of their hydrogen content within their miscible interiors, protecting it from escape. As hydrogen is removed from the top of the atmosphere, more hydrogen is exsolved from the miscible interior, resupplying the envelope mass and delaying the planet's contraction when compared with models that do not account for miscibility. We construct a population-level Bayesian hierarchical inference model which tests for the prevalence of fully miscible sub-Neptunes. With conservative measurement uncertainty and no completeness corrections, we predict that $\sim 100-200$ observed young sub-Neptunes with measured radii, masses and ages $\lesssim 1$ Gyr are required to differentiate between fully miscible and immiscible models. This survey size requirement decreases with improved measurement uncertainty. Furthermore, one can reliably infer the underlying distributions of planetary initial conditions if completeness corrections are included in the analysis.

papers.title: Investigation and Mitigation of a Prominent Off-Axis Stray Light Path in Rubin Observatory Commissioning
papers.summary: The "scratched tape" stray light feature is the most prominent and prevalent stray light artifact identified during the commissioning of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory. This scenario represented an unobstructed stray light path to the sky during Rubin commissioning due to delays in the integration of the dome slit light-wind screen. This document describes the identification, modeling, characterization, and mitigation of the scratched tape stray light artifact.

papers.title: Enhanced Astrometry of the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey: Mid and High Frequency Epochs
papers.summary: Accurate radio astrometry is essential for reliable cross-identification of sources across wavelengths, precision localisation of transient events, and the construction of stable all-sky reference catalogues. In this work we extend our astrometric correction framework for the Rapid ASKAP Continuum Survey (RACS) to its mid- and high-frequency epochs (RACS-Mid1 and RACS-High1), building on our previous corrections to the low-frequency surveys. Using a hierarchical crossmatching strategy with high-precision external catalogues, we remove large-scale systematic positional errors that were present in the uncorrected data and significantly reduce the residual scatter across the sky. After correction, the median positional offsets are effectively eliminated, and the 68\% confidence interval of the mean residuals of RACS source positions averaged over $~\sim1$~sq. deg. regions is reduced from $\gtrsim 0.4''$ to $\lesssim 0.18''$ over most of the survey area for both epochs. Independent validation against multiple external radio astrometric references confirms that individual corrected RACS source positions are accurate to a 1-$\sigma$ confidence level of $\sim 0.25''$ across the bulk of the sky, with slightly degraded performance within the Galactic plane. While motivated primarily by the need for improved localisation of ASKAP fast radio bursts, these corrections also benefit a wide range of science applications, including transient identification, multiwavelength host association, and studies of Galactic and extragalactic radio populations. Together with our previous work, this establishes RACS as the highest precision arcsecond-resolution all-sky astrometric reference in the southern hemisphere at decimetre wavelengths.

papers.title: Volcanic Satellites and Ion Escape in the Magnetospheres of Ultra-Cool and Brown Dwarf Stars
papers.summary: Radio emissions at gigahertz frequencies of ultra-cool dwarf and brown dwarf stars suggest the presence of radiation belts not unlike Jupiter's. We investigate the possibility that the inferred magnetospheric plasma at the primary star is sourced by an active planet or via ion escape modeled as a weak ionospheric outflow. We consider indirect methods to estimate the magnetospheric plasma mass flow from auroral radio emission and apply them to the ultra-cool dwarf LSR J1835+3259. We find that an ionospheric outflow on the order of $10^{5}$ kg s$^{-1}$ is a viable source if the ionospheric effective Pedersen conductance is lower than $\sim 0.003$ mho. On the other hand, a tidally-heated volcanic satellite with the same mass and radius as Io and an orbit with a semimajor axis lower than about $10$ stellar radii, whose eccentricity ($e \sim 10^{-3}$) is maintained by perturbations by other planets in the system, is found to be a viable source of magnetospheric plasma without strong limitations on the ionospheric conductance. The volcanic satellite scenario is also naturally in sync with the recent finding that ultra-cool dwarfs with distant substellar or stellar companions are remarkably more likely to be detected as radio emitters.

papers.title: Physical Characterization of Moon Impactor 2025-010D
papers.summary: Renewed interest in lunar exploration is creating a growing population of poorly tracked cislunar objects, some of which will ultimately impact the Moon$^{1}$. The ultimate fate of rocket upper stages or failed mission payloads is often unknown and unplanned. Determining the origin and physical properties of such objects will become increasingly important as sustained lunar exploration places humans and infrastructure on the surface$^{2;3;4;5}$. Here we present a ground-based physical and dynamical characterization of 2025-010D, a Falcon 9 upper stage predicted to impact the lunar farside on 2026 August 05. Backward propagation of its orbit independently links the object to the ``Ghost Riders in the Sky'' launch, while visible and near-infrared spectroscopy distinguishes it from natural objects and reveals absorption bands consistent with spacecraft thermal control materials. Photometric lightcurves confirm its elongated shape and reveal an unexpected change of more than 8 s in its $\sim$7 min rotation period during observations. We predict an impact between Bell and Einstein craters at $\sim$2.4 km s$^{-1}$, producing a crater $\sim$40 m in diameter. Since its provenance is independently known, 2025-010D provides a benchmark for identifying and characterizing future cislunar objects of uncertain origin.

papers.title: Hyperaccreting Magnetised Neutron Stars inside Rotating Massive Envelopes: Low-Power Jets and Precursor Flares
papers.summary: The engulfment of a neutron star (NS) by a massive companion initiates a highly dynamic common-envelope (CE) evolution phase. As the NS spirals into the dense stellar core, it is subjected to hypercritical accretion rates that threaten to rapidly collapse the NS into a black hole (BH). However, if the infalling envelope possesses sufficient angular momentum and magnetic fields, the NS might survive longer and launch feedback-driving jets. To investigate this, we perform fully coupled, axisymmetric General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations of hyperaccreting NSs, featuring energy-integrated two-moment neutrino transport and a 13-isotope nuclear reaction network. We systematically vary the envelope rotation profile and the magnetic field strength of the NS surface ($B_{\rm surf} \sim 5 \times 10^{10} - 5 \times 10^{13}$~G). In non-magnetised models, we find that envelope rotation naturally forms a centrifugal barrier and a geometrically thick accretion disk, which suppresses the mass accretion rate and lowers the neutrino luminosity; conversely, the intrinsic spin of the NS has a negligible global impact. In magnetised models, the differential rotation of the accretion flow vigorously amplifies the toroidal magnetic field via the $\Omega$-effect, driving the expansion of magnetic towers. Crucially, for strong initial surface magnetic fields ($B_{\rm surf} \gtrsim 2.3 \times 10^{13}$~G), the intense magnetic pressure could completely halt the accretion flow at the NS surface and evacuates a low-density polar funnel. We conclude that while this highly magnetised NS engine successfully delays prompt BH formation and may launch low-power precursor jets (with powers up to ${\sim} 10^{46}~{\rm erg/s}$) capable of generating observable X-ray flares, it lacks the energy budget to unbind the massive envelope, potentially setting the stage for a subsequent BH-driven explosion.

papers.title: Diameters and Temperatures VII: High-angular resolution measurements of Solar-type stars with the CHARA Array
papers.summary: We present interferometric measurements of angular diameters for 27 nearby solar-type stars obtained with the Precision Astronomical Visible Observations (PAVO) beam combiner at the CHARA Array. The sample spans a broad range of metallicities, includes several known exoplanet hosts, and covers evolutionary stages from the zero-age main sequence to mildly evolved subgiants. Uniform-disk and limb-darkened angular diameters were measured for each target and combined with bolometric fluxes and Gaia parallaxes to determine precise, model-independent stellar radii, effective temperatures, and luminosities. We achieve typical uncertainties of $\sim1$\% in radius and $\sim1.5$\% in effective temperature. Comparisons with multiple stellar evolutionary model grids yield mass and age estimates and enable assessment of grid-to-grid systematics, highlighting sensitivities to abundances, evolutionary stage, and proximity to grid boundaries. Our results provide empirical benchmarks for testing stellar evolutionary theory, refining surface brightness-color relations, and improving the characterization of exoplanet host stars.

papers.title: Continuum Variability in AGN: Evidence for Systematically Suppressed Fluctuations in the BAL Population
papers.summary: We aim to compare the flux variability of Broad Absorption Line quasars (BAL) to non-BAL quasars, controlling for black hole parameters to inform models concerning the generation of the BAL phenomenon. Using SDSS DR16 and ZTF $g$- and $r$-band light curves, we select quasars with $1.57 \leq z \leq 2.00$ and $18.5 \leq rmag \leq 19.8$. This redshift range ensures that the $g$-band covers the C IV emission line (and trough in BALs) while the $r$-band probes continuum variability, and allows black hole mass (MBH) estimates via Mg II. We quantify variability using excess variance and damped random walk (DRW) parameters ($\sigma_{\mathrm{DRW}}$, $\tau_{\mathrm{DRW}}$). We also compared the DRW metrics in bins of MBH and Eddington ratio (REdd) to isolate the influence of the BAL phenomenon in objects with the same physical properties. Excess variance and $\sigma_{\mathrm{DRW}}$ are consistently smaller for BALs, confirming lower long-term variability, while the $g$-band exhibits higher variability than the $r$-band across both populations. These differences persist in fixed bins of MBH and REdd, indicating that the suppressed variability in BALs is not simply driven by differences in these properties between BAL and non-BAL samples. These results show that BAL quasars are systematically less variable than non-BAL quasars in both bands, confirming that this suppression is an intrinsic feature of the continuum rather than an effect of emission or absorption line contamination. The samples could be made to agree if BAL MBH values were systematically overestimated by a factor $\gtrsim 4$, implying a significantly higher REdd. Alternatively, the lower variability in BALs can be related to their lower X-ray luminosities, or to significant nuclear obscuration, if the inner part of the accretion disc were more obscured in BALs and more variable than the rest of the disc.

papers.title: Modelling Fourier filtering wavefront sensors for PSD-based methods: the AOPERA tool
papers.summary: Compensation of the atmospheric turbulence thanks to adaptive optics (AO) has now become commonly used for VLT or ELT class telescopes in order to retrieve a resolution close to their diffraction limit. Following the increasing trend of AO system, there is also a stronger necessity for simulations in order to understand and predict their performance facing different observing conditions, that are the evolution of the atmospheric turbulence or the diversity of AO guide source. The so-called PSD based methods are well adapted to the demand thanks to their simplicity and speed. Moreover, they provide a comprehensive breakdown error budget and impact on focal plane, that is of high interest especially in the case of extreme adaptive optics. Their drawback is the challenge to describe non-linear wavefront sensors (WFS) such as the pyramid WFS or the Zernike WFS. There is a necessity to develop fast yet accurate methods to describe the behaviour of AO systems including sensitive WFS. We thus develop a method to compute the AO system response (electromagnetic phase power spectral density, and point spread function) including the non-linear behaviour of the wavefront sensor within PSD-based numerical tools. Mathematical formalism to describe the FF-WFS sensitivity combined to non-linearity management greatly improve the accuracy of description of AO systems through numerical simulations. After a mathematical description of the method, its numerical implementation is compared with end-to-end simulations using the OOPAO tool. Indeed end-to-end simulations are reproducing the response of AO systems with high fidelity, especially regarding WFS sensitivity and non-linearity. Similarity of results for the fitting error, temporal error and noise error proves the validity of our method in managing Fourier filtering WFS sensitivity and non-linearity.

papers.title: Field-Level Baryon Acoustic Oscillation Reconstruction of the DESI DR1 Luminous Red Galaxies with Linear Field Transformer (LiFT)
papers.summary: We present the first application of neural field-level baryon-acoustic oscillation (BAO) reconstruction to real spectroscopic survey data. We develop Linear Field Transformer (LiFT), a 3D vision transformer that takes as input the observed galaxy field, its standard reconstruction, and a set of context channels encoding local line of sight, survey coverage, and redshift, and learns to correct standard reconstruction toward the linear density field. We construct a forward-modeling pipeline to produce mock lightcones similar to the DESI Data Release 1 (DR1) luminous red galaxy (LRG) sample, and train LiFT on these. We validate LiFT on held-out simulations, as well as on additional mocks which differ in gravity solver, halo finder, HOD, cosmology, and fiber-assignment history, as well as on mocks analyzed with a distorted distance-redshift relation; ultimately, we find unbiased dilation parameters with consistently tighter constraints than standard reconstruction. Applied to the DESI DR1 LRGs, LiFT improves errors on $\alpha_{\rm iso}$ by 13%, 24%, and 30% and on $\alpha_{\rm AP}$ by 5%, 22%, and 30% relative to the DESI DR1 standard reconstruction analysis in the LRG1, LRG2, and LRG3 bins respectively; meanwhile, our DR1 central values remain consistent with DR1 and DR2. This equates to a factor of 1.2, 1.7 and 2.0 increase in Figure of Merit (or effective survey volume) if one were to only use standard reconstruction. Ultimately, these results establish LiFT as a validated, survey-ready tool for current and upcoming galaxy surveys.

papers.title: The Study of Detailed Morphology of Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: Draco and Bo\"otes I
papers.summary: We present a photometric study of the outer stellar structures of the Milky Way dwarf spheroidal galaxies (dSphs) Draco and Bo\"otes I, using deep wide-field imaging data. The old main-sequence stars are used to trace their spatial distributions beyond their tidal radii. We derive global structural parameters and radial profiles of number density, ellipticity, and position angle from their stellar distributions. Draco and Bo\"otes I show contrasting features. Draco shows no prominent extended stellar distribution, although weak elongations are detected toward the eastern and northwestern directions. Its stellar distribution remains relatively compact compared with its estimated Jacobi tidal radius ($r_J=57.2^{+13.5}_{-11.1}$ arcmin), suggesting that the stellar component is tightly bound by its gravitational potential. In contrast, the radial number-density profiles of Bo\"otes I along several directions show excess from the best-fit exponential profile outside of around $r\sim20$ arcmin, near the estimated Jacobi radius ($r_J=21.6^{+9.3}_{-7.6}$ arcmin). In addition, the ellipticity of Draco decreases with radius, whereas that of Bo\"otes I increases toward larger radii. Bo"otes I also exhibits a prominent S-shaped stellar structure extending approximately along its orbital direction. Together, the radial density excess, increasing ellipticity, and S-shaped morphology suggest that the outer stellar structure of Bo\"otes I may trace tidal tails produced by interactions with the Milky Way. The contrasting morphologies of Draco and Bo\"otes I further suggest that the response of dwarf galaxies to the Milky Way tidal field may depend not only on their orbital histories, but also on the internal structure of their dark-matter halos.

papers.title: Evolving dark energy and a younger Universe from cosmic inhomogeneity
papers.summary: Joint analyses of baryon acoustic oscillations, type Ia supernovae and the cosmic microwave background show a preference for an evolving dark-energy equation of state, and recent studies suggest that cosmic inhomogeneities can produce an apparent evolution of dark energy within general relativity. Here we examine this effect within a framework in which the possibility that matter can be unevenly distributed enters the expansion dynamics directly. The framework yields redshift-dependent effective values of the Hubble constant and of the dark-energy density parameter without introducing a new free parameter. Using CMB-inferred parameters to fix the homogeneous limit, we find that the dark-energy density parameter increases by about eight percent toward the present, from 0.679 to 0.735, while the inferred Hubble constant shifts from the Planck value toward the range obtained from local measurements. Both trends are broadly consistent with published estimates from supernovae, baryon acoustic oscillations, X-ray clusters and gravitational waves, although a joint analysis of the underlying data is left for future work. Integrating the resulting expansion history gives a present-day cosmic age of 13.521 Gyr, compared with 13.827 Gyr for the homogeneous model; we interpret the difference of 0.306 Gyr as a global time dilation between the two descriptions. The framework also yields the homogeneous-limit dark-energy density parameter, two thirds, from the formation of volume alone. The predicted redshift dependences can be tested against forthcoming measurements of cosmic distances and expansion rates.

papers.title: A forest of emission lines observed by Sunrise III/SUSI above the solar limb
papers.summary: We present off-limb spectroscopy using low-straylight data from the Sunrise Spectropolarimeter and Imager (SUSI) onboard the Sunrise III stratospheric solar observatory. We detected a total of 174 spectral lines in emission off-limb, a 2.5-fold increase over previous reports. Surprisingly, 122 of these lines begin to appear in emission already on the disc, although close to the limb. In addition, one-fifth of relatively prominent emission lines are due to rare-earth and heavy elements and molecules, where the absorption lines of these transitions are typically weak on-disc.

papers.title: Rotational excitation of SiC$_6$ by collisions with helium: cross sections, rate coefficients and non-LTE modeling
papers.summary: Rotational transitions of SiC$_6$ in the $j=26$--$40$ range have been detected in IRC+10216, yet collisional rate coefficients for SiC$_6$ with He or H$_2$ were previously unavailable. This paper reports rate coefficients for rotational excitation of SiC$_6$ induced by collisions with He, calculated using a two-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) constructed at the RCCSD(T)-F12 level under the rigid-rotor approximation. The close-coupling (CC) method was employed for low rotational energy levels, while the coupled-states (CS) approximation was used for higher rotational levels. Systematic convergence tests were conducted, and the resulting CC and CS scattering cross sections were compared. The rate coefficients obtained via the CS method cover rotational levels up to $j=40$ and temperatures of 3--100\,K. Although the CC and CS rate coefficients differ by up to a factor of $\sim 2$ for some transitions, particularly those influenced by weak coupling and resonances, the two methods yield nearly identical excitation and brightness temperatures for the high-$j$ transitions (e.g., $19\rightarrow18$) examined, and the CS-based line fluxes agree with the CC-based results to within 6.5\% for $n(\mathrm{H_2}) \ge 10^{3}$\,cm$^{-3}$; this demonstrates that the CS approximation is reliable for the non-LTE modelling of high-$j$ SiC$_6$ transitions considered here, for which fully converged CC calculations are computationally impractical. Using the calculated SiC$_6$--He rate coefficients and reduced-mass scaling to estimate the corresponding SiC$_6$--H$_2$ rates, we further investigate the excitation of the observed high-$j$ transitions. Under typical low-density conditions in IRC+10216 ($n(\mathrm{H_2}) \approx 10^4$\,cm$^{-3}$), the $j=40\to39$ transition is subthermally excited, highlighting the importance of non-LTE effects when interpreting the emission of high-$j$ SiC$_6$ transitions.

papers.title: Axial-Dipole and Equatorial-Dipole Coronal Holes: Congruent Magnetic Geometry, Divergent Evolution
papers.summary: While the Sun's polar fields reverse, the axial dipole is weak and low-latitude coronal holes are common. Equatorial-dipole coronal holes (EDCHs) appear when the equatorial dipole is strong, forming at its magnetic poles, similar to the axial-dipole coronal holes (ADCHs) of minimum. Not every low-latitude hole qualifies: the 2024 maximum was quadrupole-led. Parker Solar Probe found fast wind from an EDCH deeply sub-Alfv\'enic at $9.9\,R_\odot$, at only $60\%$ of an asymptotic speed matching polar wind, which is usually thought to accelerate faster. We ask whether coronal structure predicts this, using potential-field models of synthetic and observed fields at three cycle phases. We show that pure axial and equatorial dipoles are exactly congruent, with the same open areas and core expansion factors, so any difference must arise from orientation relative to the differential-rotation pattern or from the surrounding multipoles. We find that ADCHs are stationary, sustained by converging meridional flow, whereas EDCHs depend on an equatorial dipole that active-region emergence builds and flux transport dismantles: over $18$-day sequences the axial-dipole strength at minimum is steady to $1\%$, while the equatorial dipole varies by $21\%$ at maximum and $8\%$ in the declining phase. Most open flux in EDCHs expands less than in ADCHs, but their boundaries are pseudostreamer-dominated, with non-monotonic expansion. Despite these differences, magnetic geometry alone does not predict slower acceleration in EDCHs; we argue that any real difference points to extended heating by reflection-driven Alfv\'en-wave turbulence, perhaps fed differently at those boundaries, which potential-field models cannot capture.

papers.title: How much can shape degeneracies affect the Hubble constant measurement?
papers.summary: Cluster lens models are constrained almost entirely by observed lensed image positions, leaving a large space of mass perturbations with arbitrary amplitudes such that they reproduce every image exactly. Such degeneracies are known as shape degeneracies (ShaDes). We show that these ShaDes shift the observed time delays, by the difference of the perturbing potential between the two images, without depending on the number of source/lens planes. Bounding their amplitude by preserving the positivity of the convergence, image multiplicity, and parity, in MACS J0138.0$-$2155, they can contribute at least $\simeq7$ days to the delay between the detected images of SN-Encore (i.e., $17.5\%$ of the measured value of $39.8$ days) and $\simeq112$ days (i.e., $2.8$--$3.7\%$ of predicted value of $3,000-4000$ days) to the reappearance intervals predicted for SN-Encore and SN-Requiem. These error bars transfer one-to-one to $H_0$, and remain invisible in comparisons of independent models.

papers.title: Scaling Up: A Global Optical/X-ray Correlation For Reprocessing Across Black Hole Masses
papers.summary: This study extends the optical/X-ray correlation from black hole low-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) to active galactic nuclei (AGN), bridging scales from stellar-mass to supermassive black holes (SMBHs). In XRBs, optical emission predominantly originates from the thermal reprocessing of high-energy photons on the surface of the geometrically thin, optically thick accretion disk. The reprocessed optical luminosity follows a power-law relation of the form $L_{V} \propto L_{X}^{\beta} a$, with $\beta \sim 0.5$, where $L_X$ is the X-ray luminosity and the orbital separation $a$ serves as a proxy for the disk size. To test the universality of this relationship across all mass scales, we analyzed quasi-simultaneous X-ray and optical flux data from a sample of XRBs and AGN that have estimates of the radius of the optically emitting disk. To bridge the structural differences between these populations, we utilized the characteristic optical/X-ray time lag derived from reverberation mapping as a physical proxy for the reprocessing radius. Our analysis reveals a tight, global correlation across all black hole masses, described by $\log L_V = 0.48\log L_X + 0.96\log a_R + 6.5$ with a scatter of $\sim 0.20$ dex, where $a_R$ is the reprocessing radius derived from the lag. Incorporating a geometric correction for the disk inclination angle ($\cos i$) slightly reduces this scatter to $0.18$ dex. These results suggest that X-ray reprocessing is scale-invariant across accretion disks, from stellar-mass black holes to SMBHs. This scaling relation provides new constraints for models of X-ray emission regions in accreting black holes.

papers.title: 3D Global Climate Simulations of Synthetic Mars Warming
papers.summary: Artificial warming via engineered aerosols presents a novel pathway to bypass volatile scarcity on modern Mars. Utilizing the Generic Planetary Climate Model, we evaluate the physical feasibility of aerosol-induced terraforming over a full Martian year (669 Sols). Unlike previous approaches that added aerosols to background dust or assumed continuous nanoparticle injection, we simulate the complete substitution of natural dust with a single-injection profile of radiatively active aluminium nanoparticles without continuous dumping. This tests whether initial infrared greenhouse forcing can overcome the severe ice-albedo cooling induced by a massive regional water-ice sheet ($3400 \text{ kg/m}^2$) localized in the Hellas Basin. Comparing this scenario against an unperturbed control run, we analyze surface temperature dynamics, sublimation fluxes, and water vapour concentration. Our 3D global climate simulations quantify the radiative-dynamical feedback thresholds and determine whether engineered aerosol forcing can trigger a self-sustaining water-vapour greenhouse effect or remains fundamentally limited by regional ice-albedo suppression in Hellas.
