papers.title: Pinning of a High-Energy Wavepacket by a Single Impurity
papers.summary: We demonstrate that a single repulsive impurity enhances directional confinement of a high-energy wavepacket in a finite two-dimensional lattice of quantum wells. At energies far above the interwell barriers, the impurity suppresses transverse dynamical tunneling while preserving propagation along a principal lattice axis, even as the corresponding classical regular region shrinks. Confinement is strongest at impurity amplitudes comparable to the barrier height and weakens for stronger perturbations. Spectral analysis links this nonmonotonic pinning to the wavepacket's overlap with eigenstates concentrated along the launch direction, consistent with impurity-induced variational scarring. These results show that a single local defect can control quantum propagation over distances far exceeding its own spatial extent.

papers.title: Exact analytical spectra of an effective field-modified radial Schr\"odinger equation by the Nikiforov--Uvarov method
papers.summary: We revisit the effective radial Schr\"odinger equation for a charged spinless particle in collinear static electric and magnetic fields that was formulated in our earlier work within the tridiagonal representation approach (TRA). In that model the angular factor of the electric coupling is replaced by the orientation parameter $C=\cos\theta$, the linear Zeeman term is diagonal in the azimuthal quantum number, and the effective field-modified central potential takes the form $V(r)=\Vt(r)+qECr$. Here we show that the same equation can be solved exactly without the TRA, by the Nikiforov--Uvarov (NU) method, once the potential component $\Vt(r)$ is prescribed. Three examples are worked out in closed form: a Kratzer-type component, which yields a linear-plus-Coulomb-plus-inverse-square central potential; a pseudoharmonic-type component, which yields a linear-plus-harmonic-plus-inverse-square potential; and a Hulth\'en-type component with a repulsive core (Manning--Rosen form), which yields a screened confining potential with a finite number of $s$-wave bound states. For each case we obtain the energy spectrum, the normalized eigenfunctions in terms of Laguerre or Jacobi polynomials, the location of the potential minimum, and closed-form radial moments. The spectra are independent of the orientation $\theta$ and of the electric field, in agreement with the structure found by the TRA, while the field enters through the shape of $V(r)$, the radial moments, and the expectation value $\langle V\rangle_k$. All analytical results are confirmed by an independent finite-difference diagonalization.

papers.title: Geometric-resource bounds and permutation-averaged success probabilities for the WZP algorithm
papers.summary: Solving linear systems of equations is a fundamental task in machine learning and optimization. In this work, we extend the original WZP algorithm from real symmetric linear systems to complex Hermitian linear systems. We then study the success probability of the modified WZP algorithm from a resource-theoretic perspective. By expressing the postselection success probability as the expectation value of a positive operator, we derive upper and lower bounds of the maximal success probability over separable, incoherent, and real pure states. These bounds further establish connections between the maximal success probability and geometric entanglement, coherence, and imaginarity. We further show that, under permutation averaging, the averaged success probability is an affine function of the coherence fraction, with its dependence determined by the alignment between the success operator and the equal-superposition state. We also investigate the preprocessed WZP algorithm under subgroup-constrained preprocessing. For the two-level family, the optimal success probability is determined by the maximal projection weight onto the orbit of the target projector. Our results provide a unified perspective on the WZP success probability under different operational constraints.

papers.title: A hybrid quantum interferometer bridging Hong-Ou-Mandel and N00N-state interference
papers.summary: Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference offers robustness in high-noise environments due to its phase-insensitive nature, while N00N-state interference provides enhanced phase sensitivity for precision measurements in low-noise settings. This tunability enables operation in phase-insensitive, phase-sensitive, or hybrid modes within a unified setup, as confirmed by theoretical analysis and experimental demonstration. Our system offers a versatile platform with potential for quantum sensing applications, paving the way for integrated quantum technologies capable of adapting to diverse noise conditions.

papers.title: Gaussian and Qubit Semigroup Dynamics beyond GKSL
papers.summary: A well established approach to describe open quantum system dynamics is the celebrated Gorini-Kossakowski-Sudarshan-Lindblad (GKSL) master equation. In this article we aim to shed light on semigroup dynamics that are not of this form. Such dynamics may appear in real physical systems describing asymptotic long-time dynamics. Thus, they correspond to semigroup dynamics applicable to a restricted set of initial states only. As a way of motivating our studies, first we review known results about the single-mode Gaussian Quantum Brownian motion channel and corresponding master equations. Next we discuss a conceptually simpler family of qubit semigroup generators and identify parameter regions of completely positive, merely positive, and non-positive dynamics. We then focus on the latter case to which we will refer to as restricted-positive, as the semigroup generator may well be physically meaningful when applied to a restricted set of admissible initial states.

papers.title: Petz Recovery through a Single Polar Transformation for Approximate Quantum Error Correction
papers.summary: The Petz recovery map provides a near optimal decoder for approximate quantum error correction, but its inverse square-root normalization complicates circuit implementation. We use the polar structure of the Petz recovery isometry to implement recovery through a single quantum singular value transformation (QSVT). We give explicit block-encoding circuits and an extended recovery isometry that yields approximate Petz recovery without postselection. We bound the diamond distance between the approximate and ideal Petz encoding-recovery channels in terms of a spectrum-weighted loss, which provides a channel specific objective for optimizing the QSVT angles. Uniform polynomial approximation yields an asymptotic error bound that decays exponentially with the number of QSVT iterations, at a rate controlled by the smallest nonzero scaled singular value. Applications to Haar-random encoding and the Hayden-Preskill protocol illustrate the tradeoff between circuit depth and recovery accuracy and place existing scrambling decoders within a common Petz recovery framework.

papers.title: Quantum Work Statistics from Entanglement-Assisted Invariance

This envariance-based formulation eliminates the ambiguity in work statistics related to the energetic cost of measurement.

papers.title: Intermediate memory costs of quantum channel synthesis with a protected subsystem
papers.summary: A quantum memory can preserve a subsystem perfectly while discarding information needed by a later operation. We study the total intermediate dimension required for channel synthesis when the first stage protects a $b$-dimensional subsystem and has a prescribed noncommutative graph imposing full confusability on an $a$-dimensional control register. For a finite family of classically controlled branches, exact synthesis is possible if and only if the target graph contains the prescribed graph of the first stage. For every feasible family, we construct a single processor that implements all branches exactly. The processor uses pairwise nonorthogonal pure program states in a register of dimension at most $a$. A target graph may be realizable with a carrier of dimension $b$, while synthesizing a channel with that graph can require dimension $ab$. We also characterize the closure of the attainable channels, distinguishing exact synthesis from arbitrarily accurate approximation. Finally, for a family built from the trine communication task, a four-dimensional carrier permits exact synthesis with quantum programs under output depolarization. At the same total carrier dimension and without free shared randomness, classical programs have optimal normalized diamond error $(1-\eta)/4$, where $0\leq\eta\leq1$ is the depolarization strength. For $\eta<1$, the gap persists under sufficiently small perturbations of the target branches.

papers.title: Quantum-Aware Key Rank for Side-Channel Attacks evaluation
papers.summary: Side-channel attacks on block ciphers rarely recover the key outright: they leave a residual key space ordered by subkey posteriors, and evaluation laboratories report the key rank of the true key against thresholds near 2^48 and 2^60. No evaluation framework models an adversary who collects traces classically and finishes the search on a quantum computer, although quantum search with advice provides exactly that. We give such an adversary a cost model and a metric. For a device whose key has rank r, any quantum algorithm with classical access to the posteriors needs Omega(sqrt(r)) cipher evaluations, and block search achieves O(sqrt(r)); the per-instance advantage is exactly quadratic, and the super-quadratic exponents reported for search with advice are averages over the prior that apply to no single device. Under the NIST MAXDEPTH budget D and a Grover iteration of g gates and depth d, the quadratic advantage holds only for ranks up to (4D/(pi d))^2 and collapses to a constant factor beyond; with the best published AES-128 oracle and D = 2^40 the window closes near rank 2^58.6. We define the quantum-aware key rank, the classical rank of equal cost, computable from the rank estimators laboratories already run, and derive the classical rank a device must retain to keep a given threshold against each depth budget. Block search and amplitude amplification from the product-form posterior state are within a factor of two to four of each other on Hamming-weight posteriors, so the cost of coherent indexing decides between them. Experiments on simulated leakage and a toy cipher confirm the predicted window: at SNR 0.125 a depth-limited quantum adversary is worth about 22 traces to a classical one, however large its gate budget.

papers.title: Logical CCZ state cultivation
papers.summary: Logical CCZ states enable Toffoli gates, a central building block of fault-tolerant quantum arithmetic. We introduce an end-to-end protocol for direct CCZ-state preparation on bivariate tricycle and bicycle (BT/BB) codes. Our factory combines the cup-product CCZ gates native to BT codes with two novel ingredients, both enabled by engineering the logical coupling between BT and BB codes through projection-preserving lifts. Index-2 lifted BB ancillas enable selective $Z$-basis initialization, allowing the native cup-product gates to directly prepare two disjoint logical CCZ states. The prepared CCZ states are faithfully transferred to index-3 lifted BB memories with high code distance. We use decoder-based postselection to obtain high-fidelity output states with low overhead. We perform exact simulations of our factory under a circuit-level noise model motivated by neutral-atom hardware, obtaining joint infidelities of $1.84\times10^{-5}$ at $21.94\%$ acceptance and $4.10\times10^{-7}$ at $8.89\%$ acceptance for single-qubit, CZ, and CCZ error rates of $0.01\%$, $0.1\%$, and $0.5\%$, respectively. At the output-infidelity target of our smallest factory, its estimated spacetime cost per CCZ state is lower than that of $T$-state cultivation followed by CCZ conversion, providing an efficient route to logical CCZ states for fault-tolerant quantum computation.

papers.title: Semiclassical state on algebra of observables for de Sitter space and time reversal symmetry
papers.summary: In de Sitter static patch holography, coupling bulk quantum fields to an observer's dynamical clock yields a type II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}_+$ of gauge-invariant observables. However, the unique tracial state on this algebra fails to reproduce semiclassical bulk correlation functions. We resolve this issue by introducing a family of heavy-clock states, representing an observer reference frame with heavy inertia. We prove that in the heavy-clock limit, $n$-point correlation functions of gauge-invariant dressed observables reproduce the bulk quantum field correlation functions on de Sitter spacetime. Furthermore, we investigate a generalized observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehat{\pi}|$ that incorporates both forward-running ($\pi\geq 0$) and backward-running ($\pi <0$) clocks. The resulting von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$ of gauge-invariant observables remains a type~II$_1$ factor and is isomorphic to $\mathcal{M}_+\otimes M_2(\mathbb{C})$, where $M_2(\mathbb{C})$ is the algebra of $2\times2$ complex matrices transforming between the two clock orientations. Time-reversal symmetry is implemented in this setting as an anti-unitary operator that exchanges the two clock orientations, yielding a type~II$_1$ von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{F}$ of gauge-invariant, time-reversal-invariant observables. We generalize the heavy-clock state construction to both $\mathcal{M}$ and $\mathcal{F}$, showing that $n$-point correlation functions calculated in heavy-clock states match the corresponding semiclassical bulk correlation functions. Finally, by coupling Einstein gravity to the Brown--Kucha\v{r} dust field, we derive the observer Hamiltonian $\widehat{H}_{\rm obs}=|\widehat{\pi}|$ from a perturbative reduction along the observer's worldline in the $G \to 0$ limit. This provides a field-theoretic foundation for the observer model developed in this work.

papers.title: Stabilizer entropy cones as self-dual slices of linear rank cones: a five-party gap and dependence on the local dimension
papers.summary: Entanglement entropies of multipartite pure states satisfy linear inequalities; for stabilizer states, the backbone of quantum error correction, the achievable entropy vectors generate a convex cone. We show that, after a linear lift, the closure of this cone is exactly the self-dual slice of a classical object on one more element than there are parties: the closed cone generated by the rank functions of arrangements of subspaces over $\mathrm{GF}(d)$ for a prime local dimension $d$, and of subgroups of abelian groups of exponent dividing $d$ in general. This correspondence brings two features of rank inequalities into play. First, the purifier acts as an extra variable: already for five parties the stabilizer cone is strictly smaller than the quantum linear rank cone, with which earlier evidence suggested it might coincide; an explicit six-variable inequality witnesses the gap. Second, the characteristic of the field enters, so the cone depends on the local dimension. It does not for up to four parties. With enough parties, the cone of $\mathbb{Z}_d$ qudits is contained in that of $\mathbb{Z}_{d'}$ qudits if and only if $d$ divides $d'$, and already for six parties the logical zero state of Steane's code lies outside the stabilizer cone of every odd local dimension. For this last result we show that the seven-variable characteristic-dependent inequalities we checked all follow from Shannon inequalities on the self-dual slice, and instead transfer one of them through a family of subgroups derived from the Fano plane.

papers.title: Measurement-induced criticality for non-Abelian anyons: The monitored golden chain
papers.summary: Non-Abelian anyon chains whose interactions favor a single fusion channel host quantum critical ground states described by minimal-model conformal field theories (CFTs) protected by a topological symmetry. We show that their measurement-only counterpart, where non-commuting fusion charge measurements act locally on the anyons of a chain of $L$ sites, provides a fundamental example of a non-unitary CFT controlling a non-Abelian learning problem. Mapping the monitored dynamics to a random tensor network, we numerically find $1/L$ scaling Lyapunov gaps, logarithmic entanglement scaling with the chord length, and an effective central charge in the Shannon entropy of the measurement record. The conserved topological charge sharpens with dynamical exponent $z= 1$ and is learnable by a decoder on an $O(L)$ time scale. As the topological symmetry is a non-invertible symmetry of the $SU(2)_k$ anyon theories, we establish the monitored golden chain $(k=3)$ as a non-Abelian generalization of the weakly (Kramers-Wannier) self-dual quantum critical point of the toric code $(k=2)$, and the first of a family for $k\geq 3$.

papers.title: Viscous hydrodynamics from correlated losses
papers.summary: Interactions turn a gas into a fluid. We show that two-body loss can take their place. Correlated loss induces elastic scattering, as required by the optical theorem, which dominates at strong loss via the quantum Zeno effect. A nondegenerate gas with only two-body loss thus flows hydrodynamically, with viscosity and thermal conductivity close to those of the unitary Fermi gas. As loss heats the gas, both grow in time with a universal exponent 3/8. Unlike single-particle loss, two-body loss can engineer collisions, and hence transport, in quantum matter.

papers.title: Beyond the lemon: Spectra of random Lindblad operators with a Hamiltonian component
papers.summary: Generators of continuous-time quantum Markovian evolution, known as Lindblad operators, play a key role in the theory of open quantum systems. The question of how to define and characterize random Lindblad operators has attracted considerable attention in recent years. Purely dissipative random Lindbladians have been extensively studied using toolboxes of free probability and non-Hermitian random matrix theories, which helped, among other results, to uncover a characteristic lemon-like spectral support. In this work, we focus on random Lindbladians with a Hamiltonian component. We analyze three ensembles of increasing complexity, designed to illustrate the joint effects of dissipative and Hamiltonian dynamics. While the first two ensembles allow for an exact analytic treatment with standard probabilistic and free-probability methods, the generic case of independently random Hamiltonian and dissipative components requires a novel framework that combines operator-valued free probability with sequential noise averaging. For this ensemble, our approach preserves the underlying tensor-product structure of the Lindblad operator and derives a general equation for the spectral boundary. We characterize the effect of Hamiltonian-induced spectral squeezing and explain how the spectral support changes with the relative Hamiltonian strength and the rank of the dissipative component.

papers.title: A note on the A.C. spectrum of limit-periodic Jacobi matrices

papers.title: Coherent-State Integrals Beyond the Domain of Operator Products
papers.summary: Inserting a resolution of the identity between two operators turns a matrix element of their product into a phase-space integral. For unbounded operators the product need not exist on the vector at hand, while the integral may still converge. We follow this gap through the chain $e^{\mu a^2}e^{\lambda a^{\dagger2}}$ of two-photon exponentials, where it can be traced completely. Five regions of parameter space appear: where the Bochner conditions of the strong formulation hold, where the product exists as a vector, where it exists as a sesquilinear form, where the coherent-state integral converges, and where the Fock-space series converges. The first three are strictly nested inside the intersection of the last two, and these two overlap without either containing the other. A single Hermite-type function agrees with the matrix element where it exists and with the integral and the series wherever they converge, so the integral carries the analytic continuation of the matrix element beyond the domain of the product and beyond the convergence of its Fock series. On the real slice of parameter space, an iterated form of the integral also reaches every point where the series converges. The analysis rests on a weak composition lemma whose hypotheses concern only the bra, the ket and the resolving family. For bounded chains the same identity is unconditional, and worked examples of that kind are given in a companion paper.

papers.title: Observation of correlations beyond the single-particle picture in fermionic counting statistics
papers.summary: The analysis of charge fluctuations in a mesoscopic device can shed light on the fundamental question of whether or not a single-particle picture of electron transport is appropriate, even in the presence of Coulomb interaction. It has been shown on general grounds that mapping the interacting system onto a fermionic single-particle description is subject to strict constraints on the charge-transfer statistics. These constraints can be formulated in terms of a sign rule for the factorial cumulants of the full counting statistics. We report here on the experimental observation of a sign-rule violation in a most elementary model system, i.e. a single-level quantum dot, and provide theoretical modeling that can quantitatively reproduce the experimental data. This reveals the presence of correlations introduced by electron-electron interaction.

papers.title: Dicke model of open-shell atoms with tensor polarizability
papers.summary: We study the extended Dicke model obtained from the scalar--vector--tensor polarizability of open-shell atoms coupled to a shared cavity mode. For a single electric-dipole channel, rotational symmetry fixes the tensor to vector ratio; we use $^{168}\mathrm{Er}$ with $J=6$ as a product-state example. A circular pump produces a chiral Raman vertex whose tensor-dependent matrix elements select the occupied Zeeman sector. The resulting first-order transition occurs before the empty-cavity branch loses local stability, and the ordered state is read out through $\langle\hat J_z\rangle$. A linear pump instead produces an empty-cavity $\pm x$ cat and a continuous transition into an even-$m$ cat-like state with order parameter $\langle\hat J_z^2\rangle$. With cavity loss alone, the circular trajectory emits a photon burst and approaches a Raman-dark Zeeman pole rather than a finite-field condensate. In the linear geometry, cavity-bright modes are damped toward the cat-like branch while a dark spin mode remains undamped. These are phenomena of that model; the vector-only controls show that they depend on the channel-fixed tensor coupling.

papers.title: Directional effects of the Unruh effect on steering harvesting
papers.summary: We investigate directional quantum steering harvesting by two uniformly accelerated non-identical Unruh-DeWitt detectors coupled to a massless scalar field in the Minkowski vacuum. We show that the Unruh effect does not simply degrade harvested steering, but can reshape its directionality in a strongly parameter-dependent manner. At low detector energy scales, acceleration predominantly suppresses steering, whereas at higher energy scales, moderate acceleration can enhance steering and even activate an initially absent steering direction. Most strikingly, within a finite acceleration window, the Unruh effect enhances steering in one direction while simultaneously suppressing it in the opposite direction, revealing an intrinsically directional influence of relativistic acceleration. Detector non-identicality provides an additional control mechanism: a moderate energy-gap mismatch can enhance or activate one steering direction while suppressing the reverse one, whereas sufficiently large energy-gap mismatch suppresses the harvested steering. Moreover, the maximal steering asymmetry approximately marks the transition from two-way to one-way steering. Our results establish relativistic acceleration and detector non-identicality as means of controlling the strength and directionality of vacuum-harvested quantum correlations.

papers.title: All you need is Trotter
papers.summary: The work here enables a cost scaling of $\tilde{O}\left( \frac{T ^{1+o(1)}\,{\rm log}^2 (1/\epsilon)}{\varepsilon}\right)$ and maximum depth $\tilde{O}\left( \frac{T^{1+o(1)}\,{\rm log} (1/\epsilon)}{\varepsilon}\right)$ for estimating observables after some Hamiltonian evolution $e^{i H T}$ using no extra block-encoding qubits, where $\epsilon$ is the algorithmic error of the target Hamiltonian evolution and $\varepsilon$ is the statistical error from the observable estimation. Throughout, $\tilde{O}$ suppresses factors that are doubly logarithmic in $1/\epsilon$ (i.e. ${\rm polyloglog}(1/\epsilon)$), which are subdominant to the displayed ${\rm polylog}(1/\epsilon)$ factors. This is achieved through product formulas, stable interpolation (Chebyshev), and to calculate the needed fractional queries, cardinal sine interpolation is used. This is an improvement over similar work using interpolation methods which have a superlinear scaling of the form $5^p T^{1+1/p}$, where $p$ is the order of the product formula used and an improvement on required qubits over Quantum Signal Processing methods while maintaining scaling with ${\rm polylog}{1/\epsilon}$. This is accomplished through an optimized and variable (with $T$) order $p$. The slightly better $\log^2(1/\epsilon)$ compared to $\log^3(1/\epsilon)$ comes from the use of cardinal sine interpolation compared to other methods using Chebyshev interpolation and product formulas. The work presented here also provides an alternative to Quantum Signal Processing techniques to calculate observables or amplitudes after a fractional query evolution with a cost $O(T\log{1/\epsilon})$ through this cardinal sine interpolation.

papers.title: A quantum annealing approach to the minimum distance problem of quantum codes
papers.summary: Quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs) are at the heart of fault-tolerant quantum computing. As the size of quantum platforms is expected to grow, one of the open questions is to design new optimal codes of ever-increasing size. A related challenge is to certify the quality of a given code by evaluating its minimum distance, a quantity characterizing code's capacity to preserve quantum information. This problem is known to be NP-hard. Here we propose to harness the power of contemporary quantum platforms to address this question, and in this way help design quantum platforms of the future. Namely, we introduce an approach to compute the minimum distance of quantum stabilizer codes by reformulating the problem as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem and leveraging established QUBO algorithms and heuristics as well as quantum annealing (QA) to address the latter. The reformulation as a QUBO introduces only a logarithmic multiplicative overhead in the required number of variables. We demonstrate the formulation using the D-Wave Advantage 4.1 quantum annealer and the hybrid quantum-classical algorithm Qbsolv, and benchmark the resulting QUBO-based implementations against specialized classical distance-finding methods. The QA- and SA-assisted implementations show broadly comparable performance, while the classical comparison clarifies the relative strengths of heuristic optimization and exact distance certification. Our results establish a solver-independent QUBO formulation with only a logarithmic multiplicative overhead in the number of variables and characterize connectivity and minor embedding as central limitations of its present implementation on quantum-annealing hardware.

papers.title: Relativistic generalization of Feynman's path integral on the basis of extended Lagrangians
papers.summary: In the extended Lagrange formalism of classical point dynamics, the system's dynamics is parametrized along a system evolution parameter $s$, and the physical time $t$ is treated as a \emph{dependent} variable $t(s)$ on equal footing with all other configuration space variables $q^{i}(s)$. In the action principle, the conventional classical action $L dt$ is then replaced by the generalized action $L_{e}ds$. A direct reparametrization of the conventional action yields an extended Lagrangian that is homogeneous of degree one in the velocities. A regular extended Lagrangian that is not homogeneous of degree one can also reproduce the conventional dynamics on a suitably selected invariant hypersurface. With this representation, the physical motion takes place on a hypersurface within a symplectic extended phase space of even dimension. The formal similarity of conventional and extended Lagrange formalisms provides a direct connection with the proper-time path integral approach to relativistic quantum physics. To provide an example, the non-homogeneous extended Lagrangian $L_{e}$ of a classical relativistic spinless point particle in an external electromagnetic field will be presented. This extended Lagrangian is a quadratic function in the velocities, and its selected zero-energy hypersurface is the classical mass shell. With this $L_{e}$, the generalized path integral first yields an evolution equation in $s$. Imposing the corresponding quantum mass-shell condition then yields the Klein-Gordon equation as the physical wave equation. This establishes the relation between the classical extended Lagrangian description and proper-time quantization for a charged spin-zero particle.

Consequently, the framework offers an adaptable tool for practical quantum cryptographic protocols, expanding secure communication possibilities in untrusted environments.

papers.title: Computational Aspects of the Trace Norm Contraction Coefficient
papers.summary: We show that approximating the trace norm contraction coefficient of a quantum channel within a constant factor is NP-hard. Equivalently, this shows that determining the optimal success probability for encoding a bit in a quantum system undergoing noise is NP-hard. This contrasts with the classical analogue of this problem that can clearly be solved efficiently. We also establish the NP-hardness of deciding if the contraction coefficient is equal to 1, i.e., the channel can perfectly preserve a bit. As a consequence, deciding if a non-commutative graph has an independence number of at least 2 is NP-hard. In addition, we establish a converging hierarchy of semidefinite programming upper bounds on the contraction coefficient.

papers.title: Work statistics of sudden quantum quenches: A random matrix theory perspective on Gaussianity and its deviations
papers.summary: We show that, for sudden quenches, the work distribution reduces to the statistics of the traces of powers of Haar unitaries, which are random unitary matrices drawn uniformly from the unitary group. For translation-invariant quadratic fermionic chains with interactions extending to $m$ neighbors and periodic boundary conditions, the Loschmidt amplitude admits a unitary matrix model / Toeplitz representation, which yields a work variable of the form $W=\sum_{r\le m} a_r \Re\operatorname{Tr} U^r$ (and in models with pairing terms -superconducting pairing- additional $b_r \Im\operatorname{Tr} U^r$ terms appear). By invoking multivariate central limit theorems for vectors of traces of unitaries, we obtain a Gaussian distribution for $P(W)$ with variance $\mathrm{Var}(W)=\frac{1}{2}\sum_r r (a_r^2+b_r^2)$ and asymptotic independence across different powers. We also characterise the conditions under which non-Gaussian tails arise, for example from many interaction terms or their slow decay, as well as the appearance of Fisher-Hartwig singularities. We illustrate these mechanisms in the XY chain. Various numerical diagnostics support the analytical results.

papers.title: Rare Event Simulation of Quantum Error-Correcting Circuits
papers.summary: We describe a practical approach for accessing the logical failure rates of quantum error-correcting (QEC) circuits under low physical (component) failure rate regimes. Standard Monte Carlo is often the de facto approach for studying the failure rates of quantum circuits. However, in the study of fault-tolerant error-correcting circuits, the ability to extend this approach to low physical failure rates is limited. In particular, the use of Monte Carlo to access circuits that are relatively large or have high correcting power becomes more difficult as we lower the input failure rates of the individual components (gates) in the circuit. For these reasons, many simulations studying the circuit model go no lower than end-to-end logical failure rates in the 10^{-6} regime. In this report, we outline an approach that borrows from earlier work by Bravyi and Vargo to the more complex circuit noise model. Earlier works studied both the capacity and phenomenological noise models, but the work is insufficient for generating similar simulations in the circuit-noise model. To the best of our knowledge, our team is the first to develop a full prescription of the rare event simulation by splitting technique for the circuit-based noise model. We have also generated promising results that are confirmed by standard Monte Carlo simulation under an accessible regime. This work shows that we can access noise in the circuit-model prescription of quantum error-correcting code to failure rates below 10^{-20} regime.

papers.title: Solving the traveling salesman problem on $\lceil \log_2 (N-1)! \rceil$ qubits with a variational quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold network: exact-gradient CVaR training and generalization over time-dependent graphs
papers.summary: The one-hot encoding of the traveling salesman problem (TSP) on quantum hardware needs $(N-1)^2$ qubits for $N$ sites and penalty terms that dominate the cost landscape. Permutation encodings that label every tour by its Lehmer code need only $\lceil \log_2 (N-1)! \rceil$ qubits and no penalty term, but variational solvers on them have reached the optimum reliably only up to six sites. Here we show how to train such a solver so that it scales to ten sites and transfers across graphs. A variational quantum Kolmogorov--Arnold network (VQKAN) generates the angles of a shallow circuit from the time and from features of the distance matrix; the circuit is trained on the conditional value at risk (CVaR) of the tour length with an exact adjoint gradient, a risk-level schedule, multi-start, small-angle initialization, and basin-hopping restarts, and the qubits are read as a Gray code so that neighbouring states are neighbouring tours. The method returns the optimal tour on every instance tested for $N = 4$ to $10$ (symmetric polygons and asymmetric random graphs), and in 112 of 120 cases of a thirty-run repetition at $N = 10$ with the remaining gaps at 1\% of the optimum, using 3 to 19 qubits where one-hot encoding needs 9 to 81, with as few as $10^2$ measurement shots. With the distance features as inputs, one parameter set generalizes to unseen times on time-dependent graphs. An ablation identifies basin hopping as the ingredient that removes the residual local minima at $N = 10$, while deeper circuits do not help; controls against 2-opt, the one-hot encoding, and an $N$-qubit one-hot walk separate the circuit's contribution from classical post-processing.

papers.title: Objectivity, basis ambiguity, and the classical simulability of concordant quantum computation
papers.summary: Concordant quantum computations, in which circuits whose register carries zero quantum discord with respect to every subsystem at every step, contain neither entanglement nor any other form of quantum correlation, yet no efficient classical simulation of them is known beyond restricted gate sets. We argue that the obstruction is not a shortage of correlations but the absence of a uniquely identifiable local product basis, and we develop this \emph{basis ambiguity} on two fronts. Quantitatively, we introduce the Basis Ambiguity Measure $\beta\in[0,1]$, the normalized dimension of the manifold of admissible diagonalizing bases on a gate support, and prove a sharp equivalence: a concordance-preserving gate that defeats the Local Basis Finder of Cable and Browne exists if and only if $\beta>0$. Both directions are constructive. Physically, we identify the resource whose absence the obstruction is: \emph{basis objectivity}, a redundant and independently accessible record of the local basis. We show that an environment in spectrum broadcast form, together with the system--environment interaction map, replaces the NP-hard degeneracy test of Eastin by a fixed number of pairwise fragment comparisons per gate, at a cost independent of register size and circuit depth; the two ingredients live on different axes (state and dynamics), and neither alone suffices. We further prove that a theory in which every state has a strictly unique decomposition into perfectly distinguishable pure states has a simplex state space and lacks the continuity content of Hardy's fifth axiom, so that $\beta$ is a computational witness of that axiom. Finally, as a proof of principle that basis ambiguity carries operational content, we present a concordant encryption protocol with hidden local bases, together with an explicit account of what its security does and does not rest on.

papers.title: Phase-preserving steady-state operations beyond Lindblad master equations
papers.summary: We consider a class of nonunitary operations that is naturally implemented via a combination of projective measurement and unitary operators. We implement these operations without using measurements by coupling the system to an infinite set of ancilla states and time-evolving with a single time-independent Hamiltonian. The infinite ancilla enables the main system to reach a local steady state that preserves initial phase information. We prove that these steady-state operations are not describable as a mapping from an initial state to a steady state of a time-independent Lindblad master equation acting only on the main system. As an additional degree of control, we show that the spectral resonance between the system and the ancilla acts as a switch that turns the operation on and off, and we derive a closed-form expression that quantifies the sharpness of this switch. We further find numerically that the phase preservation survives moderate disorder, over a time window set by the size of the ancilla. This Hamiltonian framework therefore provides a route to autonomous quantum control using the tunability of a closed system.

papers.title: Finite-size quantum key distribution rates from R\'enyi entropies using conic optimization
papers.summary: Finite-size general security proofs for quantum key distribution based on R\'enyi entropies have recently been introduced. These approaches are more flexible and provide tighter bounds on the secret key rate than traditional formulations based on the von Neumann entropy. However, deploying them requires minimizing the conditional R\'enyi entropy, a difficult optimization problem that has hitherto been tackled using ad-hoc techniques based on the Frank-Wolfe algorithm, which are unstable and can only handle particular cases. In this work, we introduce a method based on non-symmetric conic optimization for solving this problem. Our technique is fast, reliable, and completely general. We illustrate its performance on several protocols, whose results represent an improvement over the state of the art.

papers.title: Fundamental Limitations of QAOA on Constrained Problems and a Route to Exponential Enhancement
papers.summary: We study the feasibility limitations of generic QAOA for permutation-constrained optimization, where valid configurations occupy an exponentially small fraction of the Boolean hypercube. Using random edge-cost TSP/ATSP ensembles, we establish high-probability bounds showing that optimized generic QAOA retains exponentially small feasible probability over specified parameter domains. At depth one, the bound holds uniformly over all mixer angles and a cost-angle grid that may be exponentially large in n^2. The analysis combines Walsh-Fourier/Krawtchouk estimates, which suppress low- and high-degree contributions, with transition-feature collision bounds controlling objective-dependent interference. Complementary cost-angle averaging, fourth-moment estimates, and light-cone analysis characterize energy-fibre coherence, typical-angle concentration, and constraint-correlation geometry. We compare generic QAOA with a constraint-enhanced kernel (CE-QAOA) initialized in a product one-hot subspace and evolved with a block-local XY mixer. For N = n^2 binary variables, CE-QAOA attains feasible probability at least n!/n^n at every depth, yielding an exp[Omega(n^2)] advantage over optimized generic QAOA at depth one with high probability. For linked cost-angle schedules with independently optimized mixer angles, the generic feasibility obstruction and exponential CE-QAOA separation extend throughout linear-depth windows p 0. These parameter-uniform bounds also imply exponential raw-sample requirements for adaptive feasible sampling within the prescribed domains.

papers.title: Mirror subspace diagonalization: A real-time quantum Krylov algorithm with near-optimal sampling cost
papers.summary: Quantum Krylov algorithms are a promising approach for ground-state energy estimation on near-term quantum computers. However, their sampling cost is inherently high because each Hamiltonian term is measured individually. Despite various mitigation techniques, this overhead remains a bottleneck for large-scale electronic structure problems. We introduce mirror subspace diagonalization (MSD), which approaches the theoretical lower bound on the sampling cost for quantum Krylov algorithms built upon real-time evolution. MSD uses a finite-difference formula to express the Hamiltonian as a linear combination of time-evolution unitaries with symmetrically shifted timesteps, enabling efficient estimation of the Hamiltonian matrix within the Krylov subspace. By optimizing the timestep and shifting the energy spectrum, finite-difference and statistical errors are minimized simultaneously, allowing MSD to attain the sampling-cost lower bound up to a logarithmic factor. We further apply classical post-processing to infer Hamiltonian moments, which mitigate the ground-state energy error via the Lanczos scheme. Our analysis shows MSD is particularly effective when the Hamiltonian's spectral norm is much smaller than its 1-norm, as in high-accuracy molecular simulations with large basis sets and strong electronic correlations. Numerical results for various molecular models show sampling-cost reductions of roughly 10 to 10,000 times over the conventional quantum Krylov algorithm.

papers.title: Spatial Phase Control of Energy and Ergotropy in Quantum Batteries
papers.summary: We investigate the role of spatial geometry in controlling energy storage and work extraction in a non-Markovian quantum battery. The spatial separation between the qubits introduces a geometry-dependent phase that governs collective interference, directly modulating the decay channels and energy transfer dynamics. We show that tuning the interqubit distance allows for the engineering of bright and dark collective pathways, which, in conjunction with environmental memory, significantly enhances the charging power, maximal stored energy, and ergotropy revivals.

papers.title: Learning Quantum Operator Dynamics from Short-Time Data
papers.summary: Real-time dynamics of quantum observables provide direct access to excitation spectra and correlation functions in quantum many-body systems, but currently available quantum devices are limited to short evolution times due to decoherence. We propose a neural ordinary differential equation (Neural ODE) framework with a physics-driven neural network to reconstruct long-time operator dynamics from short-time quantum data. By expanding observables in the Pauli basis and exploiting locality and symmetry constraints, the operator evolution is reduced to a tractable set of coefficients whose dynamics are learned from the measurement data. Applied to the Ising spin chain with mixed fields, the operator learning method accurately extrapolates its long-time correlation function and resolves its excitation spectrum. We validate the framework by collecting short-time data from IBM's superconducting quantum processor and successfully reconstruct the Fourier spectrum of an $N=8$ Ising spin chain with 5 times enhanced precision. Our results demonstrate a scalable and data-efficient strategy for extracting dynamical and spectral information from practical quantum hardware.

papers.title: Classical shadows with arbitrary group representations
papers.summary: Classical shadows (CS) has recently emerged as an important framework to efficiently predict properties of an unknown quantum state. A common strategy in CS protocols is to parametrize the basis in which one measures the state by a random group action; many examples of this have been proposed and studied on a case-by-case basis. In this work, we present a unified theory that allows us to simultaneously understand CS protocols based on sampling from general group representations, extending previous approaches that worked in simplified (multiplicity-free) settings. We identify a class of measurement bases which we call "centralizing bases" that allows us to analytically characterize and invert the measurement channel, minimizing classical post-processing costs. We complement this analysis by deriving general bounds on the sample-complexity necessary to obtain estimates of a given precision. Beyond its unification of previous CS protocols, our method allows us to readily generate new protocols based on other groups, or different representations of previously considered ones. For example, we characterize novel shadow protocols based on sampling from the spin and tensor representations of $\textsf{SU}(2)$, symmetric and orthogonal groups, and the exceptional Lie group $G_2$.

papers.title: Magnetic domains stabilized by symmetry-protected zero modes
papers.summary: Understanding mechanisms for the breakdown of thermalization in closed quantum systems is a central problem in quantum many-body physics. We demonstrate strong nonergodic behavior in the XX model on coupled chains, where domain-wall initial states retain an inhomogeneous magnetization profile for arbitrarily long times. We find that this effect arises due to zero modes protected by chiral symmetry. Using an analysis based on the Lanczos algorithm, we identify evidence for a localization transition in the thermodynamic limit at a critical coupling between the chains. We further show that antiferromagnetic defects in the initial state and symmetry-breaking perturbations restore slow thermalization, whereas it remains robust for symmetry-conserving perturbations. These results establish that degenerate, symmetry-protected subspaces can give rise to thermodynamically stable nonergodic dynamics in experimentally accessible quantum systems.

papers.title: The power of unentanglement without destructive interference
papers.summary: Stoquasticity, originating in sign-problem-free physical systems, gives rise to $\sf StoqMA$, introduced by Bravyi, Bessen, and Terhal (2006), a quantum-inspired intermediate class between $\sf MA$ and $\sf AM$. Unentanglement similarly gives rise to ${\sf QMA}(2)$, introduced by Kobayashi, Matsumoto, and Yamakami (CJTCS 2009), which generalizes $\sf QMA$ to two unentangled proofs and still has only the trivial $\sf NEXP$ upper bound. In this work, we initiate a systematic study of the power of unentanglement without destructive interference via ${\sf StoqMA}(2)$, the class of unentangled stoquastic Merlin--Arthur proof systems. Beyond its complexity-theoretic interest, ${\sf StoqMA}(2)$ is connected to the optimality of non-negative tensor optimization algorithms. We highlight: 1. ${\sf NP} \subseteq {\sf StoqMA}(2)$ with $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$-qubit proofs and completenes $1-2^{-{\rm polylog}(n)}$. Conversely, the Sum-of-Squares algorithm of Barak, Kelner, and Steurer (STOC 2014) gives an exponential-time upper bound for ${\sf StoqMA}(2)$. Our tightened analysis shows the optimality of our protocol and the BKS algorithm under ETH. 2. For logarithmic-size proofs, ${\sf NP} \subseteq {\sf StoqMA}(2)_{\log}$ with completeness $1-O(n^{-2})$ and vanishing gap, while ${\sf StoqMA}(2)_{\log} \subseteq {\sf MA}$. Consequently, quantum-inspired randomness enables exponentially shorter unentangled proofs even under the assumption ${\sf MA}={\sf NP}$. 3. For ${\sf StoqMA}(2)_1$, the parameter dependence in the general ETH-optimal time bound can be exponentially improved, or the bound achieved simultaneously with polynomial space. Our lower bounds are obtained by stoquastizing the short-proof ${\sf QMA}(2)$ protocols using distribution testing techniques. Our upper bounds for the nearly perfect completeness case are proved via our rectangular closure testing framework.

papers.title: Sequential vs. Synchronized Entanglement Swapping: QKD Secret-Key Rate under Optimized Link-Layer Control
papers.summary: Quantum repeater chains build long-distance entanglement for quantum key distribution (QKD) by creating pairs on short links and joining them through entanglement swapping. Because stored pairs lose fidelity while they wait, swap timing can affect the secret-key rate. We study how network-layer swap scheduling affects six-state QKD on a simulated four-hop chain under an idealized Werner-state noise model. We compare a sequential (swap-and-wait) discipline, which builds and stores partial chains, with a synchronized (wait-and-swap) discipline, which waits until all links are ready before swapping. Both use the same reinforcement-learned link controllers, isolating the effect of the swapping discipline. When stored pairs cannot retain sufficient fidelity for one network time step, our sequential implementation produces no key, while synchronized retains a small key rate from simultaneous link deliveries. Once sequential becomes viable, it outperforms synchronized by up to 19.1% in the homogeneous chains studied, with the advantage decreasing as memory lifetime increases. We predict the synchronized short-memory pair-delivery rate from link-delivery statistics and derive a closed-form condition for when sequential can preserve progress across time steps. We also examine chains with one slower link, where partial chains can wait and decay at the bottleneck. In this setting, synchronized slightly outperforms sequential at longer memory lifetimes. Moving the slow link has little effect on key rate away from the transition region but strongly affects sequential link-buffer occupancy. Choosing a swapping discipline therefore depends not only on whether memories can preserve partial progress, but also on how the link configuration determines where that progress must wait and decay.

papers.title: On Constructing and Decoding Quantum Triorthogonal Codes
papers.summary: Triorthogonal codes are a basic ingredient in magic-state distillation, as they enable transversal implementation of logical $\mathsf{T}$ gates. As a non-Clifford operation, the $\mathsf{T}$ gate enables universal fault-tolerant quantum computation when combined with Clifford operations. We derive an existence criterion for even-weight triorthogonal generator matrices with a target dual minimum distance. The criterion combines triorthogonality constraints with MacWilliams identities via Krawtchouk-polynomial conditions on the dual weight distribution, yielding an integer linear programming formulation for the construction problem. We find novel nontrivial triorthogonal codes (degenerate and non-degenerate) that are not necessarily constructed from triply even binary linear codes. By imposing automorphism-group constraints, the formulation also recovers the known [[49,1,5]] and [[95,1,7]] triorthogonal codes. We also evaluate the performance of the obtained high-distance triorthogonal codes over the dephasing channel using different decoding methods, showing that automorphism ensemble decoding (AED) and guessing random additive-noise decoding (GRAND) are promising options.

papers.title: Sympathetic Cooling in Trapped Ions with Spectral Selectivity via the Zeeman Shift
papers.summary: High-fidelity quantum logic operations in trapped ions often require the ions' collective motion to be cooled to near the ground state. Since cooling the ions' motion typically involves dissipative processes such as spontaneous photon scattering, sympathetic cooling is used on select coolant ions between gate sequences to cool the ion chain without affecting the data qubits. Common implementations for coolant ions include different atomic species, different isotopes of the same species or individually addressable ions. Each of these approaches have challenges associated with them, which include increased hardware complexity, reduced efficiency of radial mode cooling and re-ordering events which add additional experimental overhead. We demonstrate a sympathetic cooling scheme leveraging internal metastable atomic levels accessible via a narrow quadrupole transition, utilizing the natural Zeeman shift and individually addressed Raman transitions, to achieve isolation of the non-coolant or ``data ions" from coolant ions. We demonstrate modest decoherence of the data ions due to cooling, while preserving the coherence requirements for high-fidelity gate operations.

papers.title: Nonlocal Teams and Information Structures
papers.summary: We look at Bell inequalities from the lens of information structures in stochastic teams. We consider the usual Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) game and a dynamic variant of the same to study how various classes of strategies, classical, projective and quantum, behave under team theoretic solution concepts. We endow players with a fixed quantum state that we take as the Bell state, and allow variation of the measurement strategies. In the static game, projective strategies (where each player performs projective measurements) are team optimal for all parameter values and are closed under best response. In the dynamic game these properties fail: projective strategies may be strictly outperformed by classical ones, best responses to projective strategies need not be projective, and, beyond a sharp threshold on the channel noise, team optimal projective strategies cease to be person-by-person optimal, even though person-by-person optimal projective pairs always exist. These results shed light on the delicate interplay of information structure in quantum strategies and the fragility, under a change of information structure, of structural properties that are taken for granted in the static setting.

papers.title: A quantum algorithm for one-shot signatures
papers.summary: We provide a pre-obfuscation circuit-level implementation of an efficient one shot signature scheme, which has known applications to delegated signatures, secure token transfer, and publicly verifiable randomness. The algorithm consists of two stages: a key generation stage where a classical public key/quantum secret key pair is produced, and a signing stage where the quantum secret key is processed with a message string to produce a classical signature. There is no algorithmic error in the construction and the signed message can be efficiently checked by a classical verifier. Our scheme works by preparing a superposition over elements of a random affine coset determined by the output of a puncturable pseudorandom function, together with a circuit that tests coset membership. The logical qubit number scales like $\Theta( \kappa\log(r) + n + l)$ and the gate complexity scales like $\Theta(n^3 + nl)$, where $r$ is the public key size, $n+l$ is the signature size, $l$ is the message size, and $\kappa = \Omega(n)$ is the cryptographic security parameter. We provide explicit qubit and gate counts before obfuscation. A secure instantiation additionally requires modified key generation and a security proof for the resulting obfuscated construction.

papers.title: Compact deterministic liquid-crystal polarization controller with single-measurement direct control
papers.summary: Polarization controllers (PCs) and their control algorithms are critical for compensating environmental disturbances and maintaining signal fidelity in polarization-sensitive photonic systems. However, existing controllers often involve trade-offs among key performance metrics,while associated control algorithms either converge inefficiently or require multiple state-of-polarization (SOP) measurements. This work presents a compact deterministic liquid-crystal polarization controller (LC-PC) with balanced overall performance, featuring low insertion loss (<1 dB), low driving voltage (<6 V), and full Poincar\'e sphere coverage. The device exhibits highly predictable and repeatable polarization modulation characterized by SOP-independent trajectory normal vectors, enabling a single-measurement direct-calculation algorithm using pre-characterized rotation axes and voltage-to-rotation relationships, with degree-level polarization control accuracy. The combination of this compact deterministic LC-PC and its efficient control scheme provides a practical solution for polarization management in quantum key distribution, optical sensing, and advanced photonic systems.

papers.title: Evolutionary stability and payoff equivalence in an Eisert-Wilkens-Lewenstein quantum game
papers.summary: An evolutionarily stable strategy (ESS) is a strategy that, once adopted by a population, cannot be invaded by any sufficiently rare alternative (mutant) strategy. We analyse evolutionary stability in an Eisert--Wilkens--Lewenstein (EWL) quantization of a symmetric $2\times2$ coordination game, whose classical mixed equilibrium $p^*=1/2$ is not an ESS. In the restricted two-parameter EWL strategy space, the corresponding quantum strategy is a strict symmetric Nash equilibrium and an ESS for every entanglement strength $\gamma>0$. In the full $SU(2)$ strategy space it remains a Nash equilibrium, but in the unreduced game, in which every unitary is a distinct strategy, exact payoff duplicates preclude strictness and ESS for every pure strategy. For the agreement-payoff class, the payoff factors through a Bloch map; identifying payoff-equivalent unitaries gives the reduced space $U(1)\backslash SU(2)\cong S^2$, where strictness and ESS are restored for $\gamma>0$. An arbitrarily small perturbation outside this class that preserves $p^*=1/2$ yields a profitable deviation, so the reduced-space result is not generic.

papers.title: Bimodal non-Gaussian photonic states from a single quantum emitter in a waveguide
papers.summary: We investigate the generation of deterministic and heralded non-Gaussian states of light, using a single two-level system coupled to a chiral waveguide. We study the case of a single two level system driven by pulsed coherent and squeezed drive in a chiral waveguide. For coherent input pulses, we show that the emitter can deterministically generate Wigner-negative states, albeit of limited rank. Going beyond, using squeezed-vacuum inputs, we show that the interaction produces rich bimodal non-Gaussian states from which higher-stellar-rank states, including large squeezed cat states, can be experimentally extracted with a substantial success rate. For experimental feasibility and comparison, we analyze the effect of imperfect coupling and of the intrinsic $50\%$ collection limit of symmetric, non-chiral waveguides. Following that, we propose a simple interferometric scheme that recovers an effectively chiral interaction in an otherwise bidirectional waveguide.

papers.title: Photon localization: a comparative study
papers.summary: We compare different measures for photon localization in terms of two-dimensional Gaussian wave packets of width Delta k. We find that all measures start to coalesce if the wave packet has evolved for times which are larger than a few (c Delta k)^{-1}. However, the Landau-Peierls wave function yields the largest initial offset -ct > 0 while the Fourier transform of the helicity components of the k-space wave packet yields the smallest offset -ct > 0 and converges towards -ct = 0 fastest. We also discuss local detection of photons through a model detector consisting of ions in ion traps. The position-dependent detection probabilities are inferred from the scattering matrix. We find that the local detection probability for photons can be expressed in terms of three of the proposed localization measures, viz. the Landau-Peierls wave function, the energy wave function, and the Hawton density. Those three proposals also remain close throughout the time evolution of the single-photon wave packet. However, the energy wave function is locally related to electromagnetic fields and is therefore confirmed as the preferred tool for the description of local photon densities. The novelty of our observations concerns three items, viz. the possibility to express local photon absorption matrix elements through three of the proposed localization measures, the coalescence of all the proposed localization measures after sufficiently long evolution of a photon wave packet, and the striking differences of some of the proposed localization measures during early wave packet evolution.

papers.title: State-resolved quantum-information fingerprints of partial dynamical symmetry in the interacting boson model
papers.summary: Partial dynamical symmetry (PDS) is an algebraic structure in which a symmetry is neither exact nor fully broken: a subset of eigenstates keeps good quantum numbers and stays solvable while the rest mix. It is currently identified from spectroscopy. We ask whether it also leaves a purely structural mark in the eigenstates, and find, for the $sd$-IBM Hamiltonians studied here, that it does, though not in the magnitude of entanglement. The diagnostic is the variance of a symmetry Casimir, the label variance $\Var\,\C[G]$, which shares its zero with a block-coherence entropy and a block impurity: all three vanish when a state occupies a single Casimir sector, a single irreducible representation once conjugate representations are resolved by the cubic Casimir. Resolved state by state, the variance is numerically zero on the symmetry-selected subset and large on the mixed states, isolating the PDS states from the wavefunctions alone; the separation does not close as the boson number grows and persists at Leviatan's first- and second-order critical points, whereas the magnitude of bipartite $s|d$ entanglement does not separate the two families. We anchor the analysis in $^{168}$Er, reproducing Leviatan's fitted $\su3$ admixtures and his Hamiltonian-parameter-independent $\gamma\!\to\! g$ $B(E2)$ ratios. The diagnostic also has an exact dynamical form, a Casimir Loschmidt echo rigid on the symmetry-pure states, and we demonstrate its readout on an IBM superconducting processor at $N=3$, where a single solvable/mixed exemplar reproduces the predicted pattern within finite-shot uncertainties.

papers.title: Compound beams for direct experimental comparison of quantum operations
papers.summary: Compound beams composed of simple experimental blocks (detected in simultaneous detection windows) that form specific quantum-correlated structures are suggested for simulating the properties of different quantum operations used for creating highly nonclassical and entangled multi-mode states needed in quantum communication, metrology, and information protocols. Qualitative and quantitative comparison of multi-photon addition and subtraction in compound multi-mode thermal as well as sub-Poissonian beams and multi-mode twin beams with their intensities extending over two orders in magnitude is provided. Adding and subtracting up to twenty photocounts, optimal conditions for the generation of experimental nonclassical states are identified. In general, photon addition is identified as advantageous over photon subtraction for the multi-mode thermal and sub-Poissonian beams: It induces (enhances) the nonclassicality in the former (latter) state. Contrary to this, photon subtraction outperforms photon addition in the multi-mode twin beams. Moreover, exploiting temporal photon-pair correlations in compound twin beams when post-selecting, nearly ideal experimental photon(s) addition is demonstrated. The results apply for the beams with mean photon number per mode much less than one.

papers.title: Q-Edge: Symmetry-Reduced Quantum Simulation of Structured Extreme Dependence
papers.summary: High-dimensional simulation of multivariate extremes is fundamentally limited by the combinatorial complexity of dependence, often more than by the scarcity of extreme observations. We show that symmetry admits a lossless orbit-space representation that preserves structured extreme dependence while replacing an exponentially large dependence space with a compact set of symmetry classes. Based on this principle, we develop Q-Edge (Quantum Extreme Dependence Engine), a symmetry-reduced quantum framework that operates directly in orbit space, enabling scalable simulation and digital twins of structured extreme systems. By transferring symmetry into the data representation rather than the quantum circuit, Q-Edge allows unconstrained quantum generative models to exploit dramatically reduced state spaces. For a 30-dimensional problem, approximately 1.6 million angular states collapse to 256 orbit states, reducing the required quantum representation from about 21 qubits to 8. Our results establish a general computational principle for scalable quantum simulation of structured extreme dependence.

papers.title: Time-Dependent Quantum Monte Carlo for fermions: from Bayesian conditioning to spinor dynamics
papers.summary: The time-dependent quantum Monte Carlo method represents a many-electron state by an ensemble of replicas, in which each electron is described by a cloud of walkers which samples its density in physical space, one walker and one guide wave per replica, and it replaces the Hartree potential by a conditional interaction built from the walker positions. The sampling is in physical space rather than in configuration space, which keeps the cost polynomial. Here we derive that conditional interaction. Treating the walker as a localization of its electron to a finite resolution, we show that Bayes' theorem and a single empirical substitution yield the Nadaraya-Watson form which the method has used heuristically. The nonlocality length then becomes the width of the conditioning, and the pair and mean-field limits follow from one construction. Because the conditioning removes the gauge freedom which eliminates the orthonormality multipliers in Hartree-Fock, we enforce orthonormality by a term derived from the constraint. We generalize the formulation to spinors, where the Pauli suppression at coincidence becomes graded by the local spin alignment, and it reduces through the collinear and mean-field limits to the known two-particle spin equations. For two electrons in a double quantum dot in an inhomogeneous magnetic field, compared with the exact solution, the spinor equations reproduce the non-collinear spin geometry which collinear calculations cannot represent and recover the larger part of the entanglement missing from a single determinant. In the crossover between the exchange and the Zeeman regimes, where the singlet-triplet coherence sets the spin geometry, the replicas must carry that coherence themselves, as in the spin-coupled pair of valence-bond theory.

papers.title: The cost of direction in quantum Bell certification
papers.summary: Certifying a quantum bound can require more information than realizing the correlations that attain it. We show that this distinction becomes unbounded when a proof must condition on one party's measurement question. A fixed Bell scenario attained by one entangled qubit pair has a standard degree-two sum-of-squares certificate, yet the minimum degree in either conditioning direction grows as the inverse square root of the distance to a local endpoint. Choosing the better party does not remove this cost. The obstruction also survives approximate certification: bounding the quantum maximum to any fixed fractional accuracy relative to its Bell advantage requires the same diverging level. Thus a short standard proof cannot be transferred to a uniformly bounded conditioned level, even after relaxing exactness and optimising the direction. Mixing directions within a proof removes this family's obstruction, while a separate finite separation establishes its limits. Contact geometry explains the cost and connects it to a sharp precision law for randomness certification.

papers.title: Quantum models of interaction Hamiltonians and their paradoxes
papers.summary: In quantum physics it is commonplace to model the interaction of remote systems with a many-body Hamiltonian. Taking such an action-at-a-distance description {\it \`a la lettre} leads to various paradoxes related to faster-than-light communication and apparent inconsistencies in local energy accounting. It also neglects residual effects, such as entanglement between the remote systems and the mediator that implements the interaction, or the decoherence that arises when the remote systems undergo local evolution. We study simple microscopic quantum models that respect the light cone by design and reproduce two-body Hamiltonians. For these models we quantitatively analyze the residual effects of the microscopic mediator on the remote systems, including dressing of stationary states, and decoherence in the presence of fast local control. We show how the models resolve the paradoxes.

papers.title: Exact quantum circuits for a Heisenberg triangle with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction
papers.summary: We construct short analytical quantum circuits for the exact evolution of a spin triangle with Dzyaloshinskii--Moriya (DM) interaction. We consider pure DM interaction with arbitrary real couplings and two Hamiltonian families with uniform Heisenberg exchange. For pure DM, a change of basis reduces the evolution to two single-qubit rotations. The circuits reproduce the full evolution operator at arbitrary time with a fixed gate count and admit implementations with both triangular and linear qubit connectivity. Experiments on a superconducting IBM quantum processor demonstrate directional quantum-state transfer and reproduce the amplitude and phase of transverse magnetization. In these experiments, the exact circuits reduce distortions relative to circuits based on the second-order Trotter formula. On a 12-spin kagome cluster, exact triangle blocks reduce the gate count at a prescribed accuracy. We also investigate the reduction of coherent errors by adjusting circuit angles and applying echo pulses to neighboring qubits.

papers.title: Regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergences
papers.summary: Barycentric R\'enyi divergences were introduced in [Mosonyi, Bunth, Vrana, Linear Algebra and its Applications, 2024] as an alternative to standard Kubo-Ando constructions to define multivariate quantum R\'enyi divergences. They are defined via a variational expression and depend on a finite collection of quantum relative entropies $D^{q_x}$. When all the relative entropies are monotone under CPTP maps then so are the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences, and when all the relative entropies are additive then the corresponding barycentric R\'enyi divergences are subadditive under tensor product. Additivity has only been established before for the case where all $D^{q_x}$ are chosen to be the Umegaki relative entropy, which is also the only case where the barycentric R\'enyi divergence (called the minimal one) was known to admit an explicit expression. Here we settle the problem of additivity by showing that for any choice of monotone quantum relative entropies, the regularized barycentric R\'enyi divergence coincides with the minimal barycentric R\'enyi divergence on invertible inputs. This in turn implies that if at least two of the $D^{q_x}$ are strictly larger than the Umegaki relative entropy (in a precise sense), then the resulting barycentric R\'enyi divergence is not even weakly additive.

papers.title: Classical Cellular Automaton for Measurement-Only Entanglement Transitions
papers.summary: We introduce a generalized classical long-range stochastic cellular automaton that exactly captures the entanglement dynamics and transitions of a measurement-only monitored quantum system. The corresponding quantum model consists of a one-dimensional qubit chain subject to competing single-site and long-range Bell measurements, with separations drawn from a power-law distribution. At every step of each trajectory, the state remains a tensor product of Bell pairs and unpaired qubits, with bipartite entanglement entropy fully encoded in a classical matching of the sites. This exact representation allows us to solve the dynamics analytically in several limits and to determine the steady-state scaling of the entanglement entropy. We find volume-law, fractal, and area-law regimes. Numerical results show that these regimes persist beyond the analytically solvable limit. Because Bell measurement outcomes change only the Bell-state labels and leave the matching unchanged, all subsystem entropies are outcome independent, avoiding the exponential cost of trajectory postselection often encountered in experimental studies of measurement-induced entanglement dynamics.

papers.title: SQD-Agent: LLM-driven agentic framework for Quantum Chemistry workflows
papers.summary: Quantum algorithms and quantum hardware are advancing towards a promising paradigm for scientific applications. However, translating domain-specific problems into executable hybrid quantum-classical workflows remains a significant barrier for application researchers due to the required expertise in quantum algorithms, nuances in quantum programming, and hardware-aware system integration. At the same time, AI and primarily LLM based agents are increasingly capable of interpreting natural-language intent, reasoning over complex workflows, and translating high-level objectives into executable code and building computational pipelines. In this work, we introduce SQD Agent, an LLM-based agentic framework that translates natural-language user intent into executable workflows for Quantum Chemistry applications where algorithms from the Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) family are used. By automating this translation, SQD Agent reduces the level of human expertise and configuration overhead required, thereby simplifying experimentation in hybrid quantum-classical settings for application researchers new to quantum. SQD Agent adopts a modular and extensible architecture that supports seamless integration of heterogeneous quantum backends, classical solvers, and workflow components, ensuring adaptability to rapidly evolving quantum ecosystems. The framework further incorporates interactive capabilities for on-demand profiling, bottleneck analysis, resource optimization, intelligent result caching, and convergence visualization. Key features include quantum chemistry experiments, error mitigation on real quantum hardware, together with analysis of candidate mitigation schemes in terms of their potential error-recovery behavior and computational budget, helping users understand their practical trade-offs and decide which strategies to explore in subsequent experiments.

papers.title: QMA(2) with Limited Shared Entanglement
papers.summary: In $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$, two computationally unbounded provers submit unentangled quantum witnesses to a polynomial-time quantum verifier. We ask whether allowing limited shared entanglement between the two provers changes the power of $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$. To this end, we formalize $\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)$, a variant in which the provers initially share $h$ EPR pairs, as suggested by Aaronson, Beigi, Drucker, Fefferman, and Shor (ToC~2009). We show that polynomially many shared EPR pairs give the provers no cheating advantage: $\mathsf{QMA}(2)\subseteq\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)$ for $h=\operatorname{poly}(n)$. For logarithmically many pairs, the power of $\mathsf{QMA}(2)$ remains unchanged, strengthening this inclusion to $\mathsf{QMA}(2)=\mathsf{QMA}(2;h)$ for $h=O(\log n)$. Finally, we introduce a variant that also allows classical communication between the provers when preparing the witnesses. This setting is particularly revealing for logarithmic-size witnesses: assuming $\mathsf{NP}\nsubseteq\mathsf{BQP}$, we show that superlogarithmically many shared EPR pairs strictly reduce the model's computational power.

papers.title: Theory of spacetime quantum fault tolerance
papers.summary: We present a unified algebraic theory of Clifford spacetime quantum fault tolerance, which underpins universal fault-tolerant quantum computation. We construct a spacetime chain complex from a tensor network representation of a circuit that encodes fault propagation, detector syndromes, and logical actions through the associated gauge and stabilizer structure. We show that this theory (1) unifies various formulations of quantum fault tolerance including spacetime codes, Gottesman's gadget framework, fault complexes, and ZX calculus; (2) connects spacetime distances to the gadget-level correctness properties in Gottesman's formalism; (3) naturally accommodates a range of fault models, in particular phenomenological and circuit-level models, bringing these often separately formulated descriptions into a common algebraic framework through different tensor decompositions and fault assignments; and (4) recovers many known fault tolerance constructions and results as special cases, including repeated syndrome extraction, correlated detectors for transversal and fold-transversal gates, Steane- and Knill-type syndrome extraction gadgets, and single-shot error correction.
